<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; Water
Supply</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; NPC and SPPC</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Assured
supplies of water are important for the Utilities&#8217; generating plants, and at
the present time, the Utilities have adequate water to meet their generation
needs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Reliable water supply is critical to the entire desert
southwest region, including the State of Nevada.&nbsp; The newer generation
facilities in the Utilities&#8217; fleet have been designed to minimize water usage
and employ innovative conservation based technologies such as dry cooling and
recycled water.&nbsp; Although there are current drought conditions in the Las
Vegas area, water resources for most of these facilities rely on regional
aquifers and recycled water that are not closely connected to transient drought
conditions.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;
Purchased Power</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Under the guidelines set forth in the respective ESPs,
NPC and SPPC continue to manage a diverse portfolio of contracted and spot
market supplies, as well as its own generation resources, with the objective of
minimizing its net average system operating costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;During 2012, NPC
and SPPC purchased approximately 26.0% and 44.7%, respectively, of their total
electric energy requirements.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;
NPC Electric</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NPC purchases both forward firm energy and spot market
energy based on economics, regulatory requirements, operating reserve margins,
and unit availability.&nbsp;&nbsp;NPC seeks to manage its loads efficiently by
utilizing its generation resources and long-term purchase power contracts in
conjunction with buying and selling opportunities in the market.&#160;&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160; &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NPC
has entered into long-term purchase power contracts (3 or more years) with
suppliers that generate electricity utilizing gas and renewable resource
facilities with a total nameplate capacity of approximately 2,401 MW and
contract termination dates ranging from 2013 to 2038.&nbsp;&nbsp;Included in
these contracts are approximately 797 MW of nameplate capacity of renewable
energy of which approximately 229 MW of nameplate capacity are under
development or construction and not currently available.&#160; The PECs from
renewable resource facilities are used towards compliance with the Portfolio
Standard.&#160; Energy from some of these contracts is delivered and sold to SPPC
through intercompany related purchase power contracts due to the resource
location and transmission constraints; however, NPC retains the PECs associated
with such contracts.&#160; The completion of ON Line will give NPC the ability to
take delivery of the energy from these contracts. </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NPC
is a member of the SRSG and the WSPP.&nbsp;&nbsp;NPC&#8217;s membership in the SRSG
has allowed it to network with other utilities in an effort to use its
resources more efficiently in the sharing of responsibilities for reserves.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NPC&#8217;s
credit standing may affect the terms under which NPC is able to purchase fuel
and electricity in the western energy markets; however, as a result of NPC&#8217;s
investment grade credit rating over the last several years, this was not a
significant factor in 2012.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; SPPC Electric</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">SPPC
purchases both forward firm energy and spot market energy based on economics,
regulatory requirements, operating reserve margins, and unit
availability.&nbsp;&nbsp;SPPC seeks to manage its loads efficiently by
utilizing its generation resources and long-term purchase power contracts in
conjunction with buying and selling opportunities in the market.&#160;&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">SPPC
has entered into long-term purchase power contracts (3 or more years) with
suppliers that generate electricity utilizing coal and renewable resource
facilities, with a total nameplate capacity of approximately 415 MW and
contract termination dates ranging from 2016 to 2039.&nbsp;&nbsp;Included in
these contracts are approximately 212 MW of nameplate capacity of renewable
energy.&#160; The PECs from renewable resource facilities are used towards
compliance with the Portfolio Standard.&#160; Energy from one of these contracts is
delivered and sold to NPC through an intercompany related purchase power
contract due to the resource location and transmission constraints; however,
SPPC retains the PECs associated with this contract.&#160; The completion of ON Line
will give SPPC the ability to take delivery of the energy from these contracts.
</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">SPPC
is a member of the NWPP and WSPP.&nbsp;&nbsp;These pools have provided SPPC
further access to reserves and spot market power, respectively, in the Pacific
Northwest and Southwest.&nbsp;&nbsp;In turn, SPPC&#8217;s generation resources
provide a backup source for other pool members who rely heavily on
hydroelectric systems.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:2.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">SPPC&#8217;s credit standing may affect the terms under
which SPPC is able to purchase fuel and electricity in the western energy
markets; however, as a result of SPPC&#8217;s investment grade credit rating over the
last several years, this was not a significant factor in 2012.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Transmission&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&#160;&#160; </font><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">General&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Electric
transmission systems deliver energy from electric generators to distribution
systems for final delivery to customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Transmission systems are
designed to move electricity over long distances because generators can be
located anywhere from a few miles to hundreds of miles from customers.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
Utilities&#8217; electric transmission systems are part of the Western
Interconnection, the regional grid in the western United States.&nbsp;&nbsp;The
Western Interconnection includes the interconnected transmission systems of
fourteen western states, two Canadian provinces and the parts of Mexico that
make up the Western Electricity Coordinating Council (WECC).&nbsp;&nbsp;WECC is
one of eight regional councils of the NERC, the entity responsible for the reliability,
adequacy and security of North America&#8217;s bulk electric system.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NPC&#8217;s
transmission system links generating units within and outside of the NPC
Balancing Authority Area for delivery to the NPC distribution system and
provides interconnections with the balancing authority areas of Western Area
Power Administration, Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, California
Independent System Operator (&#8220;CAISO&#8221;), and PacifiCorp.&nbsp; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">SPPC&#8217;s
transmission system links generating units within the SPPC balancing authority
area for delivery to the SPPC distribution system and provides interconnections
with the balancing authority areas of Idaho Power, Los Angeles Department of
Water and Power, CAISO, PacifiCorp, and Bonneville Power Administration.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
service territories of NPC and SPPC are not directly interconnected at present;
however, the construction of ON Line, discussed below, is expected to be
completed in late 2013 and will interconnect the systems for the first time.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Under
the NERC Standards, the Utilities are Balancing Authorities, Transmission
Operators, and Transmission Owners among other roles.&nbsp;&nbsp;As defined by
NERC, the Balancing Authority integrates resource plans ahead of time,
maintains load-interchange-generation balance within the Balancing Authority
Area, and supports Interconnection frequency in real time (i.e., the Balancing
Authority is responsible for assuring that the demands on the system are
matched by an equivalent amount of resources, whether from generators within
its area or from energy imports).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Transmission Operator is
responsible for the reliability of its local transmission system, and operates
or directs the operations of the transmission facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;The
Transmission Owner owns and maintains transmission facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;The
Utilities also schedule power deliveries over their transmission systems and
maintain reliability through their operations and maintenance practices and by
verifying that customers are matching loads with resources.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
Utilities plan, build, and operate transmission systems that delivered approximately
21,481,000 MWh and 8,558,000 MWh of electricity to NPC&#8217;s and SPPC&#8217;s retail customers,
respectively, in their Balancing Authority Areas in 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;The NPC
system handled a system peak load of 5,761 MW in 2012 through approximately
1,725</font><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;"> </font></b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">miles of transmission lines and other transmission facilities
ranging from 60 kV to 500 kV.&nbsp;&nbsp;The SPPC system handled a system peak
load of 1,676 MW in 2012 through 2,050 miles of transmission lines and other
facilities ranging from 55 kV to 345 kV.&#160; The Utilities process generation and
transmission interconnection requests and requests for transmission service
from a variety of customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;These requests usually involve new
planning studies and the negotiation of contracts with new and existing
customers.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Transmission
Regulatory Environment</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Transmission
for the Utilities&#8217; bundled retail customers is subject to the jurisdiction of
the PUCN for rate making purposes.&nbsp; The Utilities provide cost based
wholesale and retail access transmission services under the terms of a FERC
approved Open Access Transmission Tariff (&#8220;OATT&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;In accordance
with the OATT, the Utilities offer several services to eligible customers:</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Network transmission service
(equivalent to the service NVE provides for NVE&#8217;s bundled retail customers)</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Long-term and short-term firm
point-to-point transmission service (&#8220;highest quality&#8221; service with fixed
delivery and receipt points)</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Non-firm point-to-point service
(&#8220;as available&#8221; service with fixed delivery and receipt points)</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Generation interconnection</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Retail open access </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">These services are all offered on a nondiscriminatory
basis in that all potential customers, including the Utilities, have an equal
opportunity to access the transmission system.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Utilities&#8217;
transmission business is managed and operated independently from the energy
marketing business in accordance with FERC&#8217;s Standards of Conduct.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">On
October 31, 2012, NVE filed separate Notices of Transmission Rate Changes with
FERC for NPC and SPPC. &#160;The filings requested incremental rate relief of
approximately $14.5 million annually effective January 1, 2013. On December 31,
2012, FERC suspended the effective date of the rates until June 1, 2013 (except
for two rates that were reductions from the existing rate which were effective
January 1, 2013) and set the cases for hearing or settlement proceedings.&#160; See
Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Regulatory Actions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">FERC Matters</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">, of the Notes to
Financial Statements for further discussion of these rate cases.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; The One Nevada Transmission Line (&#8220;ON Line&#8221;)</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">As discussed earlier, the Utilities are currently
constructing ON Line.&#160; ON Line is Phase 1 of a Joint Project between the
Utilities and GBT-South.&nbsp;&#160; The Joint Project consists of two
phases.&nbsp;&#160; In Phase 1 of the Joint Project, the parties will complete
construction of a 500 kV interconnection between the Robinson Summit <a name="bcl_connect_next"></a><a name="page_40"></a><a name="bcl_connect_prev"></a><a name="bcl_connect_next_bclEnd"></a><a name="bcl_connect_prev_bclEnd"></a><a name="page_40_bclEnd"></a>substation on the SPPC system and the Harry Allen
substation on the NPC system.&nbsp; The Utilities own a 25% undivided ownership
interest in ON Line under the terms of the Transmission Use and Capacity
Exchange Agreement (TUA) with GBT-South, which owns the remaining 75% undivided
ownership interest in ON Line.&#160; The Utilities&#8217; 25% interest in ON Line, which
approximates $138 million (based on the revised costs, discussed below) will be
allocated 95% and 5% to NPC and SPPC, respectively.&nbsp; The Utilities will
have rights to 100% of the capacity of ON Line during Phase 1 (estimated to be
approximately 600-800 MW).&nbsp; If GBT elects to construct Phase 2, it would
construct two additional transmission segments at either end of ON Line: one would
extend from the Robinson Summit substation north to Midpoint, Idaho, and the
other would commence at the Harry Allen substation and interconnect south at
the Eldorado substation.&nbsp; GBT would pay for and own 100% of Phase 2
facilities.&nbsp;&#160; However, NPC and SPPC would have rights to transmission
capacity from Midpoint to Eldorado (for a total of approximately 760 MW based
on a rating of 2,000 MW for the completed Phase 1 and Phase 2 project). </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In
March 2012, NVE announced that the in-service date for ON Line would be delayed
due to efforts to address wind-related damage sustained by some of the tower
structures erected for the project.&nbsp; On June 29, 2012, NPC filed its
triennial 2013 &#8211; 2032 IRP with the PUCN.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2012 IRP included
revised cost estimates for the ON Line project and provided an expected
in-service date of no later than December 31, 2013.&nbsp; The overall ON Line
construction budget was revised from approximately $510 million to approximately
$552 million before AFUDC.&nbsp;&nbsp;The revised construction budget is based
on the estimated cost of completing the project, including the costs for
installation of mitigation measures identified to address the wind-induced
vibration issues that delayed the project.&nbsp; The Utilities requested PUCN
approval of the decision to continue with construction of ON Line with the
revised in-service date and revised budget.&nbsp; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">On
December 24, 2012, the PUCN issued an order on NPC and SPPC&#8217;s IRP&#8217;s approving
the Utilities&#8217; request and finding that it was reasonable to continue</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:normal;"> </font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">with the construction of the ON Line project with the
revised budget and according to the revised schedule, subject to certain
conditions described below under </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Integrated Resource Plan</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align=center style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; Regional
Planning</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The Utilities are members of the WestConnect
Subregional Transmission Planning Committee.&nbsp;&nbsp;This planning committee
was established to provide coordinated transmission planning across the
WestConnect footprint, including the Southwest Area Transmission Group, in
which NPC participates, and the Sierra Subregional Planning Group, in which
SPPC participates.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In
October 2012, NPC and SPPC submitted a compliance filing to the FERC reflecting
their participation with other jurisdictional utilities in the WestConnect
Planning Management Committee relating to certain FERC Order 1000
requirements.&nbsp; FERC Order 1000, issued in July 2011, establishes certain
procedural and substantive requirements relating to participation, cost
allocation and non-incumbent developer aspects of regional and inter-regional
electric transmission planning activities.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Integrated Resource Plan&#160;&#160; </font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
Utilities are required to file IRPs every three years, and as necessary, may
file amendments to their IRPs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The IRPs are prepared in compliance
with Nevada laws and regulations and cover a 20-year period.&nbsp;&nbsp;The
IRPs develop a comprehensive, integrated plan that considers customer energy
requirements and propose the resources to meet those requirements in a manner
that is consistent with prevailing market fundamentals.&nbsp;&nbsp;The ultimate
goal of the IRPs is to balance the objectives of minimizing costs and reducing
volatility while reliably meeting the electric needs of NPC&#8217;s and SPPC&#8217;s
customers.&#160; Projects approved through the IRP process still remain subject to
prudency review by the PUCN.&#160;&#160; The ESP, discussed in detail later, operates in
conjunction with the IRP.&#160; It serves as a guide for near-term execution and
fulfillment of energy needs.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160; NPC Electric</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; In

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Energy Supply
Planning</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&#160;&#160; </font><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">General&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The energy supply function at the Utilities
encompasses the reliable and efficient operation of the Utilities&#8217; owned
generation, the procurement of all fuels and purchased power and resource
optimization (e.g., physical and economic dispatch).</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">There
is the potential for continued price volatility in each Utility&#8217;s service
territory, particularly during peak periods.&#160; Too great a dependence on
generation from the wholesale market can lead to power price volatilities
depending on available power supply and prevailing gas prices.&#160; Both Utilities
face load obligation uncertainty due to the potential for customer switching.&#160;
Some counterparties in these areas have significant credit difficulties,
representing credit risk to the Utilities.&#160; Finally, each Utility&#8217;s own credit
situation can have an impact on its ability to enter into transactions.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In
response to these energy supply challenges, the Utilities have adopted an
approach to managing the energy supply function that has three primary
elements.&#160; The first element is a set of management guidelines to procuring and
optimizing the supply portfolio that is consistent with the requirements of a
load serving entity with a full requirements obligation.&#160; The second element is
an energy risk management and risk control approach that ensures clear separation
of roles between the day-to-day management of risks and compliance monitoring
and control; and ensures clear distinction between policy setting (or planning)
and execution.&#160; Lastly, the Utilities will pursue a process of ongoing
regulatory involvement and acknowledgement of the resource portfolio management
plans.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Within
the energy supply planning process, there are three key components covering
different time frames:</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

  </td>
 <td valign=top width=89% style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;">
  <p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The PUCN-approved
  long-term IRP, which is filed every three years, has a twenty-year planning
  horizon;</font></p>
  </td>
 </tr>
<tr>
  <td valign=top width=8% style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;">

  </td>
 <td valign=top width=3% style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;">
  <p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>
  </td>
 <td valign=top width=89% style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;">
  <p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The PUCN-approved ESP
  which is an intermediate term resource procurement and risk management plan
  that establishes the supply portfolio strategies within which intermediate
  term resource requirements will be met, has a one to three year planning
  horizon; and</font></p>
  </td>
 </tr>
<tr>
  <td valign=top width=8% style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;">
  <p align=right style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:right;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">3.</font></p>

 <td valign=top width=3% style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;">
  <p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>
  </td>
 <td valign=top width=89% style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;">
  <p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Tactical execution
  activities with a one-month to twelve-month focus.</font></p>
  </td>
 </tr>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
ESP operates in conjunction with the PUCN-approved twenty-year IRP.&#160; It serves
as a guide for near-term execution and fulfillment of energy needs.&#160; When the
ESP calls for executing contracts of longer than three years, PUCN approval is
required.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

developing and executing ESPs, management guidelines followed by the Utilities

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; Energy Risk Management and
Control</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
Utilities&#8217; efforts to manage energy commodity (electricity, natural gas, coal
and oil) price risk are governed by the BOD's revised and approved Enterprise
Risk Management and Control Policy.&#160; That policy created the EROC and made that
committee responsible for the overall policy direction of the Utilities&#8217; risk
management and control efforts.&#160; That policy further instructed the EROC to
oversee the development of appropriate risk management and control policies,
including the Energy Risk Management and Control Policy.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;<a name="EHWf7adee04_9a53_45d2_96dc_dc516624c6ca"></a>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHWf7adee04_9a53_45d2_96dc_dc516624c6ca_"></a></font>&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
Utilities&#8217; commodity risk management program establishes a control framework
based on existing commercial practices.&#160; The program creates predefined risk
thresholds and delineates management responsibilities and organizational
relationships.&#160; The program requires that transaction accounting systems and
procedures be maintained for systematically identifying, measuring, evaluating
and responding to the variety of risks inherent in the Utilities&#8217; commercial
activities.&#160; The program&#8217;s control framework consists of a disclosure and
reporting mechanism designed to keep management fully informed of the
operation&#8217;s compliance with portfolio and credit limits.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;<a name="EHW18202530_a938_4acd_b1c8_95732bb2527b"></a>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW18202530_a938_4acd_b1c8_95732bb2527b_"></a></font>&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Currently,
the Utilities are not operating under a PUCN-approved hedging plan, nor are
they hedged against commodities.&#160; However, the Utilities may purchase and sell
financial instruments and physical products to maintain an energy risk
management program that limits energy risk to levels consistent with ESPs
approved by the CEO and the EROC.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160; &#160;</font></b><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Intermediate
Term ESPs</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
Utilities update their intermediate term ESPs annually. In June 2012, NPC filed
its 2013-2015 ESP, and in August 2012, SPPC filed its ESP update for 2013. Both
plans were approved by the EROC and the CEO prior to submission to the PUCN.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The summer needs
of 2013 for both Utilities will be met through a portfolio consisting of
self-generation, forward contracts for power and peaking and seasonal capacity,
or synthetic tolling based contracts (e.g., power prices indexed to gas prices)
while striving to provide the lowest cost energy within reliability and
transmission constraints.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; Long-Term Purchased Power
Activities</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font color=#0070C0 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;<a name="EHWc2842055_27d8_46eb_a30d_d3e5c95f5606"></a>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHWc2842055_27d8_46eb_a30d_d3e5c95f5606_"></a></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The Utilities update their respective planning documents (IRPs, ESPs,
and the Portfolio Standard Annual Report) on a regular and as needed basis to
determine their energy and PEC needs.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;When the planning
documents call for long term purchased power and/or PEC agreements, RFPs are
issued, bids are evaluated, and contracts are executed with the successful
bidders.&nbsp;&nbsp;Contracts requiring PUCN approval are submitted to the PUCN
as part of the IRP or an amendment to an IRP.&#160; Long-term purchased power
contracts are discussed in more detail earlier, under </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Purchased Power</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Short-Term
Resource Optimization Strategy</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The Utilities&#8217; short-term resource optimization
strategy involves both day-ahead (next day through the end of the current
month) and real-time (next hour through the end of the current day) activities
that require buying, selling and scheduling power resources to determine the
most economical way to produce or procure the power resources needed to meet
the retail customer load and operating reserve requirement.&nbsp;&nbsp;The
Utilities commit and dispatch generating units based on the comparative
economics of generation versus spot-market purchase
opportunities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any amount of excess capacity or energy is sold on
the wholesale market, while any deficient capacity or energy position is filled
by either buying on the spot market or utilizing available generating capacity.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;<a name="EHW16800ac6_e3f4_45a8_976b_aa174cfead2d"></a>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW16800ac6_e3f4_45a8_976b_aa174cfead2d_"></a>The day-ahead resource
optimization begins with an analysis of projected hourly loads, existing
resources and operating reserve requirements.&nbsp;&nbsp;Firm forward
take-or-pay contracts are scheduled and counted towards meeting the capacity
needs of the day being pre-scheduled.&nbsp;&nbsp;The day-of resource
optimization involves minimizing system production costs each hour by lowering
or raising generating unit output or buying power and/or selling excess power
in the wholesale market all in order to meet the system load requirement and
operating reserve requirement.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any sale of excess power priced above
the incremental cost of producing such power </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:2.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

</DIV><HR noshade align="center" width="100%" size=2><DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always">&nbsp;</div><a name="page_25"></a><DIV bclPageBorder STYLE="BORDER-TOP: #000000 0cm dashed; BORDER-BOTTOM: #000000 0cm dashed; BORDER-LEFT: #000000 0cm dashed; BORDER-RIGHT: #000000 0cm dashed; PADDING-TOP: 0.3in; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0.3in; WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0.1in; PADDING-LEFT: 0.1in">

<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><a name=bcl_connect_prev></a><!-- Do not modify before this point! !--><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">reduces
the net production cost of operating the electrical system and thereby benefits
the end use customer.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Utilities endeavor to reduce the
electrical systems&#8217; net production cost by selling available excess energy when
it exists.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;<a name="EHWfba673bc_4de7_461b_a69f_f51dc3534c85"></a>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHWfba673bc_4de7_461b_a69f_f51dc3534c85_"></a>Real-time resource
optimization requires an hourly determination of whether to increase or
decrease the loading of on-line generating units, commit previously off-line
generating units, un-commit on-line generating units, sell excess power, or
purchase power in the real-time market to meet the companies&#8217; resource
needs.&nbsp;&nbsp;In order to achieve the lowest production cost, the projected
incremental or decremental cost of the next available generation resource
options are compared to determine the lowest cost option.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Construction
Program</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NVE&#8217;s
and the Utilities construction programs and estimated expenditures are subject
to continuing review, and are periodically revised to include the rate of load
growth, construction costs, availability of fuel types, the number and status
of proposed independent generation projects, the need for additional
transmission capacity in Nevada, regulatory considerations and impact to
customers, NVE&#8217;s and the Utilities&#8217; ability to raise necessary capital, and
changes in environmental regulations.&nbsp; Under the Utilities&#8217; franchise
agreements, they are obligated to provide a safe and reliable source of energy
to their customers.&nbsp; Capital construction expenditures and estimates are
reflective of the Utilities&#8217; obligation to serve their customer base.&#160;
Estimated construction expenditures may change depending on additional
resources needed by the Utilities as disclosed in the </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Load and Resources</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">
table, earlier.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Gross construction expenditures for 2012, including
AFUDC-debt, net salvage and CIAC, were $498.9 million, $287.6 million and
$211.3 million for NVE, NPC and SPPC, respectively, and for the period 2008
through 2012, were $4.1 billion, $3.2 billion and $907.8 million,
respectively.&nbsp; Cash requirements related to construction projects in 2012
for NVE, NPC and SPPC were $414.3 million, $245.2 million and $169.1 million,
respectively. Estimated construction expenditures for PUCN approved projects,
projects under contract, environmental compliance projects and other base
capital requirements are as follows (dollars in thousands):</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align=center style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:center;"><b><u><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">ENVIRONMENTAL
(NVE, NPC AND SPPC)</font></u></b></p>

<p align=center style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">As
with other utilities, NPC and SPPC </font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">are subject to
various environmental laws and regulations enforced by federal, state and local
authorities.&#160; </font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The EPA, NDEP, the Southern Nevada Health District, and
the Clark County Department of Air Quality and Environmental Management
administer regulations involving air quality, water pollution, solid, and
hazardous and toxic waste.&nbsp;&nbsp;Nevada&#8217;s Utility Environmental Protection
Act also requires the Utilities to obtain approval of the PUCN prior to
construction of major utility, generation or transmission facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">From the beginning phases of siting and development to the ongoing
operation of existing or new electric generating, transmission and distribution
facilities, our activities involve compliance with diverse laws and regulations
which address noise, emissions, impacts to air and water, protected and
cultural resources, and solid, hazardous, and toxic waste. Our activities often
require complex and lengthy processes as we obtain approvals, permits or
licenses for new, existing or modified facilities. Additionally, the use and
handling of various chemicals or hazardous materials (including waste) requires
release prevention plans and emergency response procedures. As new laws or
regulations are promulgated, we assess their applicability and implement the necessary
modifications to our facilities or our operations to ensure complete
compliance.&#160; </font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The most significant
environmental laws and regulations, both in effect and proposed, that could
impact NPC and SPPC are discussed below:</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:6.0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Federal
Environmental Laws, Regulations and Regulatory Initiatives</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; </font><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Clean
Air Standards</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The Clean Air Act (CAA) provides a framework for
protecting and improving the nation&#8217;s air quality and controlling mobile and
stationary sources of air emissions.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 1990 amendments to the CAA
impose limitations on the emissions of sulfur dioxide (SO<sub>2</sub>),
nitrogen oxide (NO<sub>X</sub>) as well as other pollutants. &nbsp;All of the
Utilities' fossil fuel generating stations are subject to these limitations and
are in compliance with current standards.&nbsp;&nbsp;Congress has from time to
time considered legislation that would amend the CAA to target specific
emissions from electric utility generating plants.&nbsp;&nbsp;The EPA has also
proposed potential regulations associated </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>
<DIV bclFooter>





<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font><font style="mso-no-proof:yes;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;">27</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:2.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
