<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name=bcl_connect_prev></a><!-- Do not modify before this point! !--><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">once
every twelve months so that the PUCN may verify the prudence of the energy
costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Nevada law also requires the PUCN to act on these cases
within a specified time period.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any of these costs determined by the
PUCN to have been imprudently incurred cannot be recovered from the Utilities&#8217;
customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">For a discussion
of NPC&#8217;s and SPPC&#8217;s recent and pending deferred energy rate cases, see Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory
Actions,</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> of the Notes to Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Material
disallowances of deferred energy costs or inadequate BTERs would have a significant
adverse effect on the Utilities&#8217; financial condition and future results of
operations, could cause downgrades of NVE&#8217;s and the Utilities&#8217; securities by
the rating agencies and could make it more difficult or expensive to finance
operations and construction projects and buy fuel, natural gas and purchased
power from third parties.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Utilities
purchase a portion of the power that they sell to their customers from power
suppliers.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the Utilities&#8217; and/or their power suppliers&#8217; credit
ratings are downgraded, the Utilities may experience difficulty entering into
new power supply contracts, and to the extent that they must rely on the spot
market, they may experience difficulty obtaining such power from suppliers in
the spot market in light of their financial condition, or the financial
condition of their power suppliers.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, if the Utilities
experience unexpected failures or outages in their generation facilities, they
may need to purchase a greater portion of the power they provide to their
customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;If access to liquidity is limited to obtain their power
requirements, particularly for NPC at the onset of the summer months, and the
Utilities are unable to obtain power through other means, their business,
operations and financial condition will be materially adversely affected.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">If
the Utilities cannot maintain the required level of renewable energy or procure
sufficient solar energy to meet Nevada&#8217;s Portfolio Standard, the PUCN may,
among other things, impose an administrative fine for noncompliance. </font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Nevada law sets
forth the Portfolio Standard requiring providers of electric service to
acquire, generate or save from renewable energy systems or energy efficiency
measures a specific percentage of its total retail sales from renewable energy
sources or efficiency measures, which increases over time.&#160; The standard also
includes a specific requirement for solar energy that must be met on an annual
basis by both Utilities.&#160; The required amount of renewable energy and available
supply can fluctuate widely based on multiple factors, including customer
energy use, changes in law or regulation, renewable resource availability, and
the contractual performance of renewable counterparties.&#160; These fluctuations
make the ability to anticipate future renewable energy needs and supplies
difficult.&#160; Renewable energy and qualified contributions from conservation and
energy efficiency measures must also be certified by the PUCN as forecasted
each year in order to be used by the Utilities for compliance with the
Portfolio Standard.&#160; In the event the Utilities do not fully meet the standard
in a given year, if the PUCN does not exempt them, they will be required to
make up the PEC deficiency in subsequent years and may be subject to a
financial penalty.&#160; While both Utilities are expected to be successful in 2012
with respect to the Portfolio Standard, the intermittent nature of renewable
energy, variations in customer load and any legislative changes in the
Portfolio Standard, mean that future years may still be subject to
uncertainty around the Utilities&#8217; ability to comply with the Portfolio
Standard.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Utilities&#8217; ability to access the capital markets
is dependent on their ability to obtain regulatory approval to do so. </font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Utilities
will need to continue to support capital expenditures and to refinance maturing
debt through external financing.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Utilities must obtain
regulatory approval in Nevada in order to borrow money or to issue securities
and are&nbsp;therefore&nbsp;dependent on the PUCN to issue favorable orders in
a timely manner to permit them to finance their operations, construction and
acquisition costs and to purchase power and fuel necessary to serve their
customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2012, NPC has financing authority from
the PUCN for the period ending December 31, 2013, consisting of authority (1)
to issue additional long-term debt securities of up to $725 million; (2) to
refinance up to approximately $322.5 million of long-term debt securities; and
(3) ongoing authority to maintain a revolving credit facility of up to $1.3
billion. As of December 31, 2012, SPPC has financing authority from the PUCN
for the period ending December 31, 2015, consisting of authority to (1) issue
additional long-term debt securities of up to $350 million; (2) to refinance approximately
$348 million of long-term debt securities; and (3) ongoing authority to
maintain a revolving credit facility of up to $600 million.&#160; However, we cannot
assure you that in the future the PUCN will issue such favorable orders or that
such favorable orders will be issued on a timely basis.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font color=#0070C0 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Risks
related to NVE and the Utilities&#8217; Environmental Matters</font></b></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font color=#0070C0 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Utilities are subject to numerous environmental laws and regulations that may
increase our cost of operations, impact or limit our business plans, expose us
to environmental liabilities, or make some electric generating units
uneconomical to maintain or operate.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Utilities are subject to extensive federal, state and local laws and
regulations relating to environmental protection.&nbsp;&nbsp;These laws and
regulations can result in increased capital, construction, operating, and other
costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;These laws and regulations generally require us to obtain and
comply with a wide variety of environmental licenses, permits, inspections and
other approvals, and may be enforced by both public officials and private
individuals.&nbsp;&nbsp;We cannot predict the outcome or effect of any action
or litigation that may arise from applicable environmental regulations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition,
either of the Utilities may be identified as a responsible party for
environmental cleanup by environmental agencies or regulatory
bodies.&nbsp;&nbsp;We cannot predict with certainty the amount or timing of
future expenditures related to environmental matters because of the difficulty
of estimating clean-up costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;There is also uncertainty in
quantifying liabilities under environmental laws that impose joint and several
liabilities on all potentially responsible parties.&nbsp;&nbsp;Environmental
regulations may also require us to install pollution control equipment at, or
perform environmental remediation on, our facilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Existing
environmental regulations regarding air emissions (such as NO<sub>X</sub>, SO<sub>2</sub>
or mercury emissions), water quality, coal combustion by products and other
pollutants may be revised or new climate change laws or regulations may be
adopted or become applicable to us.&nbsp;&nbsp;Revised or additional laws or
regulations, which may result in increased compliance costs, including the
adoption of new technologies or additional operating restrictions, could have a
material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations
particularly if those costs are not fully recoverable from our customers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Emissions of
nitrogen and sulfur oxides, mercury and particulates from fossil fueled
generating plants are potentially subject to increased regulations, controls
and mitigation expenses.&#160; Certain congressional leaders, environmental advocacy
groups and regulatory agencies in the U.S. have also been focusing considerable
attention on emissions from power generation facilities and their potential
role in climate change and/or regional air quality.&#160; Moreover, there are many
legislative and rulemaking initiatives pending at the federal and state level
that are aimed at the reduction of fossil plant emissions, as well as modification
of the NAAQS for ozone and other pollutants. We cannot predict the outcome of
pending or future legislative and rulemaking proposals.&nbsp;&nbsp;Future
changes in environmental laws or regulations governing emissions reductions
could make certain electric generating units, especially those utilizing coal
for fuel, uneconomical to construct, maintain or operate or could require
design changes or the adoption of new technologies that could significantly
increase costs or delay in-service dates.&#160; In addition, any legal obligation
that would require the Utilities to substantially reduce their emissions beyond
present levels could require extensive mitigation efforts and, in the case of
CO<sub>2</sub> legislation or regulation, would raise uncertainty about the
future viability of fossil fuels, particularly coal, as an energy source for
new and existing electric generation facilities. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:9.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;Furthermore,
we may not be able to obtain or maintain all environmental regulatory approvals
necessary to our business.&nbsp;&nbsp;If there is a delay in obtaining any
required environmental regulatory approval or if we fail to obtain, maintain or
comply with any such approval, operations at our affected facilities could be
delayed, halted or subjected to additional costs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Risks
related to NVE and the Utilities&#8217; Liquidity and Capital Resources </font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Changes
in actuarial pension and other postretirement assumptions and other factors may
increase NVE&#8217;s pension and other postretirement plan liability and funding
requirements</font></i></b><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Substantially
all of NVE employees are covered by a single employer defined benefit pension
and other postretirement plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;At present, the pension and other
postretirement plan is underfunded in that the projected benefit obligations
exceed the aggregate fair value of plan assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;The funded status of
the plan can be affected by contributions to plan assets, plan design,
investment returns on plan assets, discount rates, mortality rates of plan
participants, pension reform legislation and a number of other factors.&nbsp;&nbsp;There
can be no assurance that the value of NVE&#8217;s pension and other postretirement
plan assets will be sufficient to cover future liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although
NVE has made significant contributions to its pension and other postretirement
plan in recent years, it is possible that NVE could incur a significant pension
and other postretirement liability adjustment, or could be required to make
significant additional cash contributions to its plan, which would reduce the
cash available for operating activities, and have a material impact on
earnings.&nbsp; Refer to Note 10, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retirement Plan and Postretirement
Benefits,</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> of the Notes to Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>


<DIV bclFooter>

<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Utilities are subject to fuel and wholesale
electricity pricing risks, which could result in unanticipated liabilities and
cash flow requirements or increased volatility in our earnings, and to related
credit and liquidity risks. </font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Utilities&#8217; business and operations are subject to changes in
purchased power prices and fuel costs that may cause increases in the amounts
they must pay for power supplies on the wholesale market and the cost of
producing power in their generation plants.&nbsp;&nbsp;Prices for electricity,
fuel and natural gas may fluctuate substantially over relatively short periods
of time and expose the Utilities to significant commodity price
risks.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Increasing
energy commodity prices, particularly with respect to natural gas, have a
significant effect on our short-term liquidity.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although the
Utilities are entitled to recover their prudently incurred power, natural gas
and fuel costs through deferred energy rate case filings with the PUCN, if
current commodity prices increase, the Utilities&#8217; deferred energy balances will
increase, which will negatively affect our cash flow and liquidity until such
costs are recovered from customers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">If deemed
prudent, the Utilities may still purchase hedging instruments in the event
circumstances occur that may have the potential to increase the cost of fuel
and purchased power.&nbsp;&nbsp;As such, fluctuating commodity prices could
have a material adverse effect on their cash flows and their ability to operate
and, consequently, on our financial condition.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Utilities
are also subject to credit risk for losses that they incur as a result of
non-performance by counterparties of their contractual obligations to deliver
fuel, purchased power, natural gas (for resale) or settlement
payments.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Utilities often extend credit to counterparties and
customers and they are exposed to the risk that they may not be able to collect
amounts owed to them.&nbsp;&nbsp;Credit risk includes the risk that a
counterparty may default due to circumstances relating directly to it, and also
the risk that a counterparty may default due to circumstances that relate to
other market participants that have a direct or indirect relationship with such
counterparty.&nbsp;&nbsp;Should a counterparty, customer or supplier fail to
perform, the Utilities may be required to replace existing contracts with
contracts at then-current market prices or to honor the underlying commitment.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Utilities
are also subject to liquidity risk resulting from the exposure that their
counterparties perceive with respect to the possible non-performance by the
Utilities of their physical and financial obligations under their energy, fuel
and natural gas contracts.&nbsp;&nbsp;These counterparties may under certain
circumstances, pursuant to the Utilities&#8217; agreements with them, seek assurances
of performance from the Utilities in the form of letters of credit, prepayment
or cash deposits, or reduce availability under the Utilities&#8217; revolving credit
facilities for negative mark-to-market positions.&nbsp;&nbsp;In periods of
price volatility, the Utilities&#8217; exposure levels can change significantly,
which could have a significant negative impact on our liquidity and earnings.&nbsp;&nbsp;In
the event the Utilities&#8217; credit ratings are downgraded below investment grade,
the maximum amount of collateral the Utilities would currently be required to
post is approximately $86.7 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, the Utilities
must reduce their availability under their revolving credit facilities for
negative mark-to-market positions on hedging contracts with counterparties who
are lenders under the revolving credit facilities provided that the reduction
of availability under the revolving credit facilities shall at no time exceed
50% of the total commitments then in effect under the credit facilities.&#160; As of
December 31, 2012, the Utilities were not parties to any hedging contracts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">If
NVE is precluded from receiving dividends from the Utilities, its financial
condition, and its ability to meet its debt service obligations, pay dividends
and make capital contributions to its subsidiaries, will be materially
adversely affected.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Since
NVE is a holding company, substantially all of its cash flow is provided by
dividends paid to NVE by NPC and SPPC on their common stock, all of which is
owned by NVE.&nbsp;&nbsp;Since NPC and SPPC are public utilities, they are
subject to regulation by the PUCN, which may impose limits on investment
returns or otherwise impact the amount of dividends that the Utilities may
declare and pay.&nbsp; While the PUCN has in the past imposed a dividend
restriction with respect to NPC and SPPC, as of December 31, 2012, there were
no dividend restrictions imposed on the Utilities by the PUCN.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;In
addition, certain agreements entered into by the Utilities set restrictions on
the amount of dividends they may declare and pay and restrict the circumstances
under which such dividends may be declared and paid.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of
the Utilities&#8217; credit rating on their senior secured debt at investment grade
by S&amp;P and Moody&#8217;s, these restrictions are suspended and no longer in
effect so long as the debt remains investment grade by both rating
agencies.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to the restrictions imposed by specific agreements,
the Federal Power Act prohibits the payment of dividends from &#8220;capital
accounts.&#8221;&nbsp;&nbsp;Although the meaning of this provision is unclear, the
Utilities believe that the Federal Power Act restriction, as applied to their
particular circumstances, would not be construed or applied by the FERC to
prohibit the payment of dividends for lawful and legitimate business purposes
from current year earnings, or in the absence of current year earnings, from
other/additional paid-in capital accounts.&nbsp;&nbsp;If, however, the FERC
were to interpret this provision differently, the ability of the Utilities to
pay dividends to NVE could be jeopardized.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">We cannot assure investors
that future dividend payments on NVE&#8217;s Common Stock will be made or, if made,
in what amounts they may be paid. </font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Dividends are considered periodically by NVE&#8217;s BOD and
are subject to factors that ordinarily affect dividend policy, such as current
and prospective financial condition, earnings and liquidity, prospective
business conditions, regulatory factors, and dividend restrictions in NVE&#8217;s and
the Utilities&#8217; financing agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The BOD will continue to review
these&nbsp;factors on a periodic basis to determine if and when it would be
prudent to declare a dividend on NVE&#8217;s Common Stock;&nbsp;however, there is no
guarantee that dividends will be paid in the future, or that, if paid, the
dividends will be paid in the same amount or with the same frequency as in the
past.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE&#8217;s indebtedness is
effectively subordinated to the liabilities of its subsidiaries, particularly
NPC and SPPC.&nbsp;&nbsp;NVE and the Utilities have the ability to issue a
significant amount of additional indebtedness under the terms of their various
financing agreements.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Because NVE is a
holding company, its indebtedness is effectively subordinated to the Utilities&#8217;
existing indebtedness and other future liabilities, including claims by the
Utilities&#8217; trade creditors, debt holders, secured creditors, taxing
authorities, and guarantee holders.&nbsp;&nbsp;NVE conducts substantially all
of its operations through its subsidiaries, and thus NVE&#8217;s ability to meet its
obligations under its indebtedness and to pay any dividends on its common stock
will be dependent on the earnings and cash flows of those subsidiaries and the
ability of those subsidiaries to pay dividends or to advance or repay funds to
NVE.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2012, the Utilities had approximately $4.5
billion of debt outstanding.&nbsp;&nbsp;The terms of NVE&#8217;s indebtedness
restrict the amount of additional indebtedness that NVE and the Utilities may
issue.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on NVE&#8217;s December 31, 2012 financial statements, NVE&#8217;s
indebtedness restrictions would allow NVE and the Utilities to issue up to approximately
$3.3 billion</font><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> </font></b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">of additional indebtedness in the aggregate, plus
indebtedness that is specifically permitted under the terms of NVE&#8217;s
indebtedness.&#160; However, NPC and SPPC are subject to restrictions under the
terms of their various financing agreements and PUCN restrictions on their
ability to issue additional indebtedness.&#160; See Note 8, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Debt Covenant and
Other Restrictions, </font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">of the Notes to Financial Statements.</font></p>








<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><a name="Unresolved_bclEnd"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">None.</font></p>








<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><a name="Properties_bclEnd"></a><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Substantially all of NPC&#8217;s and SPPC&#8217;s property in
Nevada is subject to the lien of the General and Refunding Mortgage Indentures
dated as of May 1, 2001, between NPC and SPPC, respectively, and The Bank of
New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A., as trustee, as amended and supplemented.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NVE&#8217;s total summer MW capacity and units were 6,078
and 61 units, respectively.&#160; The following is a list of the Utilities&#8217; share of
electric generation plants including the type and fuel used, the anticipated
2013 net capacity (MW), and the years that the units were installed.</font></p>

is no guarantee that NVE will continue to pay dividends in the future, or that
the dividends will be paid at the same amount or with the same frequency.&nbsp;
See Note 8, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Debt Covenant and Other Restrictions,</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;"> of the Notes to

&nbsp;</font></sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;">During the fourth quarter of
2012, SPPC discovered an error in its calculation of accumulated deferred
income taxes and the related income tax regulatory asset specific to amounts
associated with AFUDC-equity resulting in an understatement of both regulatory
assets and deferred tax liabilities of the same amount.&nbsp; Total Assets for
NVE has been corrected in the table above as of December 31, 2011, 2010, 2009,
and 2008, by $32.0 million, $30.6 million, $28.9 million, and $27.3 million,
respectively.&#160; Refer to Note 1, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies,
NVE and SPPC Balance Sheet Corrections</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;">, of the Notes to Financial
Statements for further information. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=#0070C0 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE&#8217;s Utilities
operate three regulated business segments which are NPC electric, SPPC electric
and SPPC natural gas.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Utilities are public utilities engaged in
the generation, transmission, distribution and sale of electricity and, in the
case of SPPC, sale of natural gas.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other operations consist mainly
of unregulated operations and the holding company operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;The
Utilities are the principal operating subsidiaries of NVE and account for
substantially all of NVE&#8217;s assets and revenues.&nbsp;&nbsp;NVE, NPC and SPPC
are separate filers for SEC reporting purposes and as such this discussion has
been divided to reflect the individual filers (NVE, NPC and SPPC), except for
discussions that relate to all three entities or the Utilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Utilities
are regulated by the PUCN with respect to rates, standards of service, siting
of and necessity for generation and certain transmission facilities,
accounting, issuance of securities and other matters with respect to generation,
distribution and transmission operations.&#160; The FERC has jurisdiction under the
Federal Power Act with respect to wholesale rates, service, interconnection,
accounting, and other matters in connection with the Utilities&#8217; sale of
electricity for resale and interstate transmission.&nbsp;&nbsp;The FERC also
has jurisdiction over the natural gas pipeline companies from which the
Utilities take service.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of regulation, many of the
fundamental business decisions of the Utilities, as well as the ROR they are
permitted to earn on their utility assets, are subject to the approval of
governmental agencies.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Utilities&#8217;
revenues and operating income are subject to fluctuations during the year due
to impacts that seasonal weather, rate changes, and customer usage patterns
have on demand for electric energy and resources.&nbsp;&nbsp;NPC is a summer
peaking utility experiencing its highest retail energy sales in response to the
demand for air conditioning.&nbsp;&nbsp;SPPC&#8217;s electric system peak typically occurs
in the summer, while its gas business typically peaks in the
winter.&nbsp;&nbsp;The variations in energy usage due to varying weather,
customer growth and other energy usage patterns, including energy efficiency
and conservation measures, necessitates a continual balancing of loads and
resources and purchases and sales of energy under short and long term energy
supply contracts.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, the prudent management and
optimization of available resources has a direct effect on the operating and
financial performance of the Utilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, the timely
recovery of purchased power and fuel costs, and other costs, and the ability to
earn a fair return on investments through rates are essential to the operating
and financial performance of the Utilities.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Overview of Major Factors Affecting Results of

net income of $321.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2012, compared to
$163.4 million for the same period in 2011.&#160; The increase in net income is
primarily due to the following pre-tax items:</font></p>

the decrease in net income was a decrease in interest expense and reduced
operating expenses.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE Transformation</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Beginning in
2006, NVE committed to an energy strategy to manage resources against our load
by constructing/purchasing generating facilities, purchasing and developing
renewable energy, encouraging energy efficiency and conservation programs, as
well as, expanding our transmission capability in an effort to reduce our
reliance on purchased power.&#160; The implementation of this strategy required
significant amounts of liquidity and capital.&#160; To meet these capital
requirements during the transformation, NVE and the Utilities issued,
refinanced and reduced debt which improved credit ratings and decreased
interest costs.&#160; At the same time, management worked with the PUCN to
communicate the necessity of investments to better serve our customers, the
prudency of costs incurred and the importance of a reasonable and timely return
on such investments for our shareholders.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The energy
strategy and regulatory diligence discussed above created a strong foundation
for NVE and the Utilities to earn our allowable return on their investments
during 2012, while meeting a higher percentage of its load through owned
generation.&#160; Additionally, as a result of our financial policies, which focused
on lowering interest rates and reducing debt, interest costs decreased and our
capital structure improved during 2012.&#160; Furthermore, through employee
dedication and increased use of technology we continued to improve processes to
enhance performance while keeping operating and maintenance costs relatively
stable.&#160; As a result, NVE was able to generate free cash flow in 2012, which
has provided it the ability to increase its dividend while preserving its
ability to invest in new opportunities.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Key
Initiatives </font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The economy in Nevada continues to recover slowly.&#160; While a low growth
environment can be challenging, the foundation established in prior years,
including establishing energy independence, improving capital structure and
liquidity and managing our regulatory environment, has positioned the Utilities
to operate in this environment.&#160; However, NVE and the Utilities continue to
implement and develop key initiatives that collectively may further our ability
to increase our common stock dividend, strengthen our capital structure and
consider new investment opportunities.&#160; These initiatives should enable us to
contain operating and maintenance costs while effectively managing our
regulatory environment and continuing to promote and improve a safe and
reliable work environment.&#160;&#160; These key initiatives are discussed below.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; Continuous Improvement of</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">
</font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Safety&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;text-align:justify;"><a name="EHW0c7a5dcd_4b1a_489e_ba79_85918f5d9635"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW0c7a5dcd_4b1a_489e_ba79_85918f5d9635_"></a>The safety of NVE&#8217;s
employees and the public is a core value of NVE and the Utilities. Accordingly,
NVE has worked to integrate a set of safety principles into their business
operations and culture.&nbsp; These principles include complying with
applicable safety, health, and security regulations and implementing programs
and processes aimed at continually improving safety and security
conditions.&nbsp; Our initiatives in 2013 and beyond will include modeling a
safety culture in all areas of the company similar to the achievements
recognized at SPPC&#8217;s Fort Churchill Generating Station.&#160; In January 2013, </font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">t</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">he Fort Churchill Generating Station reached a
safety milestone of operating 25 years without a lost-time
accident.&nbsp;According to the Edison Electric Institute, the 226-MW natural
gas-fueled plant has the longest safety record for any fossil-fueled generating
station in the nation. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; Empower Customers through
Focused Service and Efficiency Programs</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NV Energize is
a NVE project that includes Advanced Meter Infrastructure, Smart Grid
Technology and Meter Data Management.&#160; The NV Energize capabilities will allow
NVE to help customers better manage their usage with the most cost-effective
mix of pricing, service, efficiency and conservation options. &#160;As of December
31, 2012, NVE had installed approximately 1.3 million Smart Meters in Nevada,
and the implementation of the NV Energize project is nearing completion.&#160; NVE
expects to substantially complete the installation process of the final 80,000 Smart
Meters before the end of the second quarter of 2013.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The NV Energize
system provides more convenience for customers and is achieving operating
savings through both automated meter reading and the elimination to date of
approximately 1 million trips to customers&#8217; premises to process service
requests.&#160; The system also enables NVE to launch new customer programs.&#160; Recruitment
of participants for a trial of a combination of time based rates, supporting
technology and education options is now underway.&#160; New detailed customer usage
reports have been integrated into our web self-service capability, and
customers can also request alerts on their billing information.&#160; An enhanced
air conditioning demand response program was launched in the fourth quarter.&#160;&#160;
It is designed to provide energy market based rebates for specific event
participation and also includes an energy efficiency management capability.&#160;
Similar programs for commercial customers are under development. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; Managing Generation Portfolio
Within Environmental Compliance</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">As discussed in
more detail in Note 12, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Commitments and Contingencies</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the Notes to
Financial Statements, certain generating stations of NVE are affected under
EPA&#8217;s Regional Haze Rules.&#160; The implementation costs of the Regional Haze Rules
are significant.&#160; Therefore, NVE must balance the cost of implementing the
retrofits associated with the Regional Haze Rule with the effect current and future
load requirements, retirements of generating stations and plant outages will
have on its ability to serve its customers reliably.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Investment
opportunities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE continues to explore investment opportunities that may benefit our
customers and that will add to our core business of generation, transmission
and distribution of energy.&#160; In addition, NVE&#8217;s geographical location affords
it access to various renewable resources for potential investment opportunities.</font></p>








<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align=center style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">CRITICAL ACCOUNTING POLICIES AND ESTIMATES</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NVE prepared its
consolidated&nbsp;financial&nbsp;statements in accordance with
GAAP.&nbsp;&nbsp;In doing so, certain&nbsp;estimates&nbsp;were made that
were&nbsp;critical&nbsp;in nature to the&nbsp;results&nbsp;of operations.&nbsp;
The following discusses those significant estimates that may have a
material&nbsp;impact on the financial&nbsp;results of NVE and the Utilities and
are subject to the greatest amount of subjectivity.&nbsp;&nbsp;Senior
management has discussed the development and selection of these
critical&nbsp;accounting policies with the Audit Committee of NVE's
BOD.&nbsp;&nbsp;The items discussed below represent critical accounting
estimates that under different conditions or using different assumptions could
have a material effect on the financial condition, results of operation, cash
flows, liquidity and capital resources of NVE and the Utilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Regulatory
Accounting</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The Utilities&#8217; retail rates are currently subject to
the approval of the PUCN and are designed to recover the cost of providing
generation, transmission and distribution services.&nbsp; NVE is a &#8220;holding
company&#8221; under the Public Utility Holding Company Act of 2005 (PUHCA
2005).&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, NVE and all of its subsidiaries (whether or not
engaged in any energy related business) are required to maintain books, accounts
and other records in accordance with FERC regulations and to make them
available to the FERC and the PUCN.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the PUCN or the
FERC have the authority to review allocations of costs of non-power goods and
administrative services among NVE and its subsidiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;The FERC has
the authority generally to require that rates subject to its jurisdiction be
just and reasonable and in this context would continue to be able to, among
other things, review transactions between NVE, NPC and/or SPPC and/or any other
affiliated company.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=#0070C0 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">As
a result, the Utilities qualify for the application of regulatory accounting
treatment as allowed by the Regulated Operations Topic of the
FASC.&nbsp;&nbsp;The accounting guidance for regulated operations recognizes
that the rate actions of a regulator can provide reasonable assurance of the
existence of an asset and requires the capitalization of incurred costs that
would otherwise be charged to expense where it is probable that future revenue
will be provided to recover these costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The accounting guidance
prescribes the method to be used to record the financial transactions of a
regulated entity.&nbsp;&nbsp;The criteria for applying the accounting guidance
for regulated operations include the following: (i) rates are set by an
independent third party regulator, (ii) approved rates are intended to recover
the specific costs of the regulated products or services, and (iii) rates that
are set at levels that will recover costs can be charged to and collected from
customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under federal law, wholesale rates charged by the
Utilities are subject to certain jurisdictional regulation, primarily by the
FERC.&nbsp;&nbsp;The FERC has jurisdiction under the Federal Power Act with
respect to rates, service, interconnection, accounting, and other matters in
connection with the Utilities&#8217; sale of electricity for resale and interstate
transmission.&nbsp;&nbsp;The FERC also has jurisdiction over the natural gas
pipeline companies from which the Utilities take service.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Regulatory
assets represent incurred costs that have been deferred because it is probable
they will be recovered through future rates collected from
customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Regulatory liabilities generally represent obligations to
make refunds to customers for previous collections for costs that are not
likely to be incurred.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although current rates do not include the
recovery of all existing regulatory assets as discussed further below and in
Note 1, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">, of the Notes to
Financial Statements, management believes the existing regulatory assets are
probable of recovery either because we have received prior PUCN approval or due
to regulatory precedent set for similar circumstances.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management&#8217;s
judgment reflects the current political and regulatory climate in the state,
and is subject to change in the future.&nbsp;&nbsp;If future recovery of costs
ceases to be probable, the write-off of regulatory assets would be required to
be recognized as a charge and expensed in current period earnings.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Regulatory
Accounting affects other Critical Accounting Policies, including Deferred
Energy Accounting, Accounting for Pensions, and Accounting for Derivatives and
Hedging Activities, all of which are discussed immediately below.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font color=#002060 face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;</font><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Deferred Energy
Accounting</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Under deferred energy accounting, to the extent actual
fuel and purchased power costs exceed fuel and purchased power costs
recoverable through current rates, the excess is not recorded as a current
expense on the statement of operations but rather is deferred and recorded as
an asset on the balance sheet.&nbsp;&nbsp;Conversely, a liability is recorded
to the extent fuel and purchased power costs recoverable through current rates
exceed actual fuel and purchased power costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;These excess amounts
are reflected in adjustments to rates and recorded as revenue or expense in future
time periods, subject to PUCN approval.&nbsp;&nbsp;Nevada law provides that the
PUCN may </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>
<DIV bclFooter>





<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font><font style="mso-no-proof:yes;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;">50</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:2.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
</DIV><HR noshade align="center" width="100%" size=2><DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always">&nbsp;</div><a name="page_51"></a><DIV bclPageBorder STYLE="BORDER-TOP: #000000 0cm dashed; BORDER-BOTTOM: #000000 0cm dashed; BORDER-LEFT: #000000 0cm dashed; BORDER-RIGHT: #000000 0cm dashed; PADDING-TOP: 0.3in; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0.3in; WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0.1in; PADDING-LEFT: 0.1in">

<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><a name=bcl_connect_prev></a><!-- Do not modify before this point! !--><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">not allow the recovery of any costs for
purchased fuel or purchased power &#8220;that were the result of any practice or
transaction that was undertaken, managed or performed imprudently by the
electric utility.&#8221;&nbsp;&nbsp;Nevada law specifies that fuel and purchased
power costs include all costs incurred to purchase fuel, to purchase capacity,
and to purchase energy.&nbsp;&nbsp;Both Utilities are entitled under statute to
utilize deferred energy accounting for their electric operations and both
Utilities accumulate amounts in their deferral of energy costs
accounts.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Utilities also record a carrying charge, equal to the
weighted cost of capital, on such deferred balances, recognized as interest
income/expense on regulatory items in the current period.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
Utilities are exposed to commodity price risk primarily related to changes in
the market price of electricity, and the suspension of our hedging program, as
well as changes in fuel costs incurred to generate electricity.&nbsp;&nbsp;See
Item 7A, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">, for
a discussion of the Utilities&#8217; purchased power procurement strategies, and
commodity price risk and commodity risk management
program.&nbsp;&nbsp;Currently, commodity price increases and decreases are
recoverable through the deferred energy accounting mechanism, with no
anticipated effect on earnings.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, the Utilities are subject
to regulatory risk related to commodity price changes due to the fact that the
PUCN may disallow recovery for any of these costs that it considers imprudently
incurred.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">See
Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Regulatory Actions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">, of the Notes to Financial Statements, for
additional discussion of the regulatory process to recover these deferred
costs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Energy
Efficiency Implementation Rate (EEIR) and Energy Efficiency Program Rate (EEPR)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In July 2010, regulations were adopted by the Nevada
Legislature that authorizes an electric utility to recover lost revenue that is
attributable to the measurable and verifiable effects associated with the
implementation of efficiency and conservation programs approved by the PUCN.&#160;
As a result, the Utilities file annually in March, to adjust rates and set a
clearing rate or EEIR effective in October of the same year for over or under
collected balance, similar to the deferred energy mechanism discussed above. In
addition, the regulation approved the transition of the recovery for the
implementation costs of energy efficiency programs from general rates (filed
every 3 years) to recovery through annual rate filings annually in March, to
adjust rates and set a clearing rate or EEPR effective in October of the same
year for over or under collected balance, similar to the deferred energy
mechanism discussed above.&#160; See Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Regulatory Actions, </font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">of the Notes
to Financial Statements for details regarding EEIR and EEPR balances.&#160; Although
a rate is established for EEIR, the actual effects associated with the
implementation of energy efficiency and conservation programs is still subject
to a measurement and verification process by the PUCN.&#160; To the extent the PUCN
does not approve the measurement and </font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">verification
amounts, the Utilities may not be allowed recovery of such amounts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Fair Value
Measurements and Disclosures</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NVE and the Utilities&#8217; follow the Fair Value
Measurements and Disclosure Topic of the FASC, which defines fair value,
establishes a framework for measuring fair value and enhances disclosures about
assets and liabilities recorded at fair value.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Fair
Value Measurements and Disclosure Topic of the FASC establishes a three-level
hierarchy which requires an entity to maximize the use of observable inputs and
minimize the use of unobservable inputs when measuring fair value.&nbsp; The
three levels are defined as follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Level 1 &#8211; Quoted prices in active markets for
identical assets or liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Active markets are those in which
transactions for the asset or liability occur in sufficient frequency and
volume to provide pricing information on an ongoing basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Level 1
primarily consists of financial instruments such as exchange-traded derivatives
and listed equities.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Level 2 &#8211; Observable inputs other than Level 1 prices,
such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities; quoted prices in
markets that are not active; or other inputs that are observable or can be
corroborated by observable market data for substantially the full term of the
assets or liabilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Level 3 &#8211; Unobservable
inputs that are supported by little or no market activity and that are
significant.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;As
required by the Fair Value Measurements and Disclosure Topic of the FASC,
financial assets and liabilities are classified in their entirety based on the
lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurement.&#160;
&nbsp;NVE and the Utilities&#8217; assessment of the significance of a particular
input to fair value measurements requires judgment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value
of the Utilities&#8217; assets and liabilities are sensitive to market price
fluctuations that can occur on a daily basis.&#160; The use of different assumptions
and variables in determining fair value could significantly impact the
valuation and classification within the fair value hierarchy of assets and
liabilities.&#160; See Note 1, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">,
Note 4, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Investments and Other Property</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;"> and Note 10, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Retirement &nbsp;</font></i><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>
<DIV bclFooter>





<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font><font style="mso-no-proof:yes;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;">51</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><a name=bcl_connect_prev></a><!-- Do not modify before this point! !--><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Plan and Postretirement Benefits</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;"> of the Notes to
Financial Statements for more detailed disclosure of NVE&#8217;s, NPC&#8217;s and SPPC&#8217;s
fair value measurements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Accounting for
Income Taxes</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Current and deferred income tax provisions
and benefits as well as deferred income tax assets and liabilities involve
significant management estimates and judgments.&nbsp; NVE and the Utilities
file a consolidated federal income tax return.&#160; Current income taxes are
allocated based on NVE and the Utilities&#8217; respective taxable income or loss and
tax credits as if each utility filed a separate return.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NVE and the Utilities recognize deferred tax
liabilities and assets for the future tax consequences of events that have been
included in the financial statements or tax returns.&nbsp; Deferred tax
liabilities and assets are determined based on the difference between the
financial statement and tax basis of assets and liabilities using tax rates in
effect for the year in which the differences are expected to reverse.&nbsp;
Deferred tax assets are also recorded for deductions incurred and credits
earned that have not been utilized in tax returns filed or to be filed for tax
years through the date of the financial statements.&#160; Management considers
estimates of the amount and character of future taxable income by tax
jurisdiction in assessing the likelihood of realization of deferred tax
assets.&nbsp; If it is not more likely than not that a deferred tax asset will
be realized in its entirety, a valuation allowance is recorded with respect to
the portion estimated not likely to be realized.&#160; Management has determined
that the Federal NOL does not require a valuation allowance based on
projections of future taxable income and the reversal of deferred tax
liabilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">At December 31, 2012, NVE had a gross Federal NOL
