<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Actual
income taxes could vary from estimated amounts due to the future impacts of
various items, including changes in income tax laws, our financial condition
and results of operations in future periods, and the review of filed tax
returns by taxing authorities.&#160; NVE and the Utilities&#8217; income tax returns are
regularly audited by applicable tax authorities.&#160; Tax benefits associated with
income tax positions taken, or expected to be taken, in a tax return are
recorded only when the more-likely-than-not recognition threshold is satisfied
and measured at the largest amount of benefit that is greater than 50% likely
of being realized upon settlement.&nbsp; NVE and the Utilities classify
interest and penalties associated with unrecognized tax benefits as interest
and other expense, respectively, within the income statement.&#160; No interest
expense or penalties associated with unrecognized tax benefits have been
recorded.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2012, NVE and the Utilities recorded a
liability for uncertain tax positions of approximately $6.6 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
Utilities reduce rates to reflect the current tax benefits associated with
recognizing certain tax deductions sooner than when the expenses are recognized
for financial reporting purposes.&nbsp; A regulatory asset is recorded for
these amounts to reflect the future increases in income taxes payable that will
be recovered from customers when these temporary differences reverse.&nbsp; The
Utilities have been fully normalized since 1987.&nbsp; AFUDC-equity is recorded
on an after-tax basis.&nbsp; Accordingly, a regulatory asset is recorded when
AFUDC-equity is recognized.&nbsp; This regulatory asset reverses as the related
plant is depreciated, resulting in an increase to the tax provision.&#160; The
Utilities also record regulatory liabilities for obligations to reduce rates
charged customers for deferred taxes recovered from customers in prior years at
corporate tax rates higher than the current tax rates.&nbsp; The reduction in
rates charged customers will occur as the temporary differences resulting in
the excess deferred tax liabilities reverse. &#160;NVE and subsidiaries had a net
regulatory tax liability of $254.6 million at December 31, 2012.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Environmental Contingencies</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NVE
and its subsidiaries are subject to federal, state and local regulations
governing air and water quality, hazardous and solid waste, land use and other
environmental considerations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Nevada&#8217;s Utility Environmental
Protection Act requires approval of the </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><a name=bcl_connect_prev></a><!-- Do not modify before this point! !--><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">PUCN prior to
construction of major utility, generation or transmission
facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;The EPA, NDEP and Clark County Department of Air Quality
and Environmental Management administer regulations involving air and water
quality, solid, and hazardous and toxic waste.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NVE
and its subsidiaries are subject to rising costs that result from a steady
increase in the number of federal, state and local laws and regulations
designed to protect the environment.&nbsp;&nbsp;These laws and regulations can
result in increased capital, operating, and other costs as a result of
compliance, remediation, containment and monitoring obligations, particularly
with laws relating to power plant emissions.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, NVE or its
subsidiaries may be a responsible party for environmental cleanup at any site
identified by a regulatory body.&nbsp;&nbsp;The management of NVE and its
subsidiaries cannot predict with certainty the amount and timing of all future
expenditures related to environmental matters because of the difficulty of
estimating cleanup costs and compliance and the possibility that changes will
be made to current environmental laws and regulations.&nbsp;&nbsp;There is also
uncertainty in quantifying liabilities under environmental laws that impose
joint and several liabilities on all potentially responsible parties.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Depending
on whether environmental liabilities occurred from normal operations or as part
of new environmental laws, the Utilities accrue for environmental remediation
liabilities in accordance with the accounting guidance required by the Asset
Retirement and Environmental Obligations Topic of the FASC.&nbsp;&nbsp;Estimated
costs from environmental remediation obligations generally are recognized no
later than completion of the remedial feasibility study or when the accounting
requirements for environmental obligations have been met.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such costs
are adjusted as additional information develops or circumstances change.&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain
environmental costs receive regulatory accounting treatment, under which the
costs are recorded as regulatory assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Recoveries of environmental
remediation costs from other parties are recognized when their receipt is
deemed probable.&nbsp; Environmental expenditures that have future economic
benefits are capitalized in accordance with our asset capitalization policy.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Note
1, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Asset Retirement
Obligations,</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;"> of the Notes to Financial Statements and Note 12, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Commitments
and Contingencies,</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;"> of the Notes to Financial Statements, discusses the
environmental matters of NVE and its subsidiaries that have been identified,
and the estimated financial effect of those matters.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the extent
that (1) actual results differ from the estimated financial effects, (2) there
are environmental matters not yet identified for which NVE or its subsidiaries
are determined to be responsible, or (3) the Utilities are unable to recover
through future rates the costs to remediate such environmental matters, there
could be a material adverse effect on the financial condition and future
liquidity and results of operations of NVE and its subsidiaries.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Defined Benefit Plans and Other Postretirement Plans</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">As further explained in Note 10, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retirement
Plan and Postretirement Benefits,</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> of the Notes to Financial Statements, NVE
maintains a qualified pension plan, a non-qualified supplemental executive
retirement plan (SERP) and restoration plan, as well as a postretirement
benefit (OPEB) plan which provides health and life insurance for retired
employees. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; Pension Plans</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE&#8217;s reported costs of providing
non-contributory defined pension benefits (described in Note 10, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retirement
Plan and Postretirement Benefits,</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> of the Notes to Financial Statements) are
dependent upon numerous factors resulting from actual plan experience and
assumptions for future experience.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In accordance with the Compensation
Retirement Benefits Topic of the FASC, changes in pension obligations
associated with these factors may not be immediately recognized as pension
costs on the income statement, but generally are recognized in future years
over the remaining average service period of plan participants. As such,
significant portions of pension costs recorded in any period may not reflect
the actual level of cash benefits provided to plan participants. Furthermore,
the Compensation Retirement Benefits Topic of the FASC requires the immediate
recognition of changes in benefit obligations due to differences between
actuarial assumptions and actual experience in Accumulated Other Comprehensive
Income, net of taxes. However, since NVE recovers costs through rates, amounts
to be recovered in rates will be recorded as Other Regulatory Assets under the
provisions of the Regulated Operations Topic of the FASC, and will be
recognized as expense over a period of time.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">For the years ended December 31, 2012,
2011, and 2010, NVE recorded pension expense for all pension plans of
approximately $19.7 million, $24.0 million, and $30.8 million, respectively, in
accordance with the accounting guidance as defined by the Compensation
Retirement Benefits Topic of the FASC. Actual payments of benefits made to
retirees and terminated vested employees for the years ended December 31, 2012,
2011 and 2010 were $73.0 million, $42.5 million, and $58.0 million,
respectively.&#160; Pension costs are impacted by actual employee demographics
(including age and employment periods), the level of contributions NVE makes to
the plan, and earnings on plan assets. Changes made to the provisions of the
plan may also impact current and future pension costs. Pension costs may also
be significantly affected by changes in key actuarial assumptions, including
anticipated rates of return </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><a name=bcl_connect_prev></a><!-- Do not modify before this point! !--><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">on plan assets, the
discount rates and demographic (mortality, retirement, termination) assumptions
used in determining the projected benefit obligation and pension costs.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In 2012, NVE offered a voluntary lump sum
pension payout to former employees not currently of retirement age but eligible
for future benefits and certain retiree participants already receiving benefits
under NVE&#8217;s pension plan in an effort to reduce NVE&#8217;s future pension
obligation.&#160; The 2012 payouts increased the benefits paid by approximately
$28.9 million.&#160; NVE expects to payout an additional lump sum of approximately
$15.6 million from the pension assets during 2013 based on outstanding offers
at December 31, 2012.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Plan Assets</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE&#8217;s
pension plan assets are primarily made up of equity and fixed income
investments.&#160; Fluctuations in actual equity market returns as well as changes
in general interest rates may result in increased or decreased pension costs in
future periods. See Note 10, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retirement and Postretirement Benefits,</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> of
the Notes to Financial Statements, for further discussion on NVE&#8217;s investment
strategy and asset allocation.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Plan Assumptions
and Sensitivities Analysis</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">As further described in Note 10, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Retirement Plan and Postretirement
Benefits,</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;"> of the Notes to Financial Statements, NVE has revised the pension
plan discount rate for its 2012 benefit obligations to 4.01%, as compared to
the 2011 benefit obligations rate of 4.91%.&#160; In determining the pension benefit
obligation and related costs, these assumptions can change with each
measurement date, and such changes could result in material changes to such
amounts.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">As disclosed in Note 10, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retirement
and Postretirement Benefits,</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> of the Notes to Financial Statements, the
funded status of the plan has decreased compared to the prior year due
primarily to the change in the discount rate.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The pension plan discount rates for
2012 and 2011 related to the benefit obligations were determined by identifying
a theoretical settlement portfolio of high quality corporate bonds sufficient
to provide for the plans projected benefit payments.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The pension plan discount rates for 2012 related to the net
periodic benefit costs were determined by identifying a theoretical settlement
portfolio of high quality corporate bonds sufficient to provide for the plans
projected benefit payments. However, to determine the pension plan discount
rates for 2011 and 2010 related to the net periodic benefit costs, NVE&#8217;s
projected benefit payments were matched to the yield curve derived from a
portfolio of over 300 high quality Aa bonds with yields within the 10th to 90th
percentiles of these bond yields.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In selecting an assumed rate of
return on plan assets, NVE considers past performance and economic forecasts
for the types of investments held by the plan.&#160; NVE used an assumed rate of
return on plan assets of 6.15% for 2012 and 6.75% for 2011, as disclosed in
Note 10, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retirement and Postretirement Benefits,</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> of the Notes to
Financial Statements. Actual return on pension plan assets increased by
approximately $8.0 million in 2012 and $7.3 million in 2011.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The

actuarial assumptions by the indicated percentage for all pension plans
(dollars in thousands): </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other
Postretirement Benefits</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE&#8217;s
reported costs of providing other postretirement benefits (described in Note 10,
</font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retirement Plan and Postretirement Benefits</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> of the Notes to Financial
Statements) are dependent upon numerous factors resulting from actual plan
experience and assumptions of future experience.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December 31,
2012, 2011, and 2010, NVE recorded other postretirement benefit expense of $2.7
million, $5.0 million, and $5.4 million, respectively, in accordance with the
provisions of the Compensation Retirement Benefits Topic of the FASC. Actual
payments of benefits made to retirees for the year ended December 31, 2012,
2011 and 2010 were $11.2 million, $12.3 million, and $12.5 million,
respectively.&#160; Other postretirement benefit costs are impacted by actual
employee demographics (including age and employment periods), the level of
contributions made to the plan, earnings on plan assets, and health care cost
trends. Changes made to the provisions of the plan may also impact current and
future other postretirement benefit costs. Other postretirement benefit costs
may also be significantly affected by changes in key actuarial assumptions,
including anticipated rates of return on plan assets, discount rates and
demographic (mortality, retirement, termination) assumptions used in
determining the postretirement benefit obligation and postretirement costs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Plan Assets</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE&#8217;s other postretirement benefit
plan assets are primarily made up of equity and fixed income investments.&#160;
Fluctuations in actual equity market returns, as well as, changes in general
interest rates may result in increased or decreased other postretirement
benefit costs in future periods. See Note 10, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retirement and Postretirement
Benefits</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> of the Notes to Financial Statements, for further discussion on
NVE&#8217;s investment strategy and asset allocation.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Plan Assumptions and Sensitivities Analysis</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">As further described in Note 10, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retirement
Plan and Postretirement Benefits</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> of the Notes to Financial Statements, NVE
has revised the other postretirement benefits discount rate for its 2012 benefit
obligations to 4.09%, as compared to the 2011 benefit obligations rate of
5.09%.&#160;&#160; In determining the other postretirement benefit obligation and related
cost, these assumptions can change with each measurement date, and such changes
could result in material changes to such amounts.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The other postretirement benefits
discount rates for 2012 and 2011 related to the benefit obligations were
determined by identifying a theoretical settlement portfolio of high quality
corporate bonds sufficient to provide for the plans projected benefit payments.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The other postretirement benefits discount rates for 2012
related to the net periodic benefit costs were determined by identifying a
theoretical settlement portfolio of high quality corporate bonds sufficient to
provide for the plans projected benefit payments. However, to determine the
other postretirement benefits discount rates for 2011 and 2010 related to the
net periodic benefit costs, NVE&#8217;s projected benefit payments were matched to
the yield curve derived from a portfolio of over 300 high quality Aa bonds with
yields within the 10th to 90th percentiles of these bond yields.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In selecting an assumed rate of
return on plan assets, NVE considers past performance and economic forecasts
for the types of investments held by the plan. NVE used an assumed rate of
return on plan assets of 7.10% for some plans and 6.15% for others in 2012, and
7.10% and 6.75% in 2011, as disclosed in Note 10, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retirement and Postretirement
Benefits</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> of the Notes to Financial Statements.&#160; Actual return on other
postretirement benefit plan assets increased $2.5 million in 2012 and decreased
$2.0 million in 2011.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following chart reflects the
sensitivities associated with a change in certain actuarial assumptions by the
indicated percentage (dollars in thousands): </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Revenues</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; </font></b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Unbilled Receivables</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Revenues
related to the sale of energy are recorded based on meter reads, which occur on
a systematic basis throughout a month, rather than when the service is rendered
or energy is delivered.&nbsp;&nbsp;At the end of each month, the energy
delivered to the customers from the date of their last meter read to the end of
the month is estimated and the corresponding unbilled revenues are
calculated.&nbsp;&nbsp;These estimates of unbilled sales and revenues are based
on the ratio of billable days versus unbilled days, amount of energy procured
and generated during that month, historical customer class usage patterns, line
loss and the Utilities&#8217; current tariffs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accounts receivable as of
December 31, 2012, include unbilled receivables of $86 million and $50 million
for NPC and SPPC, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accounts receivable as of December
31, 2011, include unbilled receivables of $93 million and $51 million for NPC
and SPPC, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align=center style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">RECENT PRONOUNCEMENTS</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">As of December 31, 2012, there were no recent
accounting pronouncements which would have a significant impact on NVE and the
Utilities financial statements or financial statement disclosure requirements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash used by Investing Activities - </font></i></b><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The increase in cash used by investing activities was

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash used by Financing Activities - </font></i></b><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash used by financing activities increased due to the reduction

reissued to satisfy future equity compensation costs, and higher dividend
payments partially offset by a 2011 settlement payment for the interest rate
swap agreement as discussed in Note 6, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Long Term Debt</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the Notes to

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE&#8217;s cash flows increased in 2011 compared to 2010 due to
a decrease in cash used by investing and financing, offset partially by a
reduction in cash from operating activities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash from Operating Activities - </font></i></b><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The decrease in cash from operating activities was
primarily due to a decrease in net income, overall decrease in rates resulting
from quarterly BTER adjustments and negative DEAA rates implemented in October
2010 to refund prior period over collected balances to customers, as well as a
reduction in revenues from California customers due to the sale of the
California Assets, as discussed in Note 15, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Assets Held for Sale</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the
Notes to Financial Statements.&nbsp;&nbsp;Also contributing to this decrease
was an increase in coal and other inventory, increased incentive compensation
payments for 2010 operating results, refund of customer deposits and an
increase in conservation programs and solar rebates.&nbsp;&nbsp;These decreases
were partially offset by an increase in cash resulting from NPC&#8217;s deferred rate
increase beginning in October 2010 and recovery of deferred conservation
program costs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

primarily due to the receipt of proceeds from the sale of California Assets by
SPPC and telecommunication towers by NPC, as discussed in Note 15, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Assets

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

gas, other operating expenses, capital expenditures and interest.&nbsp;Another

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE and the Utilities attempt to maintain their cash
and cash equivalents in highly liquid investments, such as U.S. Treasury Bills
and bank deposits.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to cash on hand, the Utilities&#8217; may
use their revolving credit facilities in order to meet their liquidity needs.&#160;
Alternatively, depending on the usage of their revolving credit facilities, the
Utilities may issue debt, subject to certain restrictions as discussed in </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Factors
Affecting Liquidity</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Ability to Issue Debt</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, below. </font></p>

<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE has no debt maturities in 2013.&#160;&#160; However, NPC is
required to redeem approximately $98.1 million of its variable rate debt, due
2020, prior to ON Line&#8217;s commercial operation date expected by December 31,
2013, and SPPC&#8217;s $250 million 5.45% General and Refunding Notes, Series Q, will
mature on September 1, 2013.&#160; To meet these long term maturing debt obligations,
the Utilities intend to use a combination of internally generated funds, the
Utilities&#8217; revolving credit facilities, and/or the issuance of long-term debt.&#160;
In 2012, NVE and the Utilities&#8217; credit ratings on their senior secured debt
remained at investment grade (see </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Credit Ratings</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">
below).&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2012, NVE and the Utilities did not experience any
limitations in the credit markets nor do we expect any in 2013.&#160; However,
disruptions in the banking and capital markets not specifically related to NVE
or the Utilities may affect their ability to access funding sources or cause an
increase in the interest rates paid on&nbsp;newly issued debt.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In prior years, NVE and the Utilities required
significant amounts of liquidity due to the magnitude of capital expenditures
needed to support a growing customer base and to support unstable energy
markets.&#160; As NVE and the Utilities have transitioned to slower growth, the
amount of capital expenditures has declined.&#160; NVE and the Utilities&#8217; investment
in generating stations in the past several years and more stable energy markets
have positioned the Utilities to better manage and optimize their resources.&#160;
As a result, NVE and the Utilities anticipate that they will be able to meet
short term operating costs and capital expenditures with internally generated
funds and the use of the Utilities revolving credit facilities.&#160; Furthermore,
with new investments now in rates, the decrease of hedging costs, more current
rate recovery of deferred energy costs, various rate reset mechanisms, federal
tax NOL and a decrease in capital expenditures, NVE and the Utilities expect to
generate free cash flow.&#160; The free cash flow may be used to reduce debt, to
increase the dividend payout and for potential investment opportunities.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">However,
if energy costs rise at a rapid rate and the Utilities do not recover the cost
of fuel, purchased power and operating costs in a timely manner or the
Utilities were to experience a credit rating downgrade resulting in the posting
of collateral as discussed below under </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Gas Supplier Matters</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;"> and </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Financial
Gas Hedges</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">, the amount of liquidity available to the Utilities could be
significantly less.&#160; In order to maintain sufficient liquidity, NVE and the
Utilities may be required to delay capital expenditures, re-finance debt or
issue equity at NVE.&#160; Additionally, if deemed prudent, the Utilities may enter
into hedging transactions in an attempt to mitigate projected or actual rising
energy costs.&#160; Currently, the Utilities are not operating under a PUCN approved
hedging plan.&#160; Hedging transactions may have a material impact on the
Utilities&#8217; cash flows, unless recovered in rates in a timely manner.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of February 21, 2013, NVE has approximately $24.3
million payable of debt service obligations remaining for 2013, which it
intends to pay through dividends from subsidiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;(See </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Factors
Affecting Liquidity-Dividends from Subsidiaries</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> below).&nbsp;&nbsp;On
February 7, 2013, NPC declared a dividend payable to NVE of $50 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE designs operating and capital budgets to control
operating costs and capital expenditures.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to operating
expenses, NVE has continuing commitments for capital expenditures for
construction, improvement and maintenance of facilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Detailed below are NVE&#8217;s Capital Structure, Capital
Requirements, recently completed financing transactions and factors affecting
our ability to obtain debt on favorable terms, including the effect of our
holding company structure and limitation on dividends from the Utilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE&#8217;s

(dollars in thousands):</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; Pension
and Other Postretirement Benefit Plan Matters&#160;&#160; </font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;text-decoration:none;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE has a qualified pension plan and
other postretirement benefits plan which cover substantially all employees of NVE,
NPC and SPPC. The annual net benefit cost for the plans is expected to increase
in 2013 by approximately $3.1 million compared to the 2012 cost of $22.5
million. As of December 31, 2012, the measurement date, the plan was under
funded under the provisions of the Compensation Retirement Benefits Topic of
the FASC. &#160;Refer to Note 10, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retirement Plan and Postretirement Benefits</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">,
of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements. During 2012, NVE funded
a total of $22.1 million to the trusts established for the qualified pension
and postretirement benefit plans. At the present time it is not anticipated
that additional funding will be required in 2013 to meet the minimum funding
level requirements defined by the Pension Protection Act of 2006.&#160; However, NVE
and the Utilities have included in their 2013 assumptions funding levels
similar to the 2012 funding.&#160; The amounts to be contributed in 2013 may change
subject to market conditions.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Factors Affecting Liquidity</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; Ability
to Issue Debt</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160; &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NVE&#8217;s Term Loan contains conditions of borrowing,
events of default, and affirmative and negative covenants.&#160; The Term Loan includes
(i) a financial covenant to maintain a ratio of total consolidated indebtedness
to total consolidated capitalization, determined on the last day of each fiscal
quarter, not to exceed 0.70 to 1.00 and (ii) a fixed charge covenant that
requires NVE not to permit the fixed charge coverage ratio, determined on the
last day of each fiscal quarter, to be less than 1.50 to 1.00.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;Under these covenant restrictions, as of
December 31, 2012, NVE (consolidated) would be allowed to incur up to $3.3
billion of additional indebtedness, which includes the use of the Utilities
revolving credit facilities.&#160; The amount of additional indebtedness allowed
would likely be impacted if there is a change in current market conditions or
material change in our financial condition. &#160;NPC&#8217;s and SPPC&#8217;s </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Ability to
Issue Debt</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;"> sections further discuss the limitations on their ability to
issue debt.</font><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">
&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Effect
of Holding Company Structure</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">As of December 31, 2012, NVE (on a stand-alone basis)
has outstanding debt and other obligations including, but not limited to: $195
million Term Loan due 2014; and $315 million of its unsecured 6.25% Senior
Notes due 2020.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Due
to the holding company structure, NVE&#8217;s right as a common shareholder to
receive assets of any of its direct or indirect subsidiaries upon a
subsidiary&#8217;s liquidation or reorganization is junior to the claims against the
assets of such subsidiary by its creditors.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, NVE&#8217;s debt
obligations are effectively subordinated to all existing and future claims of
the creditors of NPC and SPPC and its other subsidiaries, including trade
creditors, debt holders, secured creditors, taxing authorities and guarantee
holders.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">As of December 31, 2012, NVE, NPC, SPPC and their
subsidiaries had approximately $5.0 billion of debt and other obligations
outstanding, consisting of approximately $3.3 billion of debt at NPC,
approximately $1.2 billion of debt at SPPC and approximately $510 million of
debt at the holding company and other subsidiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although NVE and
the Utilities are parties to agreements that limit the amount of additional
indebtedness they may incur, NVE and the Utilities retain the ability to incur
substantial additional indebtedness and other liabilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Dividends
from Subsidiaries</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Since NVE is a holding company,
substantially all of its cash flow is provided by dividends paid to NVE by NPC
and SPPC on their common stock, all of which is owned by NVE.&nbsp;&nbsp;Since
NPC and SPPC are public utilities, they are subject to regulation by the PUCN,
which may impose limits on investment returns or otherwise impact the amount of
dividends that the Utilities may declare and pay.&nbsp; While the PUCN has in
the past imposed a dividend restriction with respect to NPC and SPPC, as of
December 31, 2012, there were no dividend restrictions imposed on the Utilities
by the PUCN.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;In addition, certain financing agreements entered into
by the Utilities set restrictions on the amount of dividends they may declare
and pay and restrict the circumstances under which such dividends may be
declared and paid.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of the Utilities&#8217; credit rating on
their senior secured debt being rated investment grade by S&amp;P and Moody&#8217;s,
these restrictions are suspended and no longer in effect so long as such debt
remains investment grade by both rating agencies.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to the
restrictions imposed by specific agreements, the Federal Power Act prohibits
the payment of dividends from &#8220;capital accounts.&#8221;&nbsp;&nbsp;Although the
meaning of this provision is unclear, the Utilities believe that the Federal
Power Act restriction, as applied to their particular circumstances, would not
be construed or applied by the FERC to prohibit the payment of dividends for
lawful and legitimate business purposes from current year earnings, or in the
absence of current year earnings, from other/additional paid-in capital
accounts.&nbsp;&nbsp;If, however, the FERC were to interpret this provision
differently, the ability of the Utilities to pay dividends to NVE could be
jeopardized.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; </font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Credit Ratings</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
liquidity of NVE and the Utilities, the cost and availability of borrowing by
the Utilities under their respective credit facilities, the potential exposure
of the Utilities to collateral calls under various contracts and the ability of
the Utilities to acquire fuel and purchased power on favorable terms are all
directly affected by the credit ratings for the companies&#8217; debt.&#160; On February
20, 2013, S&amp;P upgraded NVE&#8217;s corporate credit ratings for NVE, NPC and SPPC
from BB+ to investment grade BBB-.&#160; NPC&#8217;s and SPPC&#8217;s senior secured debt is rated
investment grade by three NRSROs:&#160; Fitch, Moody&#8217;s and S&amp;P.&nbsp;&nbsp;The
senior debt credit ratings are as follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fitch&#8217;s rating outlook is Positive, while Moody&#8217;s and
S&amp;P&#8217;s rating outlook is Stable for NVE, NPC and SPPC.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; A
security rating is not a recommendation to buy, sell or hold
securities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Security ratings are subject to revision and withdrawal
at any time by the assigning rating organization.&#160; Each security rating agency
has its own methodology for assigning ratings, and, accordingly, each rating
should be evaluated in the context of the applicable methodology, independently
of all other ratings.&#160; The rating agencies provide ratings at the request of
the company being rated and charge the company fees for their services.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;
</font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Energy Supplier Matters</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">With respect to NPC&#8217;s and SPPC&#8217;s contracts for
purchased power, NPC and SPPC purchase and sell electricity with counterparties
under the WSPP agreement, an industry standard contract that NPC and SPPC use
as members of the WSPP. &nbsp;The WSPP contract is posted on the WSPP website.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under these contracts, a
material adverse change, which includes a credit rating downgrade of NPC and
SPPC, may allow the counterparty to request adequate financial assurance,
which, if not provided within three business days, could cause a default.
&nbsp;Most contracts and confirmations for purchased power have been modified
or separate agreements have been made to either shorten the normal payment due
date or require payment in advance of delivery in response to requests for
financial assurance.&#160; A default must be declared within 30 days of the event
giving rise to the default becoming known. &nbsp;A default will result in a
termination payment equal to the present value of the net gains and losses for
the entire remaining term of all contracts between the parties aggregated to a
single liquidated amount due within three business days following the date the
notice of termination is received. &nbsp;The mark-to-market value, which is
substantially based on quoted market prices, can be used to roughly approximate
the termination payment and benefit at any point in time. &nbsp;The net
mark-to-market value as of December 31, 2012 for all suppliers continuing to
provide power under a WSPP agreement would approximate a $72 million payment or
obligation to NPC. &nbsp;No amounts would be due to or from SPPC.&nbsp; These
contracts qualify for the normal purchases scope exception under the
Derivatives and Hedging Topic of the FASC, and as such, are not required to be
marked-to-market on the balance sheet.&nbsp; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gas Supplier Matters</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">With respect to the purchase and sale of
natural gas, NPC and SPPC use several types of standard industry
contracts.&nbsp; The natural gas contract terms and conditions are more varied
than the electric contracts.&nbsp; Consequently, some of the contracts contain
language similar to that found in the WSPP agreement and other agreements have
unique provisions dealing with material adverse changes, which primarily means
a credit rating downgrade below investment grade. &nbsp;Most contracts and
confirmations for natural gas purchases have been modified or separate
agreements have been made to either shorten the normal payment due date or
require payment in advance of delivery in response to requests for financial
assurances.&#160; Forward physical gas supplies are purchased under index based
pricing terms and as such do not carry forward mark-to-market
exposure.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gas transmission service is secured under FERC Tariffs
or custom agreements. &nbsp;These service contracts and Tariffs require the
user to establish and maintain creditworthiness to obtain service or otherwise
post cash or a letter of credit to be able to receive service. &nbsp;Service
contracts are subject to FERC approved tariffs, which, under certain
circumstances, require the Utilities to provide collateral to continue
receiving service.&nbsp;&nbsp;NPC has a transmission counterparty for which it
is required to post cash collateral or a letter of credit in the event of
credit rating downgrades.&nbsp;&nbsp; As of December 31, 2012, the maximum
amount of additional collateral NPC would be required to post under these
contracts in the event of credit rating downgrades was approximately $86.7
million.&nbsp; Of this amount, approximately $26 million would be required if
NPC&#8217;s Senior Unsecured ratings (and/or equivalent) are rated below BB (S&amp;P)
or Ba3 (Moody&#8217;s) and an additional amount of approximately $60.7 million would
be required if NPC&#8217;s Senior Secured ratings and Senior Unsecured ratings (or
equivalent), both are downgraded to below investment grade. During the second
quarter of 2012, $17.9 million of letters of credit posted as collateral were
returned from the counterparty to NPC during the period due to NPC&#8217;s unsecured
credit rating equivalent becoming investment grade.&#160; In exchange, the amount of
additional cash collateral that would be required in the event of a credit
rating downgrade increased.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial Gas Hedges </font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Utilities may enter into certain hedging contracts
with various counterparties to manage the gas price risk inherent in purchased
power and fuel contracts.&nbsp;&nbsp;As discussed under NPC&#8217;s and SPPC&#8217;s </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financing
Transactions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, the availability under the Utilities&#8217; revolving credit
facilities is reduced for net negative mark-to-market positions on hedging
contracts with counterparties who are lenders under the revolving credit
facilities provided that the reduction of availability under the revolving
credit facilities shall at no time exceed 50% of the total commitments then in
effect under the credit facilities.&#160; Currently, there are no negative mark-to-market
exposures that would impact borrowings of the Utilities.&#160; If deemed prudent,
the Utilities may still purchase hedging instruments in the event circumstances
occur that may have the potential to increase the cost of fuel and purchased
power.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; Cross Default
Provisions</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">None of the Utilities&#8217; financing agreements contains a
cross-default provision that would result in an event of default by that
Utility upon an event of default by NVE or the other Utility under any of their
respective financing agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain of NVE&#8217;s financing
agreements, however, do contain cross-default provisions that would result in
an event of default by NVE upon an event of default by the Utilities under
their respective financing agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, certain financing
agreements of each of NVE and the Utilities provide for an event of default if
there is a failure under other financing agreements of that entity to meet
payment terms or to observe other covenants that would result in an
acceleration of payments due.&nbsp;&nbsp;Most of these default provisions
(other than ones relating to a failure to pay other indebtedness) provide for a
cure period of 30-60 days from the occurrence of a specified event, during
which time NVE or the Utilities may rectify or correct the situation before it
becomes an event of default.</font></p>








<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><a name=NPCresults></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NEVADA POWER COMPANY</font></b></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><a name="NPCresults_bclEnd"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">RESULTS
OF OPERATIONS</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC recognized net income of $257.7 million</font><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> </font></b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">in 2012 compared to
net income of $132.6 million in 2011 and $185.9 million in 2010.&nbsp;&nbsp;In
2012, NPC paid dividends to NVE of approximately $184.0 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;On
February 7, 2013, NPC declared a dividend of approximately $50 million to NVE.&#160;
Details of NPC&#8217;s operating results are further discussed below.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gross margin is
presented by NPC in order to provide information that management believes aids
the reader in determining how profitable the electric business is at the most
fundamental level.&nbsp;&nbsp;Gross margin, which is a &#8220;non-GAAP financial
measure&#8221; as defined in accordance with SEC rules, provides a measure of income
available to support the other operating expenses of the business and is a key
factor utilized by management in its analysis of its business.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC believes
presenting gross margin allows the reader to assess the impact of NPC&#8217;s
regulatory treatment and its overall regulatory environment on a consistent
basis.&#160; Gross margin, as a percentage of revenue, is primarily impacted by the
fluctuations in electric and natural gas supply costs versus the fixed rates
collected from customers.&#160; While these fluctuating costs impact gross margin as
a percentage of revenue, they only impact gross margin amounts if the costs
cannot be passed through to customers.&#160; Gross margin, which NPC calculates as
operating revenues less energy costs and EEPR costs provides a measure of
income available to support the other operating expenses of NPC.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">EEPR costs are
conservation costs being recovered from ratepayers through EEPR revenues which
were implemented in July 2011 (See Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory Actions,</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> of the
Notes to Financial Statements).&#160;&#160; Costs incurred prior to the implementation of
the EEPR are recovered through general rates and amortized to other operating
expense.&#160; See Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory Actions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the Notes to Financial
Statements for conservation program amount details.&#160; The EEPR mechanism is
designed such that conservation costs are equal to revenues collected and any
over/under collection is deferred as a regulatory asset/liability until rates
are reset.&#160; As a result, amounts related to EEPR do not have an effect on gross
margin, operating income or net income. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">For
reconciliation to operating income, see Note 2, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Segment Information,</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> of
the Notes to Financial Statements.&#160; Gross margin changes are based primarily on
general base rate adjustments (which are required by statute to be filed every
three years).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
