<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gross margin
increased for the year ended December 31, 2012, compared to the same period in
2011, primarily due to the following:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$157.6 million increase primarily due to BTGR revenues as a result of
NPC&#8217;s 2011 GRC effective January 1, 2012;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$39.1 million as a result of increased customer usage, primarily due to
an increase in CDDs, particularly during the second quarter of 2012, as well as
increased usage by certain industrial customers; and </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$5.8 million primarily due to growth.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:1.0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gross margin
decreased for the year ended December 31, 2011, compared to the same period in
2010, primarily due to decreased customer usage as a result of milder weather
and conservation programs.&#160; Partially offsetting this decrease was the
implementation of the EEIR rates, which became effective August 1, 2010 as well
as a slight increase in customer growth.&#160;&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
causes for significant changes in specific lines comprising the results of
operations for the years ended are provided below (dollars in thousands except
for amounts per unit):</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">HDDs and CDDs</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">MWh usage may
be affected by the change in HDDs or CDDs in a given period.&#160; A degree day
indicates how far that day's average temperature departed from 65 degrees Fahrenheit.&#160;
HDDs measure heating energy demand and indicate how far the average temperature
fell below 65 degrees Fahrenheit.&#160; CDDs measure cooling energy demand and
indicate how far the temperature averaged above 65 degrees Fahrenheit.&#160; For
example, if a location had a mean temperature of 60 degrees Fahrenheit on day 1
and 80 degrees Fahrenheit on day 2, there would be 5 HDDs (65 minus 60) and 0
CDDs for day 1.&#160; In contrast, there would be 0 HDDs and 15 CDDs (80 minus 65)
for day 2.&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following
table shows the HDDs and CDDs within NPC&#8217;s service territory:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div align=left><table  cellpadding=0 cellspacing=0 style="border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;">
 <tr>
  <td valign=top width=7% style="padding:0in 5.4pt 0in 5.4pt;">
  <p align=right style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:right;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font></p>
  </td>
 <td valign=top width=93% style="padding:0in 5.4pt 0in 5.4pt;">
  <p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$157.6 million primarily due to

increase in retail revenues was decrease in industrial customers primarily due
to their switch to DOS service.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&nbsp;</font></p>

December 31, 2012, the average number of retail customers increased by 1.3%,
consisting of an increase in residential and commercial customers of 1.4% and 0.7%,
respectively, and a decrease in industrial customers of 1.5%, compared to 2011.&#160;
</font></p>

  <p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:center;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(10.2)%</font></p>
  </td>
 </tr>
</table></div>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Energy Costs
decreased for the year ended December 31, 2012, compared to the same period in
2011, primarily due to a decrease in natural gas prices. Volume increased
primarily due to an increase in CDDs, as discussed previously, as well as, an
increase in demand by certain industrial customers partially offset by an
increase in heat rate option sales. The average cost per MWh decreased
primarily due to lower natural gas prices. In 2012, self-generation, which is
primarily gas fired generating units, satisfied 74% of NPC&#8217;s system load.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div align=left><table  cellpadding=0 cellspacing=0 style="border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;">
 <tr>
  <td valign=top width=11% style="padding:0in 5.4pt 0in 5.4pt;">
  <p align=right style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:right;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font></p>
  </td>
 <td valign=top width=89% style="padding:0in 5.4pt 0in 5.4pt;">
  <p style="margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fuel for
  power generation costs decreased for the year ended December 31, 2012,
  compared to the same period in 2011 primarily due to a $102.7 million
  decrease in the cost of natural gas and a $20.9 million decrease in hedging
  costs, both offset by a $32.8 million increase in volume due to increased
  reliance on internal generation. The average cost per MWh of generated power
  decreased primarily due to a decrease in the cost of natural gas and hedging
  costs.&#160; </font></p>
  </td>
 </tr>
<tr>
  <td valign=top width=11% style="padding:0in 5.4pt 0in 5.4pt;">
  <p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:8.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
  </td>
 <td valign=top width=89% style="padding:0in 5.4pt 0in 5.4pt;">
  <p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
  </td>
 </tr>
<tr>
  <td valign=top width=11% style="padding:0in 5.4pt 0in 5.4pt;">
  <p align=right style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:right;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font></p>
  </td>
 <td valign=top width=89% style="padding:0in 5.4pt 0in 5.4pt;">
  <p style="margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Purchased
  power costs decreased for the year ended December 31, 2012 compared to the
  same period in 2011 primarily due to an $81.6 million decrease in volume
  offset by a $77.1 million increase in the price of purchased power primarily
  due to an increase in the cost of renewable energy.&#160; The decrease in volume
  was primarily due to an increase in the sale of heat rate options which are
  netted in purchased power and the increased reliance on internal generation.
  The average cost per MWh of purchased power increased primarily due to an
  increase in the price and volume of renewable energy
  and the decrease in non-renewable energy coupled with an increase in the
  volume of heat rate option sales.</font></p>
  </td>
 </tr>
</table></div>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Energy Costs
decreased for the year ended December 31, 2011, compared to the same period in
2010, primarily due to a decrease in costs associated with hedging activities
and a slight decrease in natural gas prices.&#160; In 2011, self-generation, which is
primarily gas fired generating units, satisfied 70% of NPC&#8217;s system load.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

  in 2010 primarily due to a $73.1 million decrease in hedging costs as well as
  $7.6 million lower natural gas prices and a $9.2 million decrease in volume.
  The decrease in volume was primarily due to planned outages with the

  <p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Amounts for 2012, 2011 and 2010 include amortization
of deferred energy of $(170.0) million, $(105.6) million and $1.2 million,
respectively; which represent cash refunds to our customers for previous
over-collections, offset by an over-collection of amounts recoverable in rates
of $102.0 million, $89.3 million and $93.6 million, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred energy
represents the difference between actual fuel and purchased power costs
incurred during the period and amounts recoverable through current rates.&#160; To
the extent actual costs exceed amounts recoverable through current rates, the
excess is recognized as a reduction in costs.&#160; Conversely, to the extent actual
costs are less than amounts recoverable through current rates, the difference
is recognized as an increase in costs.&#160; Deferred energy also includes the
current amortization of fuel and purchased power costs previously deferred.&#160;
Reference Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory Actions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the Notes to Financial
Statements for further detail of deferred energy balances. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Energy efficiency
program costs increased for the year ended December 31, 2012 compared to the
same period in 2011 due to the implementation of EEPR base rates in July 2011
and amortization rates effective October 2011.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="EHW5d534d62_baff_4154_af92_bb00fa2c4816"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW5d534d62_baff_4154_af92_bb00fa2c4816_"></a>Energy efficiency program
costs are conservation costs being recovered from ratepayers through EEPR
revenues which were implemented in July 2011 for base rates and in October 2011
for amortization rates (See Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory Actions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the Notes to
Financial Statements).&#160; Costs incurred prior to the implementation of the EEPR
rates are recovered through the general rates and amortized to other operating
expense discussed below.&#160; The EEPR mechanism is designed such that conservation
costs are equal to revenues collected and any over/under collection is deferred
as a regulatory asset/liability until rates are reset.&#160; As a result, amounts
related to EEPR do not have an effect on gross margin, operating income or net
income.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other operating expense increased for the year ended
December 31, 2012, compared to the same period in 2011, primarily due to the
following:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

amortization costs;<a name="EHWc4d63939_87bc_4d61_9459_6045c9980832"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$2.3 million decrease in lease expense;<a name="EHW54c9fe48_ef6c_43fb_9e53_a523ab69491a"></a><a name="EHWc4d63939_87bc_4d61_9459_6045c9980832_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$1.5 million decrease in
telecommunications expenses;<a name="EHW760c04ee_32a2_4d64_bc11_b262484b32d4"></a><a name="EHW54c9fe48_ef6c_43fb_9e53_a523ab69491a_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$1.1 million decrease in transmission
and distribution costs; and <a name="EHWccbb6b7d_67b2_4c09_8723_97e5a176b551"></a><a name="EHW760c04ee_32a2_4d64_bc11_b262484b32d4_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$1.0 million decrease in pension and
benefit costs.<a name="EHW8a4bd024_efe0_4ad2_9f5b_7c29908df142"></a><a name="EHWccbb6b7d_67b2_4c09_8723_97e5a176b551_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><a name="EHW4f40cd14_3370_4553_9f3d_23c9c85a92e1"></a><font color=red face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW4f40cd14_3370_4553_9f3d_23c9c85a92e1_"></a><a name="EHW8a4bd024_efe0_4ad2_9f5b_7c29908df142_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other operating expense decreased slightly for the year
ended December 31, 2011, compared to the same period in 2010, primarily due to
the following:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$3.4 million decrease in overall
generating expenses;<a name="EHW96595d57_5405_4fd5_97cf_de19da4d22a1"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$2.5 million decrease in employee
pension and benefit cost;<a name="EHW9773cc83_cf27_487f_a37f_cfb880230727"></a><a name="EHW96595d57_5405_4fd5_97cf_de19da4d22a1_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$2.2 million decrease in consulting
fees; and<a name="EHWe26f6226_a5ba_48fb_b994_d31b1e0ec3b8"></a><a name="EHW9773cc83_cf27_487f_a37f_cfb880230727_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$2.2 million in higher capitalization
of administrative and general costs for the Harry Allen Generating Station. <a name="EHWaf199235_7c6a_49ea_bb2c_b8d7293d24db"></a><a name="EHWe26f6226_a5ba_48fb_b994_d31b1e0ec3b8_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:56.25pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="EHWaf199235_7c6a_49ea_bb2c_b8d7293d24db_"></a><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The decrease in
other operating expense was partially offset by a $9.5 million increase in
stock compensation costs.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=red face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Maintenance expense increased for the year ended December
31, 2012, compared to the same period in 2011, primarily due to the following:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">the absence of an $8 million reduction in maintenance expense recorded
in 2011 as a result of the final calculation of a terminated amount for a
long-term service agreement for the Higgins Generating Station which was
previously expensed in 2010;<a name="EHW5125c1db_8d19_45f5_a5db_cee6d046ba8c"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$11.8 million increase primarily due to planned maintenance and outages
at the Lenzie, Silverhawk, Harry Allen and Higgins Generating Stations; and<a name="EHW57d60ce8_e7a0_45c1_897a_e61a9c5e5e2e"></a><a name="EHW5125c1db_8d19_45f5_a5db_cee6d046ba8c_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$2.8 million cancellation fee for the Silverhawk Generating Station
long-term service agreement.&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW953e3aca_9979_4f48_8d56_0b3ba3a3f783"></a><a name="EHW57d60ce8_e7a0_45c1_897a_e61a9c5e5e2e_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:74.25pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="EHW953e3aca_9979_4f48_8d56_0b3ba3a3f783_"></a><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The increase was partially offset by a $12.9 million
decrease in planned maintenance and outages at the Reid Gardner, Navajo and
Clark Generating Stations. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=red face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Maintenance expense decreased for the year ended December
31, 2011, compared to the same period in 2010, primarily due to the following:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$16 million impact of an accrual in
2010 for estimated payments for the termination of the long-term service
agreement for the Higgins Generating Station, which was reversed in the third
quarter of 2011 upon final calculation of the termination amount; and<a name="EHW3053bca0_b379_4292_9754_085048e70083"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$8.3 million decrease in planned
maintenance and outages at the Higgins, Lenzie and Silverhawk Generating
Stations. <a name="EHW5d3ecc90_77f5_4185_b183_3adc7af40cde"></a><a name="EHW3053bca0_b379_4292_9754_085048e70083_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:74.25pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="EHW5d3ecc90_77f5_4185_b183_3adc7af40cde_"></a><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">This decrease was partially offset by a $15.6 million increase
in planned maintenance and outages at the Reid Gardner, Navajo, Clark and Harry
Allen Generating Stations. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Depreciation
and amortization increased for the year ended December 31, 2012, compared to
2011, primarily due to increased depreciation of $7.8 million resulting from
the expansion at Harry Allen Generating Station placed in service in May 2011.&#160;
Also contributing to the increase was a change in depreciation rates, as of
January 1, 2012, resulting from a recent depreciation study, additional regulatory
assets amortizations, and other general increases in plant-in-service.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Depreciation and
amortization increased for the year ended December 31, 2011, compared to 2010,
primarily due to increased depreciation of $14.9 million resulting from the
expansion at Harry Allen Generating Station placed in service in May 2011.&#160;
Also contributing to the increase were other general increases in
plant-in-service.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest expense decreased for the year ended December 31, 2012, compared
to the same period in 2011 primarily due to approximately $10.8 million in
decreased net interest costs from various re-financings and redemptions, partially
offset by variable rate debt fluctuations and a $1.6 million decrease in
AFUDC-debt.&#160; See Note 6, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Long-Term Debt</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the Notes to Financial
Statements for additional information regarding long-term debt.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest expense
increased for the year ended December 31, 2011, compared to the same period in
2010 primarily due to a $13.0 million decrease in AFUDC primarily due to the
completion of the Harry Allen Generating Station in May 2011.&#160; The increase was
partially offset by an $8.6 million decrease in net interest costs as a result
of various re-financings, redemptions and a lower revolving credit facility
balance.&#160; See Note 6, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Long-Term Debt</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the Notes to Financial
Statements for additional information regarding long-term debt.&#160; </font></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><a name=NPCanalysis></a><b><font face="Times New Roman Bold" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;text-transform:uppercase;">Analysis of Cash Flows</font></b></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><a name="NPCanalysis_bclEnd"></a><font face="Times New Roman Bold" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;text-transform:uppercase;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC&#8217;s cash flows
increased during the year ended December 31, 2012, compared to the same period
in 2011, due to an increase in cash from operating and a reduction in cash used
by investing activities, offset partially by an increase in cash used by
financing activities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash from
Operating Activities - </font></i></b><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
increase in cash from operating activities was primarily due to increased revenues
resulting primarily due to increase BTGR rates as a result of NPC&#8217;s 2011 GRC
and increased customer usage.&#160; Also contributing to the increase were over
collections of EEPR, reduced funding of the retirement plan, a reduction in
spend for conservation programs and refunds of customer deposits in 2011.&#160;
These increases were partially offset by quarterly BTER adjustments and
negative DEAA rates to refund prior period over collected balances and
expiration of rates to collect the deferred rate increase from NPC&#8217;s 2008 GRC.&#160;
</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash used by
Investing Activities - </font></i></b><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
decrease in cash used by investing activities was primarily due to the
completion of construction at the Harry Allen Generating Station in May 2011
partially offset by proceeds from the sale of certain telecommunication towers
in 2011 and CIAC received under the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of
2009, related to the NV Energize project.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash used by
Financing Activities -</font></i></b><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">
Cash used by financing activities increased primarily due to a reduction in capital
contribution from NVE, an increase in dividends paid to NVE and a reduction in
cash from the issuance of debt, partially offset by a 2011 settlement payment
for the interest rate swap agreement as discussed in Note 6, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Long Term Debt</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">,
of the Notes to Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC&#8217;s cash flows
decreased during in 2011 compared to 2010 due to a decrease in cash from
operating and financing activities, offset partially by a reduction in cash
used by investing activities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash from
Operating Activities - </font></i></b><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
decrease in cash from operating activities was primarily due to a decrease in
net income, an overall decrease in rates resulting from quarterly BTER
adjustments and negative DEAA rates implemented in October 2010 to refund prior
period over collected balances to customers, increased incentive compensation
payments for the 2010 operating results, an increase in coal and other
inventory, refunds of customer deposits and an increase in conservation
programs and solar rebates.&nbsp;&nbsp;These decreases were partially offset by
an increase in cash resulting from NPC&#8217;s deferred rate increase beginning in
October 2010, the recovery of deferred conservation program costs and lower
funding for pension plans.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash used by
Investing Activities - </font></i></b><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
decrease in cash used by investing activities was primarily due to proceeds
from the sale of certain telecommunication towers as discussed in Note 15, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Assets
Held for Sale</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the Notes to Financial Statements and CIAC received under
the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009, as a part of the NV
Energize project.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash used by
Financing Activities -</font></i></b><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">
Cash used by financing activities decreased primarily due to a reduction in
draws on NPC&#8217;s revolving credit facility, the redemption of NPC&#8217;s $350 million
aggregate principal amount of 8.25%, Series A, General and </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>

contribution from NVE.</font></p>








<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><a name=NPCliquidity></a><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">LIQUIDITY AND CAPITAL RESOURCES</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><a name="NPCliquidity_bclEnd"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Overall
Liquidity</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC&#8217;s primary source of operating cash flows is electric revenues,
including the recovery of previously deferred energy
costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Significant uses of cash flows from operations include the
purchase of electricity and natural gas, other operating expenses, capital
expenditures and the payment of interest on NPC&#8217;s outstanding
indebtedness.&nbsp;&nbsp;Another significant use of cash is the refunding of
previously over-collected amounts from customers.&#160; See Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory
Actions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the Notes to Financial Statements for more details of
over-collected balances.&#160; Operating cash flows can be significantly influenced
by factors such as weather, regulatory outcome, and economic conditions.&#160;
Available liquidity as of December 31, 2012 was as follows (in millions):</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC attempts to maintain its cash and cash equivalents
in highly liquid investments, such as U.S. Treasury Bills and bank
deposits.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to cash on hand, NPC may use its revolving
credit facility in order to meet its liquidity needs.&#160; Alternatively, depending
on the usage of the revolving credit facility, NPC may issue debt, subject to
certain restrictions as discussed in </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Factors Affecting Liquidity</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Ability
to Issue Debt</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, below.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC is required to redeem approximately $98.1 million
of its variable rate debt, due 2020, prior to ON Line&#8217;s commercial operation
date, expected no later than December 31, 2013.&#160; To meet this maturing debt
obligation, NPC intends to use a combination of internally generated funds, its
revolving credit facility, and/or the issuance of long-term debt.&#160; As of
February 21, 2013, NPC has no borrowings on its revolving credit facility, not
including letters of credit.&#160; In 2012, NPC&#8217;s credit ratings on its senior
secured debt remained at investment grade (see </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Credit Ratings</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">
below).&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2012, NPC did not experience any limitations in the
credit markets, nor does NPC expect any significant limitations in 2013.&#160;
However, disruptions in the banking and capital markets not specifically
related to NPC may affect its ability to access funding sources or cause an
increase in the interest rates paid on&nbsp;newly issued debt.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In prior years, NPC required significant amounts of
liquidity due to the magnitude of capital expenditures needed to support a
growing customer base and to support unstable energy markets.&#160; As NPC
transitioned to slower growth, the amount of capital expenditures has
declined.&#160; NPC&#8217;s investment in generating stations in the past several years
and more stable energy markets have positioned NPC to better manage and
optimize its resources.&#160; As a result, NPC anticipates that it will be able to
meet short term operating costs and capital expenditures with internally
generated funds and the use of its revolving credit facilities.&#160; Furthermore,
with new investments now in rates, the decrease of hedging costs, more current
rate recovery of deferred energy costs, various rate reset mechanisms, federal
tax NOL and a decrease in capital expenditures, NPC expects to generate free
cash flow.&#160; The free cash flow may be used to reduce debt, to increase dividend
payout and for potential investment opportunities.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">However,
if energy costs rise at a rapid rate and NPC does not recover the cost of fuel
and purchased power in a timely manner, if operating costs are not recovered in
a timely manner or NPC were to experience a credit rating downgrade resulting
in the posting of collateral as discussed below under </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Gas Supplier Matters</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">
and </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Financial Gas Hedges, </font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">the amount of liquidity available to NPC could
be significantly less.&#160; In order to maintain sufficient liquidity, NPC may be
required to further delay capital expenditures, refinance debt or obtain
funding through an equity issuance by NVE.&#160; Additionally, if deemed prudent,
NPC may enter into hedging transactions in an attempt to mitigate projected or
actual rising energy costs.&#160; Currently, NPC is not operating under a PUCN
approved hedging plan.&#160; Hedging transactions may have a material impact on
NPC&#8217;s cash flows, unless recovered in rates in a timely manner.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2012, NPC paid dividends to NVE of $184.0 million.&#160;
On February 7, 2013, NPC declared a dividend payable to NVE of $50 million.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC designs operating and
capital budgets to control operating costs and capital
expenditures.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to operating expenses, NPC has continuing
commitments for capital expenditures for construction, improvement and
maintenance of facilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Detailed
below are NPC&#8217;s </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Capital Structure</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Capital Requirements</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, recently
completed </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financing Transactions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> and </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Factors Affecting Liquidity</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">,
including our ability to obtain debt on favorable terms.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Capital Requirements</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Construction
Expenditures</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NPC&#8217;s
cash requirement for construction expenditures for 2013 is projected to be
$283.1 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;NPC&#8217;s cash requirements for construction
expenditures for 2013 through 2017 are projected to be $1.2
billion.&nbsp;&nbsp;Gross construction expenditures, including AFUDC-debt, net
salvage and CIAC for the years ended 2012, 2011, and 2010 were $287.6 million,
$475.1 million, and $499.4 million, respectively. Net cash requirements to fund
construction for the years ended 2012, 2011 and 2010 were $245.2 million, $387.5
million, and $452.9 million, respectively.&#160; To fund future capital projects NPC
may meet such financial obligations with a combination of internally generated
funds, the use of its revolving credit facilities, the issuance of long-term
debt, and if necessary, capital contributions from NVE.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; Contractual
Obligations</font></i></b></p>

contractual obligations, as of December 31, 2012, that NPC expects to satisfy
through a combination of internally generated cash and, as necessary, through
the issuance of short-term and long-term debt.&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain contracts
contain variable factors which required NPC to estimate the obligation
depending on the final variable amount.&nbsp;&nbsp;Actual amounts could

expenditures described above, except for major capital projects for which NPC

the FASC, all of which is classified as non-current.&nbsp;&nbsp;NPC is unable

relevant tax authorities; consequently, none of the uncertain tax liability is

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.55in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">(4)</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:46.1pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:10.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; Pension and Other Postretirement Benefit Plan
Matters&#160;&#160; </font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE has a qualified pension plan and
other postretirement benefits plan which cover substantially all employees of NVE,
NPC and SPPC. The annual net benefit cost for the plans is expected to increase
in 2013 by approximately $3.1 million compared to the 2012 cost of $22.5
million. As of December 31, 2012, the measurement date, the plan was under
funded under the provisions of the Compensation Retirement Benefits Topic of
the FASC. &#160;Refer to Note 10, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retirement Plan and Postretirement Benefits</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">,
of the Notes to Financial Statements. During 2012, NVE funded a total of $22.1
million to the trusts established for the qualified pension and postretirement
benefit plans. At the present time it is not anticipated that additional
funding will be required in 2013 to meet the minimum funding level requirements
defined by the Pension Protection Act of 2006.&#160; However, NVE and the Utilities
have included in their 2013 assumptions funding levels similar to the 2012
funding.&#160; The amounts to be contributed in 2013 may change subject to market
conditions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Financing Transactions</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; General and
Refunding Mortgage Notes, Series I</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In April 2012, NPC used $120 million from its
revolving credit facility along with $10 million cash on hand to pay for the
maturity of its 6.5% General and Refunding Mortgage Notes, Series I, in an
aggregate principal amount of $130 million.&#160; NPC did not have any other debt
maturities in 2012; however, NPC is
required to redeem approximately $98.1 million of its variable rate debt, due
2020, prior to ON Line&#8217;s commercial operation date, expected no later than
December 31, 2013.<a name="EHW60ca72e0_3e59_4474_a1b1_41b371dc9c77"></a>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW60ca72e0_3e59_4474_a1b1_41b371dc9c77_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; $500 Million Revolving Credit
Facility</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In March
2012, NPC terminated its $600 million secured revolving credit facility which
would have expired in April 2013 and replaced it with a $500 million secured
revolving credit facility, for which borrowings mature in 2017.&#160; The fees on
the $500 million revolving credit facility for the unused portion and on the
amounts borrowed have decreased from the prior facility reflecting current
market conditions.&#160; The Administrative Agent for the facility remains Wells Fargo
Bank, N.A., and amounts due under the NPC Credit Agreement are collateralized
by NPC&#8217;s general and refunding mortgage bonds.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
rate for outstanding loans under the revolving credit facility will be at
either an applicable base rate (defined as the highest of the Prime Rate, the
Federal Funds Rate plus 0.5% and the LIBOR Base Rate plus 1.0%) plus a margin,
or a LIBOR rate plus a margin.&#160; The margin varies based upon NPC&#8217;s credit rating
by S&amp;P and Moody&#8217;s.&#160; Currently, NPC&#8217;s applicable base rate margin is 0.25%
and the LIBOR rate margin is 1.25 %.&#160; The rate for outstanding letters of
credit will be at the LIBOR rate margin plus a fee for the issuing bank.&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
$500 million revolving credit facility contains a provision which reduces the
availability under the credit facility by the negative mark-to-market exposure
for hedging transactions with credit facility lenders or their energy trading
affiliates.&#160; The reduction in availability limits the amount that NPC can
borrow or use for letters of credit and would require that NPC prepay any
amount in excess of that limitation.&#160; The amount of the reduction is calculated
by NPC on a monthly basis, and after calculating such reduction, the NPC Credit
Agreement provides that the reduction in availability under the revolving
credit facility to NPC shall in no event exceed 50% of the total commitments
then in effect under the revolving credit facility.&#160; Currently, there are no
negative mark-to-market exposures that would impact borrowings.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The NPC Credit Agreement contains one financial maintenance covenant
that requires NPC to maintain a ratio of consolidated indebtedness to
consolidated capital, determined as of the last day of each fiscal quarter, not
to exceed 0.68 to 1.&#160; In the event that NPC did not meet the financial
maintenance covenant or there is a different event of default, the NPC Credit
Agreement would restrict dividends to NVE.&#160; Moreover, so long as NPC&#8217;s senior
secured debt remains rated investment grade by S&amp;P and Moody&#8217;s (in each
case, with a stable or better outlook), a representation concerning no material
adverse change in NPC&#8217;s business, assets, property or financial condition would
not be a condition to the availability of credit under the facility.&#160; In the
event that NPC&#8217;s senior secured debt rating were rated below investment grade
by either S&amp;P or Moody&#8217;s, or investment grade by either S&amp;P or </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><a name=bcl_connect_prev></a><!-- Do not modify before this point! !--><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Moody&#8217;s but with a negative outlook, a representation

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The NPC Credit
Agreement provides for an event of default if there is a failure under NPC&#8217;s
other financing agreements to meet certain payment terms or to observe other
covenants that would result in an acceleration of payments due.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The NPC Credit
Agreement places certain restrictions on debt incurrence, liens and
dividends.&nbsp;&nbsp;These restrictions are discussed in Note 8, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Debt
Covenant and Other Restrictions, </font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">of the Notes to Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Factors Affecting
Liquidity</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Ability to Issue
Debt</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;NPC&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.55in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC&#8217;s
ability to issue debt is impacted by certain factors such as financing
authority from the PUCN, financial covenants in its financing agreements and
revolving credit facility agreements, and the terms of NVE&#8217;s Term Loan.&#160; As of
December 31, 2012, the most restrictive of the factors below is the PUCN
authority.&nbsp; As such, NPC may issue up to $725</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> </font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">million
in long-term debt, in addition to the use of its existing credit
facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, depending on NVE&#8217;s or SPPC&#8217;s issuance of
long-term debt or the use of the Utilities&#8217; revolving credit facilities, the
PUCN authority may not remain the most restrictive factor.&nbsp;&nbsp;The
factors affecting NPC&#8217;s ability to issue debt are further detailed below:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.55in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:62.6pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">a.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Financing
authority from the PUCN - As of December 31, 2012, NPC has financing authority
from the PUCN for the period ending December 31, 2013, consisting of authority:
(1) to issue additional long-term debt securities of up to $725 million; (2) to
refinance up to approximately $322.5 million of long-term debt securities; and
(3) ongoing authority to maintain a revolving credit facility of up to $1.3
billion.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:62.6pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:62.6pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">b.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Financial
covenants within NPC&#8217;s financing agreements &#8211; Under its $500 million revolving
credit facility, NPC must maintain a ratio of consolidated indebtedness to
consolidated capital, determined as of the last day of each fiscal quarter, not
to exceed 0.68 to 1.&#160; Based on December 31, 2012 financial statements, NPC was
in compliance with this covenant and could incur up to $2.8</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> </font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">billion
of additional indebtedness. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:62.6pt;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:62.6pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; All
other financial covenants contained in NPC&#8217;s financing agreements are currently
suspended; as NPC&#8217;s senior secured debt is rated investment grade.&#160; However, if
NPC&#8217;s senior secured debt ratings fall below investment grade by either Moody&#8217;s
or S&amp;P, NPC would again be subject to the limitations under these
additional covenants; and </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:62.6pt;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:62.6pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">c.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Financial
covenants within NVE&#8217;s Term Loan &#8211; As discussed in NVE&#8217;s </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Ability to Issue
Debt</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, NPC is also subject to NVE&#8217;s cap on additional consolidated
indebtedness of $3.3 billion.</font><sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;
&nbsp;</font></sup></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.55in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; Ability to Issue General and Refunding Mortgage
Securities</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">To the extent that
NPC has the ability to issue debt under the most restrictive covenants in its
financing agreements and has financing authority to do so from the PUCN, NPC&#8217;s
ability to issue secured debt is still limited by the amount of bondable
property or retired bonds that can be used to issue debt under NPC&#8217;s Indenture.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC&#8217;s Indenture creates a lien on
substantially all of NPC&#8217;s properties in Nevada.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31,
2012, $3.8 billion of NPC&#8217;s General and Refunding Mortgage Securities were
outstanding.&nbsp;&nbsp;NPC had the capacity to issue $1.6 billion of
additional General and Refunding Mortgage Securities as of December 31,
2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;That amount is determined on the basis of:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">1.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; 70%
of net utility property additions; and/or</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">2.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; The
principal amount of retired General and Refunding Mortgage Securities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="display:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Property additions include
plant-in-service and specific assets in CWIP.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount of bond
capacity listed above does not include eligible property in CWIP.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC also has the ability to
release property from the lien of NPC&#8217;s Indenture on the basis of net property
additions, cash and/or retired bonds.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the extent NPC releases
property from the lien of NPC&#8217;s Indenture, it will reduce the amount of
securities issuable under the Indenture.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:10.0pt;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Credit Ratings</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:10.0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The liquidity of NPC, the cost and availability of borrowing by NPC under
its credit facility, the potential exposure of NPC to collateral calls under
various contracts and the ability of NPC to acquire fuel and purchased power on
favorable terms are all directly affected by the credit rating for NPC&#8217;s debt.&#160;
On February 20, 2013, S&amp;P upgraded NPC&#8217;s corporate credit rating from BB+
to investment grade BBB-.&#160; NPC&#8217;s senior secured debt is rated investment grade
by three NRSROs:&#160; Fitch, Moody&#8217;s and S&amp;P.&nbsp;&nbsp;The senior secured
debt credit ratings are as follows:</font></p>
