<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fitch&#8217;s rating outlook is Positive, while Moody&#8217;s and
S&amp;P&#8217;s rating outlook for NPC is Stable.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; A
security rating is not a recommendation to buy, sell or hold
securities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Security ratings are subject to revision and withdrawal
at any time by the assigning rating organization.&#160; Each security rating agency
has its own methodology for assigning ratings, and accordingly, each rating
should be evaluated in the context of the applicable methodology, independently
of all other ratings.&#160; The rating agencies provide ratings at the request of
the company being rated and charge the company fees for their services.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&nbsp;</font></i></b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; </font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Energy Supplier Matters</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">With respect to NPC&#8217;s contracts for
purchased power, NPC purchases and sells electricity with counterparties under
the WSPP agreement, an industry standard contract that NPC uses as
a&nbsp;member of the WSPP. &nbsp;The WSPP contract is posted on the WSPP
website.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under these contracts, a material adverse change,
which includes a credit rating downgrade, in NPC may allow the counterparty to
request adequate financial assurance, which, if not provided within three
business days, could cause a default. &nbsp;Most contracts and confirmations
for purchased power have been modified or separate agreements have been made to
either shorten the normal payment due date or require payment in advance of
delivery in response to requests for financial assurance.&#160; A default must be
declared within 30 days of the event giving rise to the default becoming known.
&nbsp;A default will result in a termination payment equal to the present value
of the net gains and losses for the entire remaining term of all contracts
between the parties aggregated to a single liquidated amount due within three
business days following the date the notice of termination is received.
&nbsp;The mark-to-market value, which is substantially based on quoted market
prices, can be used to roughly approximate the termination payment and benefit
at any point in time. &nbsp;The net mark-to-market value as of December 31,
2012 for all suppliers continuing to provide power under a WSPP agreement would
approximate a $72 million payment or obligation to NPC.&nbsp; These contracts
qualify for the normal purchases scope exception under the Derivatives and
Hedging Topic of the FASC, and as such, are not required to be marked-to-market
on the balance sheet.&nbsp; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gas Supplier Matters</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">With respect to the purchase and sale of natural gas,
NPC uses several types of standard industry contracts.&nbsp; The natural gas
contract terms and conditions are more varied than the electric
contracts.&nbsp; Consequently, some of the contracts contain language similar
to that found in the WSPP agreement and other agreements have unique provisions
dealing with material adverse changes, which primarily means a credit rating
downgrade below investment grade. &nbsp;Most contracts and confirmations for
natural gas purchases have been modified or separate agreements have been made
to either shorten the normal payment due date or require payment in advance of
delivery in response to requests for financial assurances.&#160; Forward physical
gas supplies are purchased under index based pricing terms and as such do not
carry forward mark-to-market exposure.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gas transmission service is secured under FERC Tariffs
or custom agreements. &nbsp;These service contracts and Tariffs require the
user to establish and maintain creditworthiness to obtain service or otherwise
post cash or a letter of credit to be able to receive </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name=bcl_connect_prev></a><!-- Do not modify before this point! !--><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">service.
&nbsp;Service contracts are subject to FERC approved Tariffs, which, under
certain circumstances, require the Utilities to provide collateral to continue
receiving service.&nbsp;&nbsp;NPC has a transmission counterparty for which it
is required to post cash collateral or a letter of credit in the event of
credit rating downgrades.&nbsp;&nbsp; As of December 31, 2012, the maximum
amount of additional collateral NPC would be required to post under these
contracts in the event of credit rating downgrades was approximately $86.7
million.&nbsp; Of this amount, approximately $26 million would be required if
NPC&#8217;s Senior Unsecured ratings (and/or equivalent) are rated below BB (S&amp;P)
or Ba3 (Moody&#8217;s) and an additional amount of approximately $60.7 million would
be required if NPC&#8217;s Senior Unsecured ratings and Senior Secured ratings (or
equivalent), both are downgraded to below investment grade. During the second
quarter of 2012, $17.9 million of letters of credit posted as collateral were
returned from the counterparty to NPC during the period due to NPC&#8217;s unsecured
credit rating equivalent becoming investment grade.&#160; In exchange, the amount of
additional cash collateral that would be required in the event of a credit
rating downgrade increased.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial Gas Hedges </font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC may enter into certain hedging contracts with
various counterparties to manage the gas price risk inherent in purchased power
and fuel contracts.&nbsp;&nbsp;As discussed under NPC&#8217;s </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financing
Transactions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, the availability under NPC&#8217;s revolving credit facility is
reduced by the amount of net negative mark-to-market positions on hedging
contracts with counterparties who are lenders to the revolving credit facility,
provided that the reduction in availability under the revolving credit facility
shall at no time exceed 50% of the total commitments then in effect under the
revolving credit facility.&#160; Currently, there are no negative mark-to-market
exposures that would impact borrowings of NPC.&#160; If deemed prudent, NPC may
still purchase hedging instruments in the event circumstances occur that may
have the potential to increase the cost of fuel and purchased power.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; Cross Default Provisions</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">None of the financing agreements of NPC
contains a cross-default provision that would result in an event of default by
NPC upon an event of default by NVE or SPPC under any of its financing
agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, certain financing agreements of NPC provide
for an event of default if there is a failure under other financing agreements
of NPC to meet payment terms or to observe other covenants that would result in
an acceleration of payments due.&nbsp;&nbsp;Most of these default provisions
(other than ones relating to a failure to pay such other indebtedness when due)
provide for a cure period of 30-60 days from the occurrence of a specified
event during which time NPC may rectify or correct the situation before it
becomes an event of default.</font></p>








<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><a name=SPPCresults></a><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;text-transform:uppercase;">Sierra Pacific Power
Company</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><a name="SPPCresults_bclEnd"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &nbsp;</font></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">RESULTS
OF OPERATIONS</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SPPC recognized net income of $84.4 million for the year ended December
31, 2012, compared to net income of $59.9 million in 2011 and a net income of $72.4
million in 2010.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2012, SPPC paid dividends to NVE of
approximately $20 million.&#160; Details of SPPC&#8217;s operating results are further
discussed below.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gross margin is
presented by SPPC in order to provide information that management believes aids
the reader in determining how profitable the electric business is at the most
fundamental level.&#160; Gross margin, which is a &#8220;non-GAAP financial measure&#8221; as
defined in accordance with SEC rules, provides a measure of income available to
support the other operating expenses of the business and is a key factor
utilized by management in its analysis of its business.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SPPC believes
presenting gross margin allows the reader to assess the impact of SPPC&#8217;s
regulatory treatment and its overall regulatory environment on a consistent
basis.&#160; Gross margin, as a percentage of revenue, is primarily impacted by the
fluctuations in regulated electric and natural gas supply costs versus the
fixed rates collected from customers.&#160; While these fluctuating costs impact
gross margin as a percentage of revenue, they only impact gross margin amounts
if the costs cannot be passed through to customers.&#160; Gross margin, which SPPC
calculates as operating revenues less energy costs and EEPR costs, provides a
measure of income available to support the other operating expenses of SPPC.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">EEPR costs are
conservation costs being recovered from ratepayers through EEPR revenues which
were implemented in July 2011 (See Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory Actions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the
Notes to Financial Statements).&#160;&#160; Costs incurred prior to the implementation of
the EEPR are recovered through general rates and amortized to other operating
expense.&#160; See Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory Actions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the Notes to Financial
Statements for conservation program amount details.&#160; The EEPR mechanism is
designed such that conservation costs are equal to revenues collected and any
over/under collection is deferred as a regulatory asset/liability until rates
are reset.&#160; As a result, amounts related to EEPR do not have an effect on gross
margin, operating income or net income. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Electric gross
margin increased for the year ended December 31, 2012, compared to the same
period in 2011, primarily due to a $7.8 increase in customer usage and a $4.4
million increase as a result of customer growth.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Electric gross
margin decreased for the year ended December 31, 2011, compared to the same
period in 2010, primarily due to the sale of the California Assets, as
discussed in Note 15, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Assets Held for Sale, </font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">of the Notes to Financial
Statements, partially offset by a related five year power sale agreement
entered into as a condition to the sale of the assets.&#160; Further contributing to
the decrease was increased margin in 2010 as a result of an adjustment for
California revenues upon a final filing in 2010 with the CPUC in regards to the
Rate Reduction Certificates Series 1991-1.&#160; In addition, reduced DOS impact
fees in 2011 contributed to the decrease in margin.&#160; Partially offsetting this
decrease were increased rates, particularly among commercial and industrial
customer classes, as a result of SPPC&#8217;s GRC effective January 1, 2011, as well
as increased customer usage among residential and industrial classes primarily
as a result of weather.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gas gross margin
decreased for the year ended December 31, 2012, compared to the same period in
2011, primarily due to decreased customer usage as a result of warmer weather.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gas gross margin
increased for the year ended December 31, 2011, as compared to the same period
in 2010, primarily due to increased customer usage.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
causes for significant changes in specific lines comprising the results of
operations for the years ended are provided below (dollars in thousands except
for amounts per unit):</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">HDDs and CDDs</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">MWh usage may
be affected by the change in HDDs or CDDs in a given period.&#160; A degree day
indicates how far that day's average temperature departed from 65 degrees Fahrenheit.&#160;
HDDs measure heating energy demand and indicate how far the average temperature
fell below 65 degrees Fahrenheit.&#160; CDDs measure cooling energy demand and
indicate how far the temperature averaged above 65 degrees Fahrenheit. &#160;For
example, if a location had a mean temperature of 60 degrees Fahrenheit on day 1
and 80 degrees Fahrenheit on day 2, there would be 5 HDDs (65 minus 60) and 0
CDDs for day 1.&#160; In contrast, there would be 0 HDDs and 15 CDDs (80 minus 65)
for day 2.&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font><font style="mso-no-proof:yes;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;">77</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:2.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SPPC&#8217;s retail
gas revenues decreased for the year ended December 31, 2012, compared to the
same period in 2011, primarily due to a $36.5 million decrease in retail rates
as a result of SPPC&#8217;s annual Deferred Energy cases, effective October 1, 2012 and
2011, and various BTER and DEAA quarterly updates (see Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory
Actions,</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> of the Notes to Financial Statements). Retail revenues further
decreased due $9.4 million related to a decrease in usage primarily due to a
decrease in HDDs, as shown in the table above. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SPPC&#8217;s retail
gas revenues decreased for the year ended December 31, 2011, compared to the
same period in 2010, primarily due to a $34.3 million decrease in retail rates
as a result of SPPC&#8217;s various BTER quarterly updates and the annual Natural Gas
and Propane Deferred Rate Cases effective October 1, 2011 and 2010 (see Note 3,
</font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory Actions, </font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">of the Notes to Financial Statements). The decrease
was partially offset by an $8.1 million increase in customer usage primarily
due to an increase in HDDs, and $2.6 million of rate increases due to SPPC&#8217;s
2010 GRC effective January 1, 2011 (see Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory Actions, </font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">of
the Notes to Financial Statements). &#160;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Wholesale
revenues decreased for year ended December 31, 2012, compared to the same
period in 2011, primarily due to a decrease in pipeline optimization sales, an
increase in the utilization of capacity releases and a general decrease in
natural gas costs.&#160;&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;Wholesale
revenues increased for the year ended December 31, 2011, compared to the same
period in 2010, primarily due to an increase in pipeline optimization sales and
seasonal availability of unused capacity. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

Power.&nbsp;&nbsp;These costs are dependent upon many factors which may vary by
season or period.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, SPPC&#8217;s usage and average cost per MWh
of Fuel for Generation versus Purchased Power can vary significantly as the
company meets the demands of the season.&nbsp;&nbsp;These factors include, but
are not limited to:</font></p>

to the same period in 2011 primarily due to lower natural gas prices and a
decrease in costs associated with hedging activities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Energy costs and
the average cost per MWh decreased for the year ended December 31, 2011,
compared to the same period in 2010, primarily due to decreased hedging costs
along with lower natural gas costs. Total system demand for the year ended
December 31, 2011 increased for the same period due to colder winter
temperatures. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Gas
purchased for resale decreased for the year ended December 31, 2012, compared
to the same period in 2011.&#160; Approximately $24.3 million of the decrease is due
to lower natural gas prices and approximately $21.0 million is due to a
decrease in volume.&#160; Volume decreased primarily due to a decrease in pipeline
optimization sales and an increase in the utilization of capacity releases.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Gas
purchased for resale decreased for the year ended December 31, 2011, compared
to the same period in 2010.&#160; Approximately $13.1 million of the decrease is due
to a decrease in option expense and approximately $12.7 million is due to lower
natural gas prices, both offset by an increase in volume of $13.2 million.&#160; The
volume of gas purchased for resale increased in 2011 compared to 2010 primarily
due to pipeline optimization sales.</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:normal;"> &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred energy -
electric for 2012, 2011 and 2010 reflect amortization of deferred energy costs
of $(78.6), $(104.9) and $(42.5) million, respectively; which represent cash
refunds to our customers for previous over-collections partially offset by an
over-collection of amounts recoverable in rates of $52.2, $39.5 and $51.0
million in 2012, 2011 and 2010 respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Refer to Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory
Actions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the Notes to Financial Statements for further detail of
deferred energy balances.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred energy -
gas for 2012, 2011 and 2010 reflect amortization of deferred energy of $(29.2),
$(22.2) and $(11.1) million, respectively; which represent cash refunds to our
customers for previous over-collections partially offset by an over-collection
of amounts recoverable in rates of $16.9, $20.7 and $20.9 million in 2012, 2011
and 2010 respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred energy
represents the difference between actual fuel and purchased power costs
incurred during the period and amounts recoverable through current
rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the extent actual costs exceed amounts recoverable through
current rates, the excess is recognized as a reduction in
costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Conversely to the extent actual costs are less than amounts
recoverable through current rates, the difference is recognized as an increase
in costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Deferred energy also includes the current amortization of
fuel and purchased power costs previously deferred.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Energy efficiency
program costs increased for the year ended December 31, 2012 compared to the
same period in 2011 due to the implementation of EEPR base rates in July 2011
and amortization rates effective October 2011.</font></p>

<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHWbb42e139_fc54_4820_9a55_a8327ec4a627_"></a>Energy efficiency program
costs are conservation costs being recovered from ratepayers through EEPR
revenues which were implemented in July 2011 for base rates and in October 2011
for amortization rates (See Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory Actions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the Notes to
Financial Statements).&#160; Costs incurred prior to the implementation of the EEPR
rates are recovered through the general rates and amortized to other operating
expense discussed below.&#160; The EEPR mechanism is designed such that conservation
costs are equal to revenues collected and any over/under collection is deferred
as a regulatory asset/liability until rates are reset.&#160; As a result, amounts
related to EEPR do not have an effect on gross margin, operating income or net
income.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other operating
expense decreased for the year ended December 31, 2012, compared to the same
period in 2011, primarily due to the following:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$4.4 million decrease in pension and benefit costs;<a name="EHWd33116ca_f862_43cd_992d_5003275fc233"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$3.3 million increase in capitalized costs due to an increase in
construction activity;<a name="EHW9390add7_0884_4987_b4bf_87b717ec2732"></a><a name="EHWd33116ca_f862_43cd_992d_5003275fc233_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$1.8 million decrease in rate cases expenses; and<a name="EHWe13eee8d_c4fc_41b3_91a0_695de7c968c5"></a><a name="EHW9390add7_0884_4987_b4bf_87b717ec2732_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$1.3 million decrease in telecommunications and information technology
expenses.&#160; <a name="EHW4b322b22_f323_4390_840f_4f7c8c106ed0"></a><a name="EHWe13eee8d_c4fc_41b3_91a0_695de7c968c5_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The decrease
was partially offset by a $2.1 million increase in outside legal consulting
fees, and a $1.4 million increase in stock compensation costs.<a name="EHW4b322b22_f323_4390_840f_4f7c8c106ed0_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other operating
expense decreased for the year ended December 31, 2011, compared to the same
period in 2010, primarily due to the following:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$5.1 million in reduced customer expenses;<a name="EHWb5045b49_3e56_4c15_8240_31f3d713aa88"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$4.0 million decrease in outside consulting fees;<a name="EHW59d20271_4fa2_414f_8e67_90ede78054bc"></a><a name="EHWb5045b49_3e56_4c15_8240_31f3d713aa88_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$2.1 million decrease in rate case expenses;<a name="EHW8d01b5d6_1f5f_4e32_a435_1bc009b1e69f"></a><a name="EHW59d20271_4fa2_414f_8e67_90ede78054bc_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$2.0 million decrease in lease expenses; and<a name="EHWb59de838_f760_4a8f_8824_f7ca73dc627b"></a><a name="EHW8d01b5d6_1f5f_4e32_a435_1bc009b1e69f_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$1.2 million decrease in employee pension and benefit costs. <a name="EHW7c2403f2_0916_4eb2_98ef_c257c74db2eb"></a><a name="EHWb59de838_f760_4a8f_8824_f7ca73dc627b_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:74.25pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="EHW7c2403f2_0916_4eb2_98ef_c257c74db2eb_"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">These decreases
were partially offset by $9.6 million of regulatory amortizations primarily for
conservation programs and a $3.7 million increase in stock compensation costs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=red face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Maintenance
expense decreased for the year ended December 31, 2012, compared to the same
period in 2011, primarily due to a $5.9 million decrease in planned maintenance
and outages at the Valmy Generating Station, offset by a $1.5 million increase
in &#160;planned maintenance and outages at the Tracy Generating Station.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=red face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Maintenance
expense increased for the year ended December 31, 2011, compared to the same
period in 2010, mainly due to a $2.1 million increase for planned maintenance outages
at the Valmy Generating Station and a $2.9 million increase for planned maintenance
and outages at the Tracy and Ft. Churchill Generating Stations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Depreciation and amortization
increased for the year ended December 31, 2012, compared to 2011, primarily due
to growth in plant.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Depreciation and
amortization decreased for the year ended December 31, 2011, compared to the
same period in 2010, primarily due to change in depreciation rates effective
January 1, 2011.</font></p>

decreased for the year ended December 31, 2012, compared to the same period in

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest expense
decreased for the year ended December 31, 2011, compared to the same period in
2010, primarily due to the decrease of interest expense of $6.1 million related
to the redemption of $100 million Series H General and Refunding Mortgage Bonds
in December 2010, offset by an increase of $5.3 million in debt redemption
amortization expenses. See Note 6, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Long-Term Debt</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the Notes to
Financial Statements for additional information regarding long-term debt. &#160;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest expense on regulatory items decreased for the
year ended December 31, 2012, compared to the same period in 2011, primarily
due to $3.2 million in decreased interest expense related to lower
over-collected deferred energy balances in 2012. See Note 3, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory
Actions</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the Notes to Financial Statements for further details of
deferred energy balances.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest expense on regulatory items decreased for the
year ended December 31, 2011, compared to the same period in 2010, primarily due
to $1.8 million in decreased interest expense related to lower over-collected
deferred energy balances in 2011 of $1.8 million, offset by a $1.0 million
decrease in carrying charges on solar conservation programs. See Note 3, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory
Actions</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the Notes to Financial Statements for further details of
deferred energy balances.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">AFUDC-equity
increased slightly for the year ended December 31, 2012, compared to 2011,
primarily due to an increase in base construction projects.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">AFUDC-equity
decreased for the year ended December 31, 2011, compared to the same period in
2010, primarily due to completion of various construction projects.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other income increased for the year ended December 31,
2012, compared to the same period in 2011, primarily due to a $1.1 million
settlement with CAISO in 2011 recognized in 2012. &#160;For further discussion, see
Note 3, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory Actions, FERC Matters</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the Notes to Financial Statements.
</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other income decreased for the year ended December 31, 2011, compared to
the same period in 2010, primarily due to</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> the
recognition of the gain on sale of Independence Lake in 2010 of $4.9 million,
as further discussed in Note 15, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Assets Held for Sale,</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> of the Notes to
Financial Statements,</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> a decrease in income from subleases in 2011 of
$2.1 million, and a reduction in other miscellaneous gains of $1.1 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other expense
decreased for the year ended December 31, 2012, as compared to the same period
in 2011 primarily due to the following:</font></p>

</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$2.8 million adjustment, recorded in 2011, as a result of an order from
the PUCN adjusting EEIR revenue recorded in 2010 see Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><a name="EHW7bce6310_052d_495b_8c6e_11c8d7d91be0_"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">These decreases

Notes to Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other expense increased for the year ended December 31, 2011 compared to
the same period in 2010 primarily due to the following:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$2.8 million adjustment in the second quarter of 2011, upon final order
from the PUCN, for EEIR revenue recorded in 2010;<a name="EHWcc518c97_e0e1_4da9_9b9e_4a09753658c9"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font face="Times New Roman Bold" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;text-transform:uppercase;">Analysis of Cash Flows</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><a name="SPPCanalysis_bclEnd"></a><font face="Times New Roman Bold" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SPPC&#8217;s cash flows
decreased during the year ended December 31, 2012, compared to the same period
in 2011, due to an increase in cash used by investing activities, offset
partially by an increase in cash from operating activities and a reduction in
cash used by financing activities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash from
Operating Activities - </font></i></b><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
increase in cash from operating activities was primarily due to a reduction in
refunds of over collected balances for energy, reduced coal purchases,
increased customer deposits and over collections of EEPR. These increases were
partially offset by increased energy payments due to a change in terms with
energy counterparties from weekly to monthly settlements in mid-2011, higher
rebates for wind energy in 2012, the receipt of cash in 2011 under the
affiliate tax sharing agreement and the timing of property tax payments.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash used by
Investing Activities - </font></i></b><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
increase in cash used by investing activities was primarily due to increased
capital expenditure for the NV Energize project in 2012 partially offset by
CIAC received under the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009 for the NV
Energize project.&#160; The increase in cash used by investing activities further
increased due to the receipt of proceeds in 2011 from the sale of the
California Assets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash used by
Financing Activities - </font></i></b><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
decrease in cash used by financing activities is primarily due to a reduction
in dividends to NVE and the repayment of draws under SPPC&#8217;s revolving credit
facility in 2011.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SPPC&#8217;s cash flows
increased in 2011 compared to 2010 due to a decrease in cash used by investing
and financing activities, offset partially by a decrease in cash from operating
activities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash from
Operating Activities - </font></i></b><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
decrease in cash from operating activities was primarily due to a decrease in
net income, an overall decrease in rates resulting from quarterly BTER
adjustments and negative DEAA rates implemented in October 2010 to refund prior
period over collected balances to customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Also contributing to
the decrease is the reduction in revenues from California customers due to the
sale of the California Assets, as discussed in Note 15, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Assets Held for Sale</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">,
of the Notes to Financial Statements, an increase in coal inventory for the
Valmy Generating Station, an increase in conservation and renewable energy
program costs, increased funding of pension plans and increased incentive
compensation payments for the 2010 operating results.&nbsp;&nbsp;These
decreases were partially offset by the recovery of deferred conservation
program costs as a result of SPPC&#8217;s 2010 GRC.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash used by
Investing Activities - </font></i></b><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;Cash
used by investing activities decreased due to the receipt of proceeds from the
sale of California Assets, as discussed in Note 15,&#160; </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Assets Held for Sale</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">,
of the Notes to Financial Statements and CIAC received under the American Recovery
and Reinvestment Act of 2009, as part of NV Energize.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash used by
Financing Activities - </font></i></b><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
decrease in cash used by financing activities is primarily due to a reduction
in retirement of long-term debt, offset partially by higher dividends to NVE.</font></p>








<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><a name=SPPCliquidity></a><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">LIQUIDITY AND CAPITAL RESOURCES</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><a name="SPPCliquidity_bclEnd"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Overall Liquidity</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SPPC&#8217;s primary source of operating cash flows is electric and natural
gas revenues, including the recovery of previously deferred energy
costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Significant uses of cash flows from operations include the
purchase of electricity and natural gas, other operating expenses, capital
expenditures and the payment of interest on SPPC&#8217;s outstanding
indebtedness.&nbsp;&nbsp;Another significant use of cash is the refunding of
previously over-collected amounts from customers.&#160; See Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory
Actions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, of the Notes to Financial Statements for more details of
over-collected balances.&#160; Operating cash flows can be significantly influenced
by factors such as weather, regulatory outcome and economic conditions.&#160;

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SPPC attempts to maintain
its cash and cash equivalents in highly liquid investments, such as U.S. Treasury
Bills and bank deposits.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to cash on hand, SPPC may use
its revolving credit facility in order to meet its liquidity needs.&#160;
Alternatively, depending on the usage of the revolving credit facility, SPPC
may issue debt, subject to certain restrictions as discussed in </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Factors
Affecting Liquidity</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, Ability to Issue Debt, below.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SPPC&#8217;s $250 million 5.45% General and Refunding Notes,
Series Q, will mature on September 1, 2013.&#160; To meet this maturing debt
obligation, SPPC intends to use a combination of internally generated funds, its
revolving credit facility, and/or the issuance of long-term debt.&#160; As of
February 21, 2013, SPPC has no borrowings on its revolving credit facility, not
including letters of credit. In 2012, SPPC&#8217;s credit ratings on its senior
secured debt remained at investment grade (see </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Credit Ratings</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">
below).&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2012, SPPC did not experience any limitations in the
credit markets, nor do we expect any significant limitations in 2013.&#160; However,
disruptions in the banking and capital markets not specifically related to SPPC
may affect its ability to access funding sources or cause an increase in the
interest rates paid on&nbsp;newly issued debt.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In prior years, SPPC required significant amounts of
liquidity due to the magnitude of capital expenditures needed to support a
growing customer base and to support unstable energy markets.&#160; As SPPC
transitioned to slower growth, the amount of capital expenditures has
declined.&#160; SPPC&#8217;s investment in generating stations in the past several years and
more stable energy markets have positioned SPPC to better manage and optimize its
resources.&#160; As a result, SPPC anticipates that it will be able to meet short
term operating costs and capital expenditures with internally generated funds
and the use of its revolving credit facilities.&#160; Furthermore, with new
investments now in rates, the decrease of hedging costs, more current rate
recovery of deferred energy costs, various rate reset mechanisms, federal tax
NOL and a decrease in capital expenditures, SPPC expects to generate free cash
flow.&#160; The free cash flow may be used to reduce debt, to increase dividend
payout and for potential investment opportunities.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">However, if energy costs rise at a rapid rate and SPPC
does not recover the cost of fuel and purchased power in a timely manner, if
operating costs are not recovered in a timely manner or SPPC were to experience
a credit rating downgrade resulting in the posting of collateral as discussed
below under </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gas Supplier Matters</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> and </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial Gas Hedges, </font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">the
amount of liquidity available to SPPC could be significantly less.&#160; In order to
maintain sufficient liquidity, SPPC may be required to further delay capital
expenditures, refinance debt or obtain funding through an equity issuance by
NVE.&#160; Additionally, if deemed prudent, SPPC may enter into hedging transactions
in an attempt to mitigate projected or actual rising energy costs.&#160; Currently,
SPPC is not operating under a PUCN approved hedging plan.&#160; Hedging transactions
may have a material impact on SPPC&#8217;s cash flows, unless recovered in rates in a
timely manner.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2012, SPPC paid dividends to NVE of $20 million.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SPPC designs operating and capital budgets to control
operating costs and capital expenditures.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to operating
expenses, SPPC has continuing commitments for capital expenditures for
construction, improvement and maintenance of facilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Detailed
below are SPPC&#8217;s Capital Structure, Capital Requirements, recently completed
Financing Transactions and Factors Affecting Liquidity, including its ability
to obtain debt on favorable terms.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:36.7pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">(1)</font></sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Includes
the TUA with GBT which is contingent upon final construction costs and reaching
commercial operation.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:36.7pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">(2)</font></sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Amounts
based on estimated usage.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:36.7pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">(3)</font></sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; SPPC,
as a joint owner, has obligations regarding the construction of ON Line.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:18.7pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:10.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:115%;">&#160;&#160; Pension and Other Postretirement Benefit Plan
Matters&#160;&#160; </font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE has a qualified pension plan and
other postretirement benefits plan which cover substantially all employees of NVE,
NPC and SPPC. The annual net benefit cost for the plans is expected to increase
in 2013 by approximately $3.1 million compared to the 2012 cost of $22.5
million. As of December 31, 2012, the measurement date, the plan was under
funded under the provisions of the Compensation Retirement Benefits Topic of
the FASC. &#160;Refer to Note 10, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retirement Plan and Postretirement Benefits</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">,
of the Notes to Financial Statements. During 2012, NVE funded a total of $22.1
million to the trusts established for the qualified pension and postretirement
benefit plans. At the present time it is not anticipated that additional
funding will be required in 2013 to meet the minimum funding level requirements
defined by the Pension Protection Act of 2006.&#160; However, NVE and the Utilities
have included in their 2013 assumptions funding levels similar to the 2012
funding.&#160; The amounts to be contributed in 2013 may change subject to market
conditions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Financing Transactions</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; $250 Million Revolving
Credit Facility</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In March
2012, SPPC terminated its $250 million secured revolving credit facility which
would have expired in April 2013 and replaced it with a $250 million secured
revolving credit facility, for which borrowings mature in 2017.&#160; The fees on
the $250 million revolving credit facility for the unused portion and on the
amounts borrowed have decreased from the prior facility reflecting current market
conditions.&#160; The Administrative Agent for the facility is Wells Fargo, N.A.,
and amounts due under the SPPC Credit Agreement are collateralized by SPPC&#8217;s
general and refunding mortgage bonds.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font><font style="mso-no-proof:yes;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;">86</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font></p>
