<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The rate for outstanding loans under the revolving
credit facility will be at either an applicable base rate (defined as the
highest of the Prime Rate, the Federal Funds Rate plus 0.5% and the LIBOR Base
Rate plus 1.0%) plus a margin, or a LIBOR rate plus a margin.&#160; The margin
varies based upon SPPC&#8217;s credit rating by S&amp;P and Moody&#8217;s.&#160; Currently,
SPPC&#8217;s applicable base rate margin is 0.25% and the LIBOR rate margin is 1.25%.&#160;
The rate for outstanding letters of credit will be at the LIBOR rate margin
plus a fee for the issuing bank.&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
$250 million revolving credit facility contains a provision which reduces the
availability under the credit facility by the negative mark-to-market exposure
for hedging transactions with credit facility lenders or their energy trading
affiliates.&#160; The reduction in availability limits the amount that SPPC can
borrow or use for letters of credit and would require that SPPC prepay any
amount in excess of that limitation.&#160; The amount of the reduction is calculated
by SPPC on a monthly basis, and after calculating such reduction, the SPPC
Credit Agreement provides that the reduction in availability under the
revolving credit facility to SPPC shall in no event exceed 50% of the total
commitments then in effect under the revolving credit facility. Currently,
there are no negative mark-to-market exposures that would impact borrowings.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
SPPC Credit Agreement contains one financial maintenance covenant that requires
SPPC to maintain a ratio of consolidated indebtedness to consolidated capital,
determined as of the last day of each fiscal quarter, not to exceed 0.68 to 1.&#160;
In the event that SPPC did not meet the financial maintenance covenant or there
is a different event of default, the SPPC Credit Agreement would restrict
dividends to NVE.&#160; Moreover, so long as SPPC&#8217;s senior secured debt remains
rated investment grade by S&amp;P and Moody&#8217;s (in each case, with a stable or
better outlook), a representation concerning no material adverse change in
SPPC&#8217;s business, assets, property or financial condition would not be a
condition to the availability of credit under the facility.&#160; In the event that
SPPC&#8217;s senior secured debt rating were rated below investment grade by either
S&amp;P or Moody&#8217;s, or investment grade by either S&amp;P or Moody&#8217;s but with a
negative outlook, a representation concerning no material adverse change in
SPPC&#8217;s business, assets, property or financial condition would be a condition
to borrowing under the revolving credit facility.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
SPPC Credit Agreement provides for an event of default if there is a failure
under SPPC&#8217;s other financing agreements to meet certain payment terms or to
observe other covenants that would result in an acceleration of payments due.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
SPPC Credit Agreement places certain restrictions on debt incurrence, liens and
dividends.&nbsp;&nbsp;These limitations are discussed in Note 8, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Debt
Covenant and Other Restrictions, </font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">of the Notes to Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Factors
Affecting Liquidity</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&nbsp;&#160;&#160; </font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Ability
to Issue Debt</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">SPPC&#8217;s
ability to issue debt is impacted by certain factors such as financing
authority from the PUCN, financial covenants in its financing agreements and
its revolving credit facility agreement, and the terms of NVE&#8217;s Term Loan.&#160; As
of December 31, 2012, the most restrictive of the factors below is the PUCN
authority.&#160; Based on this restriction, SPPC may issue up to $350 million of
long-term debt securities, and maintain a credit facility of up to $600
million.&#160; However, depending on NVE&#8217;s or NPC&#8217;s issuance of long-term debt or
the use of the Utilities&#8217; revolving credit facilities, the PUCN authority may not
remain the most restrictive factor.&#160; The factors affecting SPPC&#8217;s ability to
issue debt are further detailed below:</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:58.3pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">a.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Financing
authority from the PUCN - As of December 31, 2012, SPPC has financing authority
from the PUCN for the period ending December 31, 2015, consisting of authority
(1) to issue additional long-term debt securities of up to $350 million; (2) to
refinance approximately $348 million of long-term debt securities; and (3)
ongoing authority to maintain a revolving credit facility of up to $600
million.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:58.3pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:58.3pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">b.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Financial
covenants within SPPC&#8217;s financing agreements &#8211; Under SPPC&#8217;s $250 million
revolving credit facility, SPPC must maintain a ratio of consolidated
indebtedness to consolidated capital, determined as of the last day of each
fiscal quarter, not to exceed 0.68 to 1.&#160; Based on December 31, 2012 financial
statements, SPPC was in compliance with this covenant and could incur up to
$1.0 billion of additional indebtedness.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:58.3pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:58.3pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">All other
financial covenants contained in SPPC&#8217;s financing agreements are currently suspended;
as SPPC&#8217;s senior secured debt is rated investment grade.&#160; However, if SPPC&#8217;s
senior secured debt ratings fall below investment grade by either Moody&#8217;s or
S&amp;P, SPPC would again be subject to the limitations under these additional
covenants.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:58.3pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:58.3pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">c.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Financial
covenants within NVE&#8217;s Term Loan &#8211; As discussed in NVE&#8217;s </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Ability to Issue
Debt</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">, SPPC is also subject to NVE&#8217;s cap on additional consolidated
indebtedness of $3.3 billion.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; Ability to Issue General and Refunding Mortgage Securities</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">To the extent that SPPC has the ability to issue debt
under the most restrictive covenants in its financing agreements and has
financing authority to do so from the PUCN, SPPC&#8217;s ability to issue secured
debt is still limited by the amount of bondable property or retired bonds that
can be used to issue debt under SPPC&#8217;s Indenture.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">SPPC&#8217;s
Indenture creates a lien on substantially all of SPPC&#8217;s properties in
Nevada.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2012, $1.5 billion of SPPC&#8217;s General and
Refunding Mortgage Securities were outstanding.&nbsp;&nbsp;SPPC had the
capacity to issue $824 million</font><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;"> </font></b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">of additional General and Refunding
Mortgage Securities as of December 31, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;That amount is
determined on the basis of:</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:27.0pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">1.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; 70% of net utility property additions;
and/or</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:27.0pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">2.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; The principal amount of retired General and
Refunding Mortgage Securities.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font style="display:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Property
additions include plant in service and specific assets in CWIP.&nbsp;&nbsp;The
amount of bond capacity listed above does not include eligible property in
CWIP.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">SPPC
also has the ability to release property from the lien of SPPC&#8217;s Indenture on
the basis of net property additions, cash and/or retired bonds.&nbsp;&nbsp;To
the extent SPPC releases property from the lien of SPPC&#8217;s Indenture, it will
reduce the amount of securities issuable under the Indenture.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; </font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Credit Ratings</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:10.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The liquidity of SPPC, the cost and
availability of borrowing by SPPC under its credit facility, the potential
exposure of SPPC to collateral calls under various contracts and the ability of
SPPC to acquire fuel and purchased power on favorable terms are all directly
affected by the credit rating for SPPC&#8217;s debt.&#160; On February 20, 2013, S&amp;P
upgraded SPPC&#8217;s corporate credit rating from BB+ to investment grade BBB-.&#160;
SPPC&#8217;s senior secured debt is rated investment grade by three NRSROs:&#160; Fitch,
Moody&#8217;s and S&amp;P.&nbsp;&nbsp;The senior secured debt credit ratings are as
follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fitch&#8217;s
rating outlook is Positive, while Moody&#8217;s and S&amp;P&#8217;s rating outlook for SPPC
is Stable.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">A security rating is not a recommendation to buy, sell
or hold securities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Security ratings are subject to revision and
withdrawal at any time by the assigning rating organization.&#160; Each security
rating agency has its own methodology for assigning ratings, and, accordingly,
each rating should be evaluated in the context of the applicable methodology,
independently of all other ratings.&#160; The rating agencies provide ratings at the
request of the company being rated and charge the company fees for their
services.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Energy Supplier Matters</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">With respect to SPPC&#8217;s contracts for
purchased power, SPPC purchases and sells electricity with counterparties under
the WSPP agreement, an industry standard contract that SPPC uses as&nbsp;a
member of the WSPP. &nbsp;The WSPP contract is posted on the WSPP website.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under these contracts, a material adverse change,
which includes a credit rating downgrade, in SPPC may allow the counterparty to
request adequate financial assurance, which, if not provided within three
business days, could cause a default. &nbsp;Most contracts and confirmations
for purchased power have been modified or separate agreements have been made to
either shorten the normal payment due date or require payment in advance of
delivery in response to requests for financial assurance.&#160; A default must be
declared within 30 days of the event, giving rise to the default becoming
known. &nbsp;A default will result in a termination payment equal to the
present value of the net gains and losses for the entire remaining term of all
contracts between the parties aggregated to a single </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>
<DIV bclFooter>





<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font><font style="mso-no-proof:yes;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;">88</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:2.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name=bcl_connect_prev></a><!-- Do not modify before this point! !--><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">liquidated
amount due within three business days following the date the notice of
termination is received. &nbsp;The mark-to-market value, which is substantially
based on quoted market prices, can be used to roughly approximate the
termination payment and benefit at any point in time.&nbsp;According to the net
mark-to-market value</font><font color=red face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> </font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">as of December 31, 2012, no
amounts would be due to or from SPPC for all suppliers continuing to provide
power under a WSPP agreement.&nbsp; These contracts qualify for the normal
purchases scope exception as defined by the Derivatives and Hedging Topic of
the FASC, and as such, are not required to be mark-to-market on the balance
sheet.&nbsp; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gas Supplier Matters</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">With respect to the purchase and sale of
natural gas, SPPC uses several types of standard industry contracts.&nbsp; The
natural gas contract terms and conditions are more varied than the electric contracts.&nbsp;
Consequently, some of the contracts contain language similar to that found in
the WSPP agreement and other agreements have unique provisions dealing with
material adverse change, which primarily means a credit rating downgrade below
investment grade. &nbsp;Forward physical gas supplies are purchased under index
based pricing terms and as such do not carry forward mark-to-market
exposure.&nbsp;&nbsp;Most contracts and confirmations for natural gas purchases
have been modified or separate agreements have been made to either shorten the
normal payment due date or require payment in advance of delivery.&nbsp; At the
present time, no counterparties require payment in advance of delivery.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gas transmission service is secured under FERC Tariffs
or custom agreements. &nbsp;These service contracts and Tariffs require the
user to establish and maintain creditworthiness to obtain service or otherwise
post cash or a letter of credit to be able to receive service. &nbsp;Service
contracts are subject to FERC approved Tariffs, which, under certain
circumstances, require the Utilities to provide collateral to continue
receiving service.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial Gas Hedges </font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SPPC may enter into certain hedging contracts with
various counterparties to manage the gas price risk inherent in purchased power
and fuel contracts.&nbsp;&nbsp;As discussed under SPPC&#8217;s Financing
Transactions, the availability under SPPC&#8217;s revolving credit facility is
reduced by the amount of net negative mark-to-market positions on hedging
contracts with counterparties who are lenders to the revolving credit facility,
provided that the reduction in availability under the revolving credit facility
shall at no time exceed 50% of the total commitments then in effect under the
revolving credit facility.&#160; Currently, there are no negative mark-to-market
exposures that would impact borrowings of SPPC. </font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">If
deemed prudent, SPPC may still purchase hedging instruments in the event
circumstances occur that may have the potential to increase the cost of fuel
and purchased power.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cross Default Provisions</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">None of the financing agreements of SPPC
contains a cross default provision that would result in an event of default by
SPPC upon an event of default by NVE or NPC under any of its financing
agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, certain financing agreements of SPPC provide
for an event of default if there is a failure under other financing agreements
of SPPC to meet payment terms or to observe other covenants that would result
in an acceleration of payments due.&nbsp;&nbsp;Most of these default provisions
(other than ones relating to a failure to pay such other indebtedness when due)
provide for a cure period of 30-60 days from the occurrence of a specified
event during which time SPPC may rectify or correct the situation before it
becomes an event of default.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest Rate Risk</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December

instruments whose values are subject to market sensitivity.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such
instruments are fixed and variable rate debt.&nbsp; Fair market value is
determined using quoted market price for the same or similar issues or on the
current rates offered for debt of the same remaining maturities (dollars in
thousands): </font></p>

<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Commodity
Price Risk</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Commodity price increases due to changes in market conditions are
recovered through the deferred energy mechanism.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although the
Utilities actively manage energy commodity (electric, natural gas, coal and
oil) price risk through their procurement strategies, the ability to recover
commodity price changes through future rates substantially mitigates commodity
price risk.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, the Utilities are subject to cash flow risk due
to changes in the value of their open positions and are subject to regulatory
risk because the PUCN may disallow recovery for any costs that it considers
imprudently incurred.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Utilities mitigate both risk associated
with its open positions and regulatory risk through prudent energy supply
practices which include the use of long-term fuel supply agreements, long-term
purchase power agreements and derivative instruments such as forwards, options
and swaps to meet the anticipated fuel and power requirements.&nbsp;&nbsp;See </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Energy
Supply</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> in Item 1, Business, for a discussion of the Utilities&#8217; purchased
power procurement strategies.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Credit Risk</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Utilities monitor and manage credit risk with their trading
counterparties.&nbsp; Credit risk is defined as the possibility that a
counterparty to one or more contracts will be unable or unwilling to fulfill
its financial or physical obligations to the Utilities because of the
counterparty&#8217;s financial condition.&nbsp; The Utilities&#8217; credit risk associated
with trading counterparties was approximately $77.5 million as of December 31,
2012, compared to a balance of $40.7 million at December 31, 2011.&nbsp; </font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The increase from December 31, 2011 is primarily due to the
increase in forward prices of natural gas and power during 2012.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">To the Board of Directors and
Shareholders of</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NV Energy, Inc.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Las Vegas, Nevada</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">We have audited the
accompanying consolidated balance sheets of NV Energy, Inc. and subsidiaries
(the &quot;Company&quot;) as of December 31, 2012 and 2011, and the related
consolidated statements of comprehensive income, shareholders' equity, and cash
flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2012. Our
audits also included the financial statement schedule listed in the Index at Item
15. These financial statements and financial statement schedule are the
responsibility of the Company's management. Our responsibility is to express an
opinion on these financial statements and financial statement schedule based on
our audits.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">We conducted our audits
in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight
Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the
audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are
free of material misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis,
evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. An
audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant
estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial
statement presentation. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis
for our opinion.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In our opinion, such
consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the
financial position of NV Energy, Inc. and subsidiaries as of December 31, 2012
and 2011, and the results of their operations and their cash flows for each of
the three years in the period ended December 31, 2012, in conformity with
accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. Also,
in our opinion, such financial statement schedule, when considered in relation
to the basic consolidated financial statements taken as a whole, presents
fairly, in all material respects, the information set forth therein. </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">We have also
audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting
Oversight Board (United States), the Company's internal control over financial
reporting as of December 31, 2012, based on the criteria established in </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Internal
Control&#8212;Integrated Framework</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;"> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring
Organizations of the Treadway Commission and our report dated February 26, 2013
expressed an unqualified opinion on the Company's internal control over
financial reporting.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">/s/ Deloitte &amp; Touche LLP</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Las Vegas, Nevada</font></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES
TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTE 1.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name=Summary></a></font></b><a href="#Summary"><b><u><font color=blue face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING
POLICIES</font></u></b></a><a name="Summary_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The significant accounting
policies for both utility and non-utility operations are as follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Basis of Presentation</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The consolidated
financial statements include the accounts of NV Energy, Inc. and its
wholly-owned subsidiaries, NPC, SPPC, Sierra Pacific Communications, Lands of
Sierra, Inc., NVE Insurance and Sierra Gas Holding Company.&nbsp;&nbsp;All
intercompany balances and intercompany transactions have been eliminated in
consolidation.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The preparation
of consolidated financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires
management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts
of certain assets and liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;These estimates and assumptions
also affect the disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of
the financial statements and the reported amounts of certain revenues and
expenses during the reporting period.&nbsp;&nbsp;Actual results could differ
from these estimates.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC is an
operating public utility that provides electric service in Clark County in
southern Nevada.&nbsp;&nbsp;The assets of NPC represent approximately 72% of
the consolidated assets of NVE at December 31, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;NPC provides
electricity to approximately 850,000 customers in the communities of Las Vegas,
North Las Vegas, Henderson, Searchlight, Laughlin and adjoining areas,
including Nellis Air Force Base.&nbsp;&nbsp;The consolidated financial
statements of NPC include its wholly-owned subsidiary, NEICO.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SPPC is an
operating public utility that provides electric service in northern Nevada and
previously provided service to northeastern California.&nbsp;&nbsp;SPPC also
provides natural gas service in the Reno/Sparks area of Nevada.&nbsp;&nbsp;The
assets of SPPC represent approximately 28% of the consolidated assets of NVE at
December 31, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;SPPC provides electricity to approximately 324,000
customers in an approximate 42,000 square mile service area including western,
central and northeastern Nevada, including the cities of Reno, Sparks, Carson
City and Elko.&nbsp;&nbsp;On January 1, 2011, SPPC sold its California Assets,
as discussed in Note 15, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Assets Held for Sale</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&#160; SPPC also provides
natural gas service in Nevada to approximately 153,000 customers in an area of
about 800 square miles in the Reno and Sparks areas.&nbsp;&nbsp;The
consolidated financial statements of SPPC include the accounts of SPPC&#8217;s
wholly-owned subsidiaries, PPC, PPIC and GPSF-B.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Utilities&#8217;
accounts are maintained in accordance with the Uniform System of Accounts
prescribed by the FERC.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Reclassifications</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Financial
statement line items for current and long-term risk management liabilities from
prior periods have been combined with Other current liabilities and Other
deferred credits and liabilities lines to conform with current year presentation.&#160;
In addition, interest on regulatory items other than deferred charges has been
classified from Other income, Other expense to Interest income (expense) on
regulatory items.&#160; The reclassifications have not affected previously reported
reports of operations, statements of financial position or shareholders&#8217;
equity.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE and SPPC Balance Sheet
Corrections</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the
fourth quarter of 2012, SPPC discovered an error in its calculation of deferred
income taxes and the related income tax regulatory asset specific to amounts
associated with AFUDC-equity resulting in an understatement of both regulatory
assets and deferred tax liabilities of the same amount.&nbsp; NVE and SPPC have
corrected the December 31, 2011 consolidated balance sheets to increase the regulatory
assets and deferred income tax liabilities by $32.0 million, which did not
result in a change to net assets. NVE and SPPC&#8217;s Statements of Comprehensive
Income, Equity and Cash Flow were not impacted.&nbsp; December 31, 2011 and
2010 amounts for Assets, in Note 2, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Segment Information,</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> for both NVE
and SPPC were also adjusted by $32.0 million and $30.6 million, respectively.&#160;
Additionally, December 31, 2011 amounts for Regulatory assets, Income taxes, in
the Other Regulatory Assets tables for both NVE and SPPC in Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory
Actions,</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> and related deferred tax amounts in Note 9, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Income Taxes
(Benefits)</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, have been adjusted.&#160; Management has concluded that this
correction is immaterial</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Regulatory Accounting and Other
Regulatory Assets</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
Utilities&#8217; rates are subject to the approval of the PUCN and are designed to
recover the cost of providing generation, transmission and distribution
services.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, the Utilities qualify for the application of
regulatory accounting treatment as allowed by the Regulated Operations Topic of
the FASC.&nbsp;&nbsp; This statement recognizes that the rate actions of a
regulator can provide reasonable assurance of the existence of an asset and
requires the deferral of incurred costs that would otherwise be charged to </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>
<DIV bclFooter>





<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font><font style="mso-no-proof:yes;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;">111</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font></p>

<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><a name=bcl_connect_prev></a><!-- Do not modify before this point! !--><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">expense where it is probable that future revenue will be
provided to recover these costs.&nbsp; The accounting guidance prescribes the
method to be used to record the financial transactions of a regulated
entity.&nbsp;&nbsp;The criteria for applying the accounting for regulated operations
include the following: (i) rates are set by an independent third party
regulator; (ii) regulated rates are designed to recover the specific costs of
the regulated products or services; and (iii) it is reasonable to assume that
rates are set at levels that recovered costs can be charged to and collected
from customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management periodically assesses whether the
requirements for application of regulatory accounting treatment as allowed by
the Regulated Operations Topic of the FASC are satisfied.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Regulatory
assets represent incurred costs that have been deferred because it is probable
they will be recovered through future rates collected from
customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;If at any time the incurred costs no longer meet these
criteria, these costs are charged to earnings.&nbsp;&nbsp;Regulatory
liabilities generally represent obligations to make refunds to customers for
previous collections, except for cost of removal which represents the cost of
removing future electric and gas assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management believes the
existing regulatory assets are probable of recovery either because the
Utilities received prior PUCN approval or due to regulatory precedent set for
similar circumstances.&nbsp;&nbsp;Included in Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Regulatory Actions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">,
are details of other regulatory assets and liabilities, and their current
regulatory treatment.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Equity
Carrying Charges</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In accordance with various regulatory orders, the
Utilities record carrying charges as allowed by the Regulated Operations Topic
of the FASC.&nbsp; However, for financial reporting purposes the amounts
representing equity carrying charges are not recognized until collected through
regulated rates.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2012 and 2011, NPC and SPPC have
accumulated approximately $11.1 million and $0.6 million, and $12.7 million and
$0.9 million, respectively, of equity related carrying charges that will be
recognized into income when the corresponding regulatory assets primarily
related to NPC&#8217;s deferred rate increase, the Lenzie Generating Station and the
Utilities&#8217; conservation programs are collected through rates.&nbsp; For further
information, see Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Regulatory Actions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">, Other Regulatory Assets
table</font><font color=#002060 face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Deferred Energy Accounting</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Nevada
and California statutes permit regulated utilities to adopt deferred energy
accounting procedures.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, on January 1, 2011, SPPC sold its
California Assets, as disclosed in Note 15, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Assets Held for Sale</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">.&#160; The
intent of these procedures is to ease the effect on customers of fluctuations
in the cost of purchased gas, fuel and purchased power.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Under
deferred energy accounting, to the extent actual fuel and purchased power costs
exceed fuel and purchased power costs recoverable through current rates that
excess is not recorded as a current expense on the statement of operations but
rather is deferred and recorded as an asset on the balance sheet in accordance
with the provisions of the Regulated Operations Topic of the
FASC.&nbsp;&nbsp;Conversely, a liability is recorded to the extent fuel and
purchased power costs recoverable through current rates exceed actual fuel and
purchased power costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;These excess amounts are reflected in
adjustments to rates and recorded as revenue or expense in future time periods,
subject to PUCN review.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Nevada
law requires the Utilities file annual DEAA applications and provides that the
PUCN may not allow the recovery of any costs for purchased fuel or purchased
power &#8220;that were the result of any practice or transaction that was undertaken,
managed or performed imprudently by the electric utility.&#8221;&nbsp;&nbsp;Nevada
law also specifies that fuel and purchased power costs include all costs
incurred to purchase fuel, to purchase capacity and to purchase
energy.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Utilities also record and are eligible under the statute
to recover a carrying charge on such deferred balances.&nbsp;&nbsp;The
Utilities may also file to reset BTERs quarterly, based on the last 12 months
fuel and purchased power costs.&#160; Additionally, Nevada regulations allow an
electric or gas utility that adjusts its BTER on a quarterly basis to request
PUCN approval to make quarterly changes to its DEAA rate if the request is in
the public interest.&#160; The Utilities are still required to file an annual DEAA
case to review costs for prudency and reasonableness, and if any costs are
disallowed on such grounds, the disallowance will be incorporated into the next
subsequent quarterly rate change.&#160; See Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Regulatory Actions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;"> for
details regarding deferred energy balances</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Energy Efficiency Implementation Rate
(EEIR) and Energy Efficiency Program Rate (EEPR)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In July 2010, regulations were adopted by the
Legislature that authorizes an electric utility to recover lost revenue that is
attributable to the measurable and verifiable effects associated with the
implementation of efficiency and conservation programs approved by the PUCN.&#160;
As a result, the Utilities file annually in March, to adjust rates and set a
clearing rate or EEIR effective in October of the same year for over or under
collected balance, similar to the deferred energy mechanism discussed above. In
addition, the regulation approved the transition of the recovery for the
implementation costs of energy efficiency programs from general rates (filed
every 3 years) to recovery through annual rate filings annually in March, to
adjust rates and set a clearing rate or EEPR effective </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>

deferred energy mechanism discussed above.&#160; See Note 3, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Regulatory Actions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">
for details regarding EEIR and EEPR balances</font><font color=#002060 face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Materials,
Supplies and Fuel</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Generally, materials and supplies include the average cost of
transmission, distribution, and generating plant materials. Materials are
charged to inventory when purchased and then expensed or capitalized to plant,
as appropriate, at weighted average cost when installed.&#160; Fuel inventory
includes the average cost of coal, natural gas and oil. &#160;Fuel is charged to
inventory when purchased and then expensed as used in energy costs and
recovered by the Utilities through BTER rates approved by the PUCN.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Utility Plant</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The cost of additions, including betterments and
replacements of units of property, are charged to utility
plant.&nbsp;&nbsp;When units of property are replaced, renewed or retired,
their cost plus removal or disposal costs, less salvage proceeds, are charged
to accumulated depreciation.&nbsp;&nbsp;The cost of current repairs and minor
replacements are charged to maintenance expense when incurred, with the
exception of long term service agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;These agreements may have
annual payment amounts for repairs which could vary over the life of the
agreement between maintenance expense and amounts to be
capitalized.&nbsp;&nbsp;To ensure consistency in annual expense for rate making
purposes, the amounts to be charged to maintenance expense are smoothed over
the life of the contract, with an offset to a regulatory asset or liability account.&nbsp;&nbsp;Amounts
prepaid for capital expenditure are recorded in a prepaid asset account.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In
addition to direct labor and material costs, certain other direct and indirect
costs are capitalized.&nbsp;&nbsp;The indirect construction overhead costs
capitalized are based upon the following cost components: the cost of time
spent by administrative and supervision employees in planning and directing
construction; property taxes; employee benefits including such costs as pensions,
postretirement and post-employment benefits, vacations and payroll taxes; and
an AFUDC which includes the cost of debt and equity capital associated with
construction activity.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Included
in Total Utility Property, net, as Electric and Natural Gas Distribution assets
are the net carrying values of the remaining meters subject to early retirement
under the NV Energize program for NPC and SPPC.&#160; In accordance with a PUCN
order, the net carrying values are reclassified to a regulatory asset at the
time of retirement.&#160; NPC and SPPC expect full recovery of the regulatory assets
through the Utilities&#8217; regulatory proceedings.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Utility Property<a name=keyword></a> </font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><a name="keyword_bclEnd"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NVE, NPC and SPPC&#8217;s gross utility property and CWIP
are divided into the following major classes at December 31 (dollars in
millions)</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">: &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">AFUDC</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">AFUDC represents the cost of borrowed
funds and, where appropriate, the cost of equity funds used for construction
purposes in accordance with rules prescribed by the FERC and the PUCN.&#160; AFUDC
is capitalized in the same manner as construction labor and material costs,
however, with an offsetting credit to &#8220;other income&#8221; for the portion
representing the cost of equity funds; and as a reduction of interest charges
for the portion representing borrowed funds.&#160; Recognition of this item as a cost
of utility plant is in accordance with established regulatory ratemaking
practices.&#160; Such practices are intended to permit the Utility to earn a fair
return on, and recover in rates charged for utility services, all capital
costs.&#160; This is accomplished by including such costs in the rate base and in
the provision for depreciation.&#160; NPC&#8217;s AFUDC rate used during 2012, 2011 and
2010 were 8.09%, 8.47% and 8.32% respectively.&#160; </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>
<DIV bclFooter>





<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font><font style="mso-no-proof:yes;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;">113</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:2.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><a name=bcl_connect_prev></a><!-- Do not modify before this point! !--><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SPPC&#8217;s
AFUDC rates used during 2012, 2011 and 2010 were 7.86% (Electric), 5.15% (Gas)
and 7.59% (Common), 7.86% (Electric) and 5.15% (Gas), and 7.85%, respectively.&#160;
(In 2012 and 2011, separate rates were calculated for common due to different
rates of return allowed by PUCN Docket 10-06002 for electric and gas).&#160; As specified
by the PUCN, certain projects may be assigned a lower or higher AFUDC rate due
to specific interest-rate financings directly associated with those projects.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><a name="Xbrl_Tag1"></a><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Depreciation</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Substantially all of the Utilities&#8217;
plant is subject to the ratemaking jurisdiction of the PUCN or the FERC.&#160;
Depreciation expense is calculated using the straight-line composite method
over the estimated remaining service lives of the related properties, which
approximates the anticipated physical lives of these assets in most cases. </font><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;</font></b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC&#8217;s
depreciation provision, as authorized by the PUCN and stated as a percentage of
the average depreciable property balances for those years, was approximately
3.22%, 3.04% and 2.99% during 2012, 2011 and 2010, respectively.&#160; SPPC&#8217;s
depreciation provision for 2012, 2011 and 2010, as authorized by the PUCN and
stated as a percentage of the average cost of depreciable property, was
approximately 2.94%, 2.89% and 3.02%, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

each major class of utility property, plant and equipment are as follows</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">:<a name="Xbrl_Tag1_bclEnd"></a> </font></p>
