<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE, NPC and SPPC evaluate on an ongoing basis the
recoverability of its assets for impairments whenever events or changes in
circumstance indicate that the carrying amount may not be recoverable as
described in the Property, Plant and Equipment Topic of the FASC</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash and Cash Equivalents</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash is comprised of cash on hand and working
funds.&nbsp;&nbsp;Cash equivalents consist of high quality investments in money
market funds with maturities of 90 days or less and do not have any withdrawal
restrictions</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="Xbrl_Tag8"></a><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Allowance for Uncollectible Accounts</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face=inherit lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The allowance for uncollectible
accounts is based on the Utilities' estimate of the collectability of amounts
owed by customers.&nbsp; This estimate is primarily derived from historical
write-off trends applied to the previous five months of revenue and accounts
receivable balances.&nbsp; The Utilities' also have the ability to assess
deposits on customers who have delayed payments or who are deemed to be a
credit risk.&nbsp; Accounts&nbsp;receivable are shown on the balance sheet net
of the allowance for uncollectible accounts<a name="Xbrl_Tag8_bclEnd"></a>.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Federal Income
Taxes</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NVE and the Utilities file a consolidated federal
income tax return.&#160; Current income taxes are allocated based on NVE&#8217;s and each
Utility&#8217;s respective taxable income or loss and tax credits as if each Utility
filed a separate return.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NVE
and the Utilities recognize deferred tax liabilities and assets for the future
tax consequences of events that have been included in the financial statements
or tax returns.&nbsp; Deferred tax liabilities and assets are determined based
on the difference between the financial statement and tax basis of assets and
liabilities using enacted tax rates in effect for the year in which the
differences are expected to reverse.&nbsp; Deferred tax assets are also
recorded for deductions incurred and credits earned that have not been utilized
in tax returns filed or to be filed for tax years through the date of the
financial statements.&#160; Management considers estimates of the amount and
character of future taxable income by tax jurisdiction in assessing the
likelihood of realization of deferred tax assets.&nbsp; If it is not more
likely than not that a deferred tax asset will be realized in its entirety, a
valuation allowance is recorded with respect to the portion estimated not
likely to be realized.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:2.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Tax benefits associated with income tax positions
taken, or expected to be taken, in a tax return are recorded only when the
more-likely-than-not recognition threshold is satisfied and measured at the
largest amount of benefit that is greater than 50 percent likely of being
realized upon settlement.&nbsp; NVE and the Utilities classify interest and
penalties associated with unrecognized tax benefits as interest and other
expense, respectively, within the income statement.&#160; No interest expense or
penalties associated with unrecognized tax benefits have been recorded.&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
Utilities reduce rates to reflect the current tax benefits associated with
recognizing certain tax deductions sooner than when the expenses are recognized
for financial reporting purposes. A regulatory asset is recorded for these
amounts to reflect the future increases in income taxes payable that will be recovered
from customers when these temporary differences reverse. The Utilities have
been fully normalized since 1987. AFUDC-equity is recorded on an after-tax
basis. Accordingly, a regulatory asset is recorded when AFUDC-equity is
recognized. This regulatory asset reverses as the related plant is depreciated,
resulting in an increase to the tax provision.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
Utilities also record regulatory liabilities for obligations to reduce rates
charged customers for deferred taxes recovered from customers in prior years at
corporate tax rates higher than the current tax rates. The reduction in rates
charged customers will occur as the temporary differences resulting in the
excess deferred tax liabilities reverse.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Investment tax credits
are deferred and amortized over the estimated service lives of the related properties</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Revenues</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Unbilled&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Revenues
related to the sale of energy are recorded based on meter reads, which occur on
a systematic basis throughout a month, rather than when the service is rendered
or energy is delivered.&nbsp;&nbsp;At the end of each month, the energy
delivered to the customers from the date of their last meter read to the end of
the month is estimated and the corresponding unbilled revenues are
calculated.&nbsp;&nbsp;These estimates of unbilled sales and revenues are based
on the ratio of billable days versus unbilled days, amount of energy procured
and generated during that month, historical customer class usage patterns, line
loss and the Utilities&#8217; current tariffs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accounts receivable as of
December 31, 2012, included unbilled receivables of $86 million and $50 million
for NPC and SPPC, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accounts receivable as of December
31, 2011, included unbilled receivables of $93 million and $51 million for NPC
and SPPC, respectively</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Asset
Retirement Obligations</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The Asset Retirement and Environmental Liabilities
Topic of the FASC provides accounting requirements for the recognition and
measurement of liabilities associated with the retirement of tangible
long-lived assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the accounting guidance, these liabilities
are recognized in other deferred credits and liabilities at fair value as
incurred and capitalized as part of the cost of the related tangible long-lived
assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accretion of the liabilities due to the passage of time is classified
as an operating expense.&nbsp;&nbsp;Retirement obligations associated with
long-lived assets included within the scope of the accounting guidance are
those for which a legal obligation exists under enacted laws, statutes written
or oral contracts, including obligations arising under the doctrine of
promissory estoppel.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;Management&#8217;s
methodology to assess its legal obligation included an inventory of assets by
company, system and components and a review of rights of way and easements,
regulatory orders, leases and federal, state and local environmental
laws.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management identified a legal obligation to retire generation
plant assets specified in land leases for NPC&#8217;s jointly-owned Navajo Generating
Station and the Higgins Generating Station.&nbsp;&nbsp;Provisions of the lease
require the lessees to remove the facilities upon request of the lessors at the
expiration of the leases.&#160; Additionally, management has determined evaporative
ponds, dry ash landfills, fuel storage tanks, asbestos and oils treated with
Poly Chlorinated Biphenyl to have met the conditional asset retirement
obligations as defined in the Asset Retirement and Environmental Liabilities
Topic of the FASC.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
following table presents a reconciliation of the beginning and ending aggregate
carrying amounts of asset retirement obligation for the years presented below
(dollars in thousands)</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">:&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cost of Removal</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition to the legal asset retirement
obligations booked under the accounting guidance for asset retirement
obligations, the Utilities have accrued for the cost of removing non-legal
retirement obligations of other electric and gas assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amounts
of such accruals included in regulatory liabilities in 2012 are approximately
$252.6 million and $204.4 million for NPC and SPPC, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;In
2011, the amounts were approximately $232.0 million and $189.9 million for NPC
and SPPC, respectively</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">. &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Derivatives and Hedging Activities</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; NVE and the Utilities apply the
accounting guidance as required by the Derivatives and Hedging Topic of the
FASC.&#160; The accounting guidance for derivative instruments, including certain
derivative instruments embedded in other contracts and for hedging activities,
requires that an entity recognize all derivatives as either assets or
liabilities in the statement of financial position, measure those instruments
at fair value, and recognize changes in the fair value of the derivative
instruments in earnings in the period of change, unless the derivative meets
certain defined conditions and qualifies as an effective hedge.&#160; The accounting
guidance for derivative instruments also provides a scope exception for
commodity contracts that meet the normal purchase and sales criteria specified
in the standard.&nbsp;&nbsp;The normal purchases and normal sales exception
requires, among other things, physical delivery in quantities expected to be
used or sold over a reasonable period in the normal course of
business.&nbsp;&nbsp;Contracts that are designated as normal purchases and
normal sales are accounted for under deferred energy accounting and not
recorded on the consolidated balance sheets of NVE and the Utilities at fair
value.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; Commodity Risk</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The energy supply function encompasses
the reliable and efficient operation of the Utilities' generation, the
procurement of all fuels and power and resource optimization (i.e., physical
and economic dispatch) and is exposed to risks relating to, but not limited to,
changes in commodity prices.&nbsp;&nbsp;NVE and the Utilities' objective in
using derivative instruments is to reduce exposure to energy price
risk.&nbsp;&nbsp;Energy price risks result from activities that include the
generation, procurement and sale of power and the procurement and sale of
natural gas.&nbsp;&nbsp;Derivative instruments used to manage energy price risk
from time to time may include: forward contracts, which involve physical
delivery of an energy commodity; over-the-counter options with financial
institutions and other energy companies, which mitigate price risk by providing
the right, but not the requirement, to buy or sell energy related commodities
at a fixed price; and swaps, which require the Utilities to receive or make
payments based on the difference between a specified price and the actual price
of the underlying commodity. These contracts may assist the Utilities reduce
the risks associated in volatile electricity and natural gas markets. As of
December 31, 2012, the Utilities were not parties to such derivative
transactions.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; Interest Rate Risk</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE and the Utilities may enter
into interest rate swap agreements to manage existing and future fixed rate
interest rate exposure in an effort to lower overall borrowing costs.&nbsp;
These transactions are discussed further in Note 6, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Long Term Debt,</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">
under the respective financing agreements as applicable.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Variable
Interest Entities </font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NVE and the Utilities continually perform an analysis
to determine whether their variable interests give them controlling financial
interest in a VIE which would require consolidation.&#160; This analysis identifies
the primary beneficiary of a VIE as the enterprise that has both the following
characteristics: a) the power to direct the activities of a VIE that most
significantly impact the entity&#8217;s economic performance, and b) the obligation
to absorb losses of the entity that could potentially be significant to the VIE
or the right to receive benefits from the entity that could potentially be
significant to the VIE.&#160; To identify potential variable interests, management
reviews contracts under leases, long term purchase power contracts, tolling
contracts and jointly owned facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Utilities identified
certain long-term purchase power contracts that could be defined as variable
interests.&#160; However, the Utilities are not the primary beneficiary as defined
above, as they primarily lacked the power to direct the activities of the
entity, including the ability to operate the generating facilities and make
management decisions.&#160; The Utilities' maximum exposure to loss is limited to
the cost of replacing these purchase power contracts if the providers are
unable to deliver power.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, the Utilities believe their
exposure is mitigated as they would likely recover these costs through their
deferred energy accounting mechanism.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2012, the
carrying amount of assets and liabilities in the Utilities&#8217; balance sheets that
relate to their involvement with VIEs are </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>
<DIV bclFooter>

related to working capital accounts and generally represent the amounts owed by
the Utilities for the deliveries associated with the current billing cycle
under the contracts</font><font color=#002060 face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Franchise Fees
and Universal Energy Charges</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NPC and SPPC, as agents for some state and local
governments collect from customers franchise fees and universal energy charges
levied by the state or local governments on our customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;NPC and
SPPC present such fees on a net basis, as such, fees are excluded from revenue
and expense</font><font color=#002060 face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">.&nbsp;</font></p>








<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTE 2.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name=Seginfo></a></font></b><a href="#Seginfo"><b><u><font color=blue face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SEGMENT INFORMATION</font></u></b></a><a name="Seginfo_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Utilities operate three regulated business segments, NPC electric,
SPPC electric and SPPC natural gas service, which are reported in accordance
with Segment Reporting of the FASC.&#160; Electric service is provided to Las Vegas
and surrounding Clark County by NPC, and to northern Nevada by SPPC.&#160; Natural
gas services are provided by SPPC in the Reno-Sparks area of Nevada.&#160; Other
information includes amounts below the quantitative thresholds for separate
disclosure.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Operational information of the different business segments is set forth
below based on the nature of products and services offered.&#160; NVE evaluates
performance based on several factors, of which the primary financial measure is
business segment gross margin.&#160; Gross margin, which the Utilities calculate as
operating revenues less energy and energy efficiency program costs, provides a
measure of income available to support the other operating expenses of the
Utilities.&#160; Energy efficiency program costs are conservation costs being recovered
from ratepayers through EEPR revenues which were implemented in July 2011.&#160;
Costs incurred prior to the implementation of the EEPR are recovered through
general rates and amortized to other operating expense.&#160; The EEPR mechanism is
designed such that conservation costs are equal to revenues collected and any
under/over collection is deferred as a regulatory asset/liability until rates
are reset.&#160; As a result, amounts related to EEPR do not have an effect on gross
margin, operating income or net income. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Operating
expenses are provided by segment in order to reconcile to operating income as
reported in the consolidated financial statements for the years ended December
31 (dollars in thousands)</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">:&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTE 3.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name=Ractions></a></font></b><a href="#Ractions"><b><u><font color=blue face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">REGULATORY
ACTIONS</font></u></b></a><a name="Ractions_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Utilities are subject to the
jurisdiction of the PUCN and in the case of SPPC in prior years, the CPUC with
respect to rates, standards of service, siting of and necessity for generation
and certain transmission facilities, accounting, issuance of securities and
other matters with respect to electric distribution and transmission
operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, on January 1, 2011, SPPC sold its California
Assets, as discussed further in Note 15, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Assets Held for Sale, </font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">and
therefore is no longer subject to the jurisdiction of the CPUC. Under federal
law, the Utilities are subject to certain jurisdictional regulation, primarily
by the FERC.&nbsp;&nbsp;The FERC has jurisdiction under the Federal Power Act
with respect to rates, service, interconnection, accounting and other matters
in connection with the Utilities&#8217; sale of electricity for resale and interstate
transmission.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of regulation, the Utilities are required
to file annual electric and gas DEAA, EEIR and EEPR cases by March 1, and
triennial GRCs.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the Utilities may also file quarterly
DEAA and BTER updates for the Utilities&#8217; electric and gas departments.&#160;
Reference Note 1, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Summary of Significant</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounting Policies </font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">for
further discussion of the various rate components. </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Detailed below are
Deferred Energy Costs which relate to the DEAA and BTER filings and further
below are other regulatory assets and liabilities which primarily relate to the
GRCs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, significant pending or settled rate cases are
discussed below.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following deferred energy amounts were included in
the consolidated balance sheets as of December 31 for the years shown below
(dollars in thousands):</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">As discussed in
Note 1, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, regulatory assets
represent incurred costs that have been deferred because it is probable they
will be recovered through future rates collected from customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;If
at any time the incurred costs no longer meet these criteria, these costs are charged
to earnings.&nbsp;&nbsp;Regulatory liabilities generally represent obligations
to make refunds to customers for previous collections, except for cost of
removal which represents the cost of removing future electric and gas
assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management regularly assesses whether the regulatory assets
are probable of future recovery by considering actions of regulators, current
laws related to regulation, applicable regulatory environment changes and the
status of any current, pending or potential legislation.&nbsp;&nbsp;Detailed
below are Other Regulatory Assets and Liabilities included in the balance sheet
of NVE, NPC and SPPC and their current regulatory treatment as of December 31
(dollars in thousands)</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">:&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:33.1pt;text-indent:-.2in;"><sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;">(1)</font></sup><a name="EHW5a7b9087_9604_46bb_a647_8de90208999d"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW5a7b9087_9604_46bb_a647_8de90208999d_"></a>Earning a return includes either a carrying charge on the
asset/liability balance, or a return as a component of rate base.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:33.1pt;text-indent:-.2in;"><sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;">(2)</font></sup><a name="EHW5fb9f5b3_6ecb_4062_9728_2309d197a5f2"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW5fb9f5b3_6ecb_4062_9728_2309d197a5f2_"></a>Pending regulatory treatment includes either amounts which have prior
regulatory precedent or have been approved and are subject to prudency review. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:33.1pt;text-indent:-.2in;"><sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;">(3)</font></sup><a name="EHW86524e95_4de3_4bb5_90fa_332ced386358"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW86524e95_4de3_4bb5_90fa_332ced386358_"></a>Assets which are allowed to earn a carrying charge until included in
rates.&#160; Reference Note 1, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;">,
Equity Carrying Charges.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:33.1pt;text-indent:-.2in;"><sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;">(4)</font></sup><a name="EHW4bc1873c_2428_48ea_83c7_097247ad701e"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW4bc1873c_2428_48ea_83c7_097247ad701e_"></a> Liability balance represents amounts that have been overcollected.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><a name="EHW580f6d84_e5e5_4029_b2fb_9d443d070d01"></a><font color=#002060 face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW580f6d84_e5e5_4029_b2fb_9d443d070d01_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Regulatory Actions</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NPC&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></i></b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NPC 2012 DEAA, TRED and REPR, Rate Filings</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; In
March 2012, NPC filed an application for the PUCN to review fuel and purchased
power transactions for the 12-month period ending December 31, 2011, to reset
the TRED and REPR rate elements and to retire the unamortized balance of NPC&#8217;s
2008 GRC deferred rate increase, as discussed below in NPC&#8217;s 2010 DEAA.&#160; In
September 2012, the PUCN issued its final order which resulted in an increase
in revenue requirement, as disclosed in the table below, for the 2008 GRC
deferred rate increase, REPR and TRED effective October 2012.&#160; Included in its
September order are immaterial adjustments to deferred fuel and purchase power
balances and a requirement to increase the REPR rate to include prospective
customer incentives associated primarily with its solar rebate programs.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; NPC 2012
EEIR, EEPR Rate Filings</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Subsequent
to filing NPC&#8217;s DEAA, TRED, and REPR rate filings in March 2012, the PUCN
issued a final order in NPC&#8217;s Annual Demand Side Management Update Report,
requiring NPC to revise all lighting-specific calculations used in the EEIR and
EEPR rate applications.&#160; As a result, the parties agreed to bifurcate the EEIR
and EEPR portions of the March filing to allow NPC to amend the EEIR and EEPR
rate requests using revised lighting-specific calculations and to hold a
separate hearing on these components.&#160; In July 2012, NPC filed an amended EEIR
and EEPR rate request.&#160; In December 2012, the PUCN issued its final order which
resulted in an overall decrease in revenue requirement in EEIR and EEPR, as
disclosed in the table below.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In June 2011, NPC filed its statutorily required
triennial GRC and updated the filing in August 2011.&#160; The filing, as updated
requested an ROE of 11.25% and ROR of 8.64% and an increase to general revenues
of $249.9 million.&#160; The PUCN issued its order in December 2011, which resulted
in the following significant items:</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Increase in general rates of
$158.6 million, approximately an 8.3% overall increase effective January 1,
2012;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">ROE and ROR of 10.0% and 8.09%,
respectively;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Recovery of approximately $635.9
million, excluding AFUDC, for the 500 MW (nominally rated) expansion at the
Harry Allen Generating Station;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Recovery of approximately $23.2
million for EEC project development costs;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Recovery of approximately $17.7
million for demand side management costs;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Recovery of approximately $12.7
million for Mohave Generating Station closure costs;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Postpone final regulatory
treatment of EWAM Phase 1 of approximately $46.9 million pending project
completion and prudency review of NPC&#8217;s subsequent GRC filing; and</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Various other rate case
adjustments for the Harry Allen Generating Station, Clark Peaking Units, and
the EEC, offset by regulatory asset treatment for operating expenses for a net
decrease to NVE&#8217;s fourth quarter 2011 consolidated net income of approximately
$15.9 million before tax.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;NPC 2011 DEAA,
TRED, REPR, EEIR, EEPR Rate Filings</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In March 2011, NPC filed an application to establish a
new DEAA to refund over-collected purchased power and fuel costs and reset or
establish several other rate elements (TRED, REPR, EEIR and EEPR).&#160; In
September 2011, the PUCN accepted stipulations which resulted in an overall
decrease in revenue requirement of approximately $78.6 million.&#160; The PUCN
authorized the refund and recovery of the following amounts (dollars in
millions):</font></p>

 <td valign=bottom width=3% style="background:white;height:10.5pt;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;">
  <p align=right style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:right;"><sup><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(2)</font></sup></p>
  </td>
 <td valign=bottom width=2% style="background:white;height:10.5pt;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;">

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC 2010 DEAA</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In March 2010, NPC filed an application to create a new DEAA rate.&#160; In
its application, NPC requested to refund $102 million of deferred fuel and
purchased power costs.&#160; Separately, NPC filed a petition to offset the NPC DEAA
over collection (credit balance) of $102 million against the deferred BTGR
debit balance of $95.8 million.&#160; The BTGR debit balance of $95.8 million was a
result of NPC&#8217;s 2008 GRC, which granted NPC approval to defer billings of its
rate increase from July 1, 2009 to December 31, 2009 in a regulatory asset for
which NPC recognized revenues in 2009.&#160; The PUCN consolidated both dockets for
hearing purposes. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In September
2010, the PUCN accepted a stipulation for the DEAA and BTGR offset
applications, which resulted in an overall revenue decrease of $9.2 million or
0.41% for the period October 1, 2010 through December 31, 2011.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Mohave Generating
Station</font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; NPC
owns approximately 14% of the Mohave Generating Station.&#160; Southern California
Edison is the operating partner of the Mohave Generating Station.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; When
operating, the Mohave Generating Station obtained all of its coal supply from a
mine in northeast Arizona on lands of the Navajo Nation and the Hopi Tribe (the
Tribes).&#160; This coal was delivered from the mine to the Mohave Generating
Station by means of a coal slurry pipeline, which requires water that is
obtained from groundwater wells located on lands of the Tribes in the mine vicinity.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; The
Grand Canyon Trust and Sierra Club filed a lawsuit in the U.S. District Court,
District of Nevada in February 1998 against the owners (including NPC) of the
Mohave Generating Station, alleging violations of the Clean Air Act regarding
emissions of sulfur dioxide and particulates.&#160; An additional plaintiff,
National Parks and Conservation Association, later joined the suit.&#160; In 1999,
the plant owners and plaintiffs filed a settlement with the court, which
resulted in a consent decree, approved by the court in November 1999.&#160; The
consent decree established emission limits for sulfur dioxide and opacity and
required installation of air pollution controls for sulfur dioxide, nitrogen
oxides, and particulate matter.&#160; Pursuant to the decree, the Mohave Generating
Station Units 1 and 2 ceased operations as of January 2006 as the new emission
limits were not met.&#160; Due to the lack of resolutions regarding continual
availability of the coal and water supply with the Tribes, the Owners did not
proceed with the consent decree.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; In
December 2005, the Owners of the Mohave Generating Station suspended operation,
pending resolution of these issues.&#160; However, in June 2006, majority stake
holder Southern California Edison announced it would no longer participate in
the efforts to return the plant to service.&#160; As a result, NPC decided it is not
economically feasible to continue its participation in the project.&#160; In
September 2006, Salt River&#8217;s co-tenancy agreement expired and the operating
agreement between the Owners expired in July 2006.&#160; The Owners are discussing
the negotiation of new agreements that would address the potential disposition
of the assets and rights, title, interest and obligations in the Mohave
Generating Station.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Included
in other regulatory assets is approximately $6.9 million, which has been
approved by the PUCN and included in rates.&#160; All other costs for Mohave
Generating Station, including approximately $14.8 million of decommissioning
costs were accumulated in other regulatory assets as incurred of which $10.5
million were approved by the PUCN, see the Other Regulatory Assets/Liabilities
table above. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; In
June 2009, Southern California Edison announced that the Mohave Generating
Station will be dismantled and its operating permits terminated following a
December 2005 suspension of operations due to pending environmental matters.&#160;
NPC believes it will continue to recover the costs for the Mohave Generating
Station through the regulatory process and does not expect the dismantling of
the plant to have a material impact on its financial condition.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; SPPC 2012 Electric

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:.25in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; In March 2012, SPPC filed an application for the PUCN to review
fuel and purchased power transactions for the 12-month period ending December
31, 2011 and to reset the TRED and REPR rate elements.&#160; In September 2012, the
PUCN issued its final order which resulted in an increase in revenue
requirement, as outlined in the table below, for the REPR and TRED effective
October 2012.&#160; Included in its September order are immaterial adjustments to
deferred fuel and purchase power balances and a requirement to increase the

its solar rebate programs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; SPPC 2012 EEIR,

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:.25in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Subsequent to

hearing on these components.&#160; In July 2012, SPPC filed an amended EEIR and EEPR

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:.25in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In March 2012, SPPC filed an application for the PUCN to review the
physical gas, transportation and financial gas transactions that were recorded
during the 12-month period ending December 31, 2011 and to reset the REPR.&#160; In
September 2012, the PUCN issued its final order which resulted in an overall
increase of $0.2 million that was effective October 1, 2012.</font></p>

DEAA, TRED, REPR, EEIR, EEPR Rate Filings</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; In
March 2011, SPPC filed an application to establish a new DEAA to refund
over-collected purchased power and fuel costs and reset or establish several
other rate elements (TRED, REPR, EEIR and EEPR).&#160; In September 2011, the PUCN
accepted stipulations which resulted in an overall decrease in revenue
requirement of approximately $8.2 million.&#160; The PUCN authorized refund and
recovery of the following amounts (dollars in millions)</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">:

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; SPPC 2011 Nevada
Gas DEAA</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In March 2011,
SPPC filed an application to create a new DEAA rate to refund over-collected
gas costs and to establish a new STPR (Solar Thermal Prospective Rate) to
recover a legislatively mandated solar thermal program.&#160; In September 2011, the
PUCN accepted stipulations which resulted in an overall decrease in revenue
requirement of $12.1 million that was effective October 1, 2011.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><i><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;
</font></i><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">SPPC 2010 Nevada Gas DEAA</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In
March 2010, SPPC filed an application to create a new DEAA rate.&#160;&#160; In
September, the PUCN accepted a stipulation to decrease rates by $8.3 million, a
decrease of 4.69%, while refunding approximately $17 million of deferred gas
costs.&#160; The new DEAA rate became effective October 1, 2010.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">SPPC 2010
Nevada Electric DEAA</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><a name="EHWcf1aa965_e142_4c71_8f93_f9bf627f6543"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHWcf1aa965_e142_4c71_8f93_f9bf627f6543_"></a>In March 2010, SPPC filed an application to create a new DEAA rate.&#160;&#160;
In September, the PUCN accepted a stipulation to decrease rates by $47.0
million, a decrease of 6.31%, while refunding $101 million of deferred fuel and
purchased power costs.&#160; The new DEAA rate became effective October 1, 2010.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; SPPC 2010
Electric GRC</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><a name="EHW04baf851_d468_4a85_b38d_f92817383274"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW7ab98891_4652_4100_9121_108849fe7ea1_"></a>In June 2010, SPPC filed its statutorily required GRC for its Nevada
electric operations and further updated the filing in July and August 2010.&#160;
The filing, as updated, requested an ROE of 10.75% and ROR of 8.14% and an
increase to general revenues of $29.3 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><a name="EHW18de176c_a8e0_4a97_b5ba_67ea777e8ae5"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW18de176c_a8e0_4a97_b5ba_67ea777e8ae5_"></a>The PUCN issued its order in December 2010, which resulted in the
following significant items:</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Increase in general rates by $13.1
million, approximately a 1.90% increase effective January 1, 2011;<a name="EHW40086111_fd3a_42ad_a741_4226a6f66a82"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Authorized to recover new electric
and common plant additions along with ordinary changes in operating expense,

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;

Reference NPC&#8217;s 2011 GRC above for further discussion.<a name="EHW69fe9875_8cd3_47b2_8f9f_2547ba8b46b1"></a><a name="EHW63bbead9_eadc_43c1_a2bc_172002b90036_"></a><a name="EHW69fe9875_8cd3_47b2_8f9f_2547ba8b46b1_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; SPPC 2010 Gas GRC&#160; </font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="EHW5b153da8_2e3c_493d_99b5_1d36e60afa63"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW5b153da8_2e3c_493d_99b5_1d36e60afa63_"></a>In June 2010, SPPC filed a

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><a name="EHW4f5da1b5_8e0e_4d40_b08e_504155c4db82"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW4f5da1b5_8e0e_4d40_b08e_504155c4db82_"></a>The PUCN issued its order

</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Increase in general rates by $2.7 million, approximately a 1.93%

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">ROE and ROR of 10.00% and 5.15%, respectively; and<a name="EHW24f76f93_06ae_4f1f_a7a8_fd73c40fcb3b"></a><a name="EHWd2acb451_7c93_4a8a_9eaf_c5a531fea3c1_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#8226;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
