<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><a name="EHWd8a4d126_efd0_4695_9300_eecddb3d2dbd_"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC and SPPC</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Energy Efficiency
Implementation Rate (EEIR) and Energy Efficiency Program Rate (EEPR)</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">EEIR&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="EHWbf2f7d44_2c53_4a89_b9f3_ec1bbb7d2d1a"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHWbf2f7d44_2c53_4a89_b9f3_ec1bbb7d2d1a_"></a>In 2009, the Legislature
passed Senate Bill 358, which required the PUCN to adopt regulations
authorizing an electric utility to recover lost revenue that is attributable to
the measurable and verifiable effects associated with the implementation of
efficiency and conservation programs approved by the PUCN.&#160; As a result, the
PUCN opened Docket No. 09-07016 to amend and adopt the regulation.&#160; The
regulation was adopted by the Legislature on July 22, 2010.&#160; Accordingly, as of
August 1, 2010, the Utilities began recording the amount of additional revenues
which are objectively determinable and probable of recovery and are attributable
to reduced kWh sales related to energy efficiency programs, prior to their
inclusion in rates in accordance with FASC 980-605-25, Alternative Revenue
Programs.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="EHWf9fdddd9_83d6_41ca_aa19_896ac63372bb"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHWf9fdddd9_83d6_41ca_aa19_896ac63372bb_"></a>In October 2010, the
Utilities filed to set 2011 base rates effective mid-2011 to recover approximately
$35.1 million and $7.6 million for NPC and SPPC, respectively, for estimated
reduced kWh sales related to the Utilities&#8217; energy efficiency programs.&#160;
Annually, thereafter, the Utilities file in March, to adjust rates and set a
clearing rate or EEIR for over or under collected balances, effective in
October of the same year.&#160; In May 2011, the PUCN issued a final order on the
October 2010 filing authorizing increases to the base rates of $14.5 million
and $2.6 million for NPC and SPPC, respectively, effective July 1, 2011.&#160; As a
result of the May order, in June 2011, NPC and SPPC recorded a pre-tax
adjustment to earnings for revenue previously recorded of approximately $4.5
million and $4.1 million, respectively.&#160; As of December 31, 2011, NPC and SPPC
recognized 2011 revenues of approximately $15.5 million and $2.5 million,
respectively, of the authorized EEIR base amounts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In March 2011
and 2012, the Utilities filed applications with their annual DEAA filings to
reset the base rates and clear the accumulated regulatory asset accounts
between January 1 and December 31, 2010 and 2011, respectively, with rates
effective October 2011 and January 2013, respectively.&#160; Reference further
discussion above at </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC and SPPC DEAA, TRED, REPR, EEIR, EEPR Rate Filings.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">EEPR&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="EHW2d041a42_0e2d_456d_ba24_d5f3e655002b"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHWb941e992_ef22_4f8a_800c_0013cf77c6ab_"></a>In addition, the regulation
approved the transition of the recovery of energy efficiency program costs from
general rates (filed every 3 years) to recovery through independent annual rate
filings.&#160; Accordingly, in their filing made in October 2010, the Utilities
requested to set base rates beginning mid-2011 to recover the 2011 costs of
implementing energy efficiency program costs of approximately $71.0 million and
$12.1 million for NPC and SPPC, respectively.&#160; In May 2011, the PUCN issued a
final order authorizing increases to the base rates of $58.4 million and $9.7
million for NPC and SPPC, respectively, effective July 1, 2011.&#160; As of December
31, 2011, NPC and SPPC recorded $37.3 million and $6.2</font><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> </font></b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">million
respectively, of EEPR revenues.&#160; Costs accumulated between January 1 and
December 31, 2010 and 2011, respectively, were requested for recovery in the
March 2011 and 2012 filings with rates effective October 2011 and January 2013,
respectively.&#160; Reference further discussion above&#160; at </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC and SPPC DEAA,
TRED, REPR, EEIR, EEPR Rate Filings.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Ely Energy Center</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;<a name="EHWb96391e0_314a_4008_b039_2af19277525e"></a>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHWb96391e0_314a_4008_b039_2af19277525e_"></a>In February 2011, NVE and
the Utilities cancelled plans to construct the EEC due to increasing
environmental and economic uncertainties.&#160; In June 2009, the Utilities filed to
withdraw the initial construction application under the Utility Environmental
Protection Act (UEPA) filed in 2006 due to postponing the construction of the
EEC.&#160; The PUCN had previously approved the Utilities spending on development
costs and farming assets for the EEC up to $130 million, of which the Utilities
had spent and recorded as an other deferred asset approximately $58.0 million
as of December 31, 2011.&#160; In compliance with the SPPC 2010 Electric GRC, SPPC </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>

project development costs and farming assets and proposed reclassification of
these costs from a deferred debit to a regulatory asset.&#160; In December 2011, the
PUCN authorized recovery of approximately $23.2 million of the development
costs for NPC and reclassification of $23.1 million of farming assets to a
regulatory asset for NPC.&#160; The PUCN also authorized SPPC to reclassify
approximately $11.6 million of development costs and farming assets to
regulatory asset accounts.&#160; In accordance with NPC&#8217;s December 2011 GRC order,
farming assets on NPC and SPPC are subject to prudence review in a subsequent
filing to the PUCN.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">FERC Matters</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">California
Wholesale Spot Market Refunds</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC and SPPC were participants in a FERC proceeding wherein California
parties have been authorized to recalculate, or mitigate, the prices they paid
for wholesale spot market power between October 2, 2000 and June 20,
2001.&nbsp;&nbsp;Both of the Utilities made spot market sales that were
eligible for mitigation.&#160; NPC and SPPC have negotiated a comprehensive
settlement with the California parties and a FERC order on the joint offer of
settlement was approved in February 2012.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"><br>
</font><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">At the time of
the settlement the CAISO and CALPX owed NPC approximately $19 million (plus
interest) for power delivered during the same timeframe, but which was being
held pending resolution of the FERC proceedings, and for which NPC had fully
reserved in 2001.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a part of the settlement, NPC released these
receivables to the California parties which resulted in reversal of the
accounts receivable reserve as of December 31, 2011. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SPPC&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">At the time of
the settlement the CAISO and CALPX owed SPPC approximately $1 million (plus
interest) for power delivered during the same timeframe, but which was being
held pending resolution of the FERC proceedings, and SPPC had recorded a
reserve against the receivable in 2001.&nbsp; As a part of the settlement, SPPC
released these receivables to the California parties which resulted in reversal
of the accounts receivable reserve as of December 31, 2011. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2009, SPPC
recorded an additional $3 million liability for this item.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Settlement&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of
the February 2012 FERC order, NPC and SPPC released to the California parties,
NPC and SPPC&#8217;s claims to the receivables held by the CALPX and CAISO, plus
interest therein, and, paid an immaterial cash amount. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; NPC</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; NPC 2012 FERC Transmission Rate Case</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="EHW73d59952_8bd3_4330_a62e_fa01b3e86236"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW73d59952_8bd3_4330_a62e_fa01b3e86236_"></a>In October 2012, NPC filed
an application with the FERC to reset transmission and ancillary service rates
that were last set in 2003.&#160; The rate changes requested in this filing would
result in an overall annual revenue increase of $11.3 million.&#160; In December
2012, FERC issued an order which suspended certain rate increases until June 1,
2013 and accepted two proposed rate decreases effective January 1, 2013.&#160; All
rates are subject to final approval by FERC in 2013.&#160; </font><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; SPPC</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; SPPC 2012 FERC Transmission Rate Case</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="EHW884bd388_54e1_4ae0_b66e_e4c89c34b8aa"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW884bd388_54e1_4ae0_b66e_e4c89c34b8aa_"></a>In October 2012, SPPC filed
an application with the FERC to reset transmission and ancillary service rates
that were last set in 2007 and 2003, respectively.&#160; The rate changes requested
in this filing would result in an overall annual revenue increase of $3.2
million.&#160; In December 2012, FERC issued an order which suspended certain rate
increases until June 1, 2013 and accepted two proposed rate decreases effective
January 1, 2013.&#160; All rates are subject to final approval by FERC in 2013</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">. &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
amounts for Navajo Generating Station include NPC&#8217;s share of transmission
systems, general plant equipment and NPC&#8217;s share of the jointly owned railroad
which delivers coal to the plant.&#160; Each participant provides its own financing
for all these jointly owned facilities.&#160; NPC&#8217;s share of the operating expenses
for these facilities is included in the corresponding operating expenses in its
consolidated income statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Reid
Gardner Generating Station Unit No. 4 is owned by the CDWR (67.8%) and Nevada
Power Company (32.2%).&#160; Nevada power is operating agent.&#160; Contractually, NPC is
entitled to receive 25 MW of base load capacity and 232 MW of peaking capacity,
subject to certain operating limitations. &#160;NPC's share of the operating
expenses for this facility is included in the corresponding operating expenses
in its consolidated income statements.&#160; In June 2013, NPC will be required to
pay CDWR a termination payment.&#160; After such payment is made, NPC will be 100%
owner of Unit No. 4 and assume 100% of all operating and maintenance costs of
the Unit.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NPC
is the operator of the Silverhawk Generating Station, which is jointly owned
with SNWA.&#160; NPC&#8217;s owns 75% and its share of direct operation and maintenance expenses
is included in its accompanying consolidated income statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">SPPC
and Idaho Power Company each own an undivided 50% interest in the Valmy
Generating Station, with each company being responsible for financing its share
of capital and operating costs.&#160; SPPC is the operating agent of the plant for
both parties.&#160; SPPC&#8217;s share of direct operation and maintenance expenses for
the Valmy Generating Station are in included in its accompanying consolidated
income statements</font><font color=#002060 face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">.&nbsp;</font></p>

<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:.7pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Financing Transactions</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; NVE</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; $195 Million Term Loan
Agreement</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In
October 2011, NVE entered into a $195 million 3-year term loan agreement (Term
Loan).&#160; The Term Loan is an unsecured, single-draw loan that is due on October
7, 2014.&#160; The borrowing under the Term Loan bears interest at the LIBOR rate
plus a margin. The current LIBOR margin rate is 2.00%.&#160;&#160; The margin varies
based upon NVE&#8217;s long&#8211;term unsecured debt credit rating by S&amp;P and
Moody&#8217;s.&#160; However, NVE entered into a floating- for- fixed interest rate swap
agreement to lock in an effective interest rate of 2.81% for the length of the
Term Loan.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
Term Loan contains conditions of borrowing, events of default, and affirmative
and negative covenants.&#160; The Term Loan includes (i) a financial covenant to
maintain a ratio of total consolidated indebtedness to total consolidated
capitalization, determined on the last day of each fiscal quarter, not to
exceed 0.70 to 1.00 and (ii) a fixed charge covenant that requires NVE not to
permit the fixed charge coverage ratio, determined on the last day of each
fiscal quarter, to be less than 1.50 to 1.00.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;
Redemption of 6.75% Senior Notes</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In
November 2011, NVE used the proceeds of the Term Loan, plus cash on hand, to
redeem its unsecured $191.5 million 6.75% Senior Notes (&#8220;Senior Notes&#8221;).&#160; The
notes were redeemed at 102.25% of the stated principal amount plus accrued
interest to the date of redemption.&#160; With this redemption, NVE and the
Utilities are no longer subject to the restrictive covenants contained in the
Senior Notes, which were more restrictive then the covenants described above
for the Term Loan.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; NPC</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; 5.45%
General and Refunding Mortgage Notes, Series Y</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In
May 2011, NPC issued and sold $250 million of its 5.45% General and Refunding
Mortgage Notes, Series Y, due May 15, 2041.&#160; The approximately $248 million in net proceeds, plus a portion of the
proceeds from a draw on NPC&#8217;s revolving credit facility, were utilized to pay
at maturity NPC&#8217;s $350 million aggregate principal amount of 8.25%&#160; General and
Refunding Mortgage Notes, Series A, which matured on June 1, 2011.&#160; In
conjunction with this debt issuance, NPC entered into an interest rate swap
hedging agreement with a notional principal amount of $250 million and a
mandatory termination date of June 1, 2011.&#160; The interest rate swap agreement
was entered into to effectively lock the interest rate of the U.S. Treasury component
of the prospective General and Refunding Note issuance.&#160; The swap transaction
was settled on May 9, 2011, when NPC launched and priced the Series Y Notes,
resulting in a settlement payment amount of $14.9 million, which was recorded
as a cost to issue in a deferred debit and will be amortized over the 30 year
life of the Series Y Notes in accordance with past accounting precedent for our
regulated Utilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;
General and Refunding Mortgage Notes, Series I</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In April 2012, NPC used $120 million from its
revolving credit facility along with $10 million cash on hand to pay for the
maturity of its 6.5% General and Refunding Mortgage Notes, Series I, in an
aggregate principal amount of $130 million.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; $500 Million Revolving Credit
Facility</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In March
2012, NPC terminated its $600 million secured revolving credit facility which
would have expired in April 2013 and replaced it with a $500 million secured
revolving credit facility, for which borrowings mature in 2017.&#160; The fees on
the $500 million revolving credit facility for the unused portion and on the
amounts borrowed have decreased from the prior facility reflecting current
market conditions.&#160; The Administrative Agent for the facility remains Wells Fargo
Bank, N.A., and amounts due under the NPC Credit Agreement are collateralized
by NPC&#8217;s general and refunding mortgage bonds.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
rate for outstanding loans under the revolving credit facility will be at
either an applicable base rate (defined as the highest of the Prime Rate, the
Federal Funds Rate plus 0.5% and the LIBOR Base Rate plus 1.0%) plus a margin,
or a LIBOR rate plus a margin.&#160; The margin varies based upon NPC&#8217;s credit
rating by S&amp;P and Moody&#8217;s.&#160; Currently, NPC&#8217;s applicable base rate margin is
0.25% and the LIBOR rate margin is 1.25 %.&#160; The rate for outstanding letters of
credit will be at the LIBOR rate margin plus a fee for the issuing bank.&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
$500 million revolving credit facility contains a provision which reduces the
availability under the credit facility by the negative mark-to-market exposure
for hedging transactions with credit facility lenders or their energy trading
affiliates.&#160; The reduction </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>
<DIV bclFooter>





<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font><font style="mso-no-proof:yes;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;">134</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font></p>

<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><a name=bcl_connect_prev></a><!-- Do not modify before this point! !--><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">in availability limits the
amount that NPC can borrow or use for letters of credit and would require that
NPC prepay any amount in excess of that limitation.&#160; The amount of the
reduction is calculated by NPC on a monthly basis, and after calculating such
reduction, the NPC Credit Agreement provides that the reduction in availability
under the revolving credit facility to NPC shall in no event exceed 50% of the
total commitments then in effect under the revolving credit facility.&#160;
Currently, there are no negative mark-to-market exposures that would impact
borrowings.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The NPC Credit Agreement contains one financial maintenance
covenant that requires NPC to maintain a ratio of consolidated indebtedness to
consolidated capital, determined as of the last day of each fiscal quarter, not
to exceed 0.68 to 1.&#160; In the event that NPC did not meet the financial
maintenance covenant or there is a different event of default, the NPC Credit
Agreement would restrict dividends to NVE.&#160; Moreover, so long as NPC&#8217;s senior
secured debt remains rated investment grade by S&amp;P and Moody&#8217;s (in each
case, with a stable or better outlook), a representation concerning no material
adverse change in NPC&#8217;s business, assets, property or financial condition would
not be a condition to the availability of credit under the facility.&#160; In the
event that NPC&#8217;s senior secured debt rating were rated below investment grade
by either S&amp;P or Moody&#8217;s, or investment grade by either S&amp;P or Moody&#8217;s
but with a negative outlook, a representation concerning no material adverse
change in NPC&#8217;s business, assets, property or financial condition would be a
condition to borrowing under the revolving credit facility.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
NPC Credit Agreement provides for an event of default if there is a failure
under NPC&#8217;s other financing agreements to meet certain payment terms or to
observe other covenants that would result in an acceleration of payments due.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
NPC Credit Agreement places certain restrictions on debt incurrence, liens and
dividends.&nbsp;&nbsp;These restrictions are discussed in Note 8, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Debt
Covenant and Other Restrictions</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></i><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">SPPC&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; $250
Million Revolving Credit Facility</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In March 2012, SPPC terminated its $250 million
secured revolving credit facility which would have expired in April 2013 and
replaced it with a $250 million secured revolving credit facility, for which
borrowings mature in 2017.&#160; The fees on the $250 million revolving credit
facility for the unused portion and on the amounts borrowed have decreased from
the prior facility reflecting current market conditions.&#160; The Administrative
Agent for the facility is Wells Fargo, N.A., and amounts due under the SPPC
Credit Agreement are collateralized by SPPC&#8217;s general and refunding mortgage
bonds.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The rate for outstanding loans under the revolving
credit facility will be at either an applicable base rate (defined as the
highest of the Prime Rate, the Federal Funds Rate plus 0.5% and the LIBOR Base
Rate plus 1.0%) plus a margin, or a LIBOR rate plus a margin.&#160; The margin
varies based upon SPPC&#8217;s credit rating by S&amp;P and Moody&#8217;s.&#160; Currently,
SPPC&#8217;s applicable base rate margin is 0.25%% and the LIBOR rate margin is 1.25%.&#160;
The rate for outstanding letters of credit will be at the LIBOR rate margin
plus a fee for the issuing bank.&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
$250 million revolving credit facility contains a provision which reduces the
availability under the credit facility by the negative mark-to-market exposure
for hedging transactions with credit facility lenders or their energy trading
affiliates.&#160; The reduction in availability limits the amount that SPPC can
borrow or use for letters of credit and would require that SPPC prepay any
amount in excess of that limitation.&#160; The amount of the reduction is calculated
by SPPC on a monthly basis, and after calculating such reduction, the SPPC
Credit Agreement provides that the reduction in availability under the
revolving credit facility to SPPC shall in no event exceed 50% of the total
commitments then in effect under the revolving credit facility. Currently,
there are no negative mark-to-market exposures that would impact borrowings.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
SPPC Credit Agreement contains one financial maintenance covenant that requires
SPPC to maintain a ratio of consolidated indebtedness to consolidated capital,
determined as of the last day of each fiscal quarter, not to exceed 0.68 to 1.&#160;
In the event that SPPC did not meet the financial maintenance covenant or there
is a different event of default, the SPPC Credit Agreement would restrict
dividends to NVE.&#160; Moreover, so long as SPPC&#8217;s senior secured debt remains
rated investment grade by S&amp;P and Moody&#8217;s (in each case, with a stable or
better outlook), a representation concerning no material adverse change in
SPPC&#8217;s business, assets, property or financial condition would not be a
condition to the availability of credit under the facility.&#160; In the event that
SPPC&#8217;s senior secured debt rating were rated below investment grade by either
S&amp;P or Moody&#8217;s, or investment grade by either S&amp;P or Moody&#8217;s but with a
negative outlook, a representation concerning no material adverse change in
SPPC&#8217;s business, assets, property or financial condition would be a condition
to borrowing under the revolving credit facility.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
SPPC Credit Agreement provides for an event of default if there is a failure
under SPPC&#8217;s other financing agreements to meet certain payment terms or to
observe other covenants that would result in an acceleration of payments due.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTE 7.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name=Fairvalue></a></font></b><a href="#Fairvalue"><b><u><font color=blue face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">FAIR

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The total fair value of SPPC&#8217;s consolidated long-term

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTE 8.<a name="EHW70a5db3b_8632_47da_91d6_7e7ba34c3989"></a>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name=Dcovenant></a><a name="EHWfe1404a6_8571_461f_a343_d22ccbd54bab"></a><a name="EHW70a5db3b_8632_47da_91d6_7e7ba34c3989_"></a></font></b><a href="#Dcovenant"><b><u><font color=blue face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">DEBT COVENANT AND OTHER
RESTRICTIONS</font></u></b></a><a name="EHWfe1404a6_8571_461f_a343_d22ccbd54bab_"></a><a name="Dcovenant_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Dividends from Subsidiaries</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Since NVE is a holding company,
substantially all of its cash flow is provided by dividends paid to NVE by NPC
and SPPC on their common stock, all of which is owned by NVE.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2012,
NPC and SPPC paid $184.0 million and $20.0 million in dividends, respectively,
to NVE.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February 7, 2013, NPC declared dividends to NVE of $50
million to NVE.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Limits on Restricted Payments</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; NVE</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Dividends are considered periodically by
NVE&#8217;s BOD and are subject to factors that ordinarily affect dividend policy,
such as current and prospective earnings, current and prospective business
conditions, regulatory factors, NVE&#8217;s financial conditions and other matters
within the discretion of the BOD, as well as dividend restrictions set forth in
NVE&#8217;s debt.&nbsp;&nbsp;The BOD will continue to review the factors described
above on a periodic basis to determine if and when it is prudent to declare a
dividend on NVE&#8217;s Common Stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;There is no guarantee that dividends
will be paid in the future, or that, if paid; the dividends will be paid at the
same amount or with the same frequency as in the past.&nbsp;&nbsp;In February
2012, NVE declared a cash dividend of $0.13 per share and for each of May,
August and November of 2012, NVE declared a cash dividend of $0.17 per
share.&nbsp;&nbsp;In February, 2013, NVE declared a cash dividend of $0.19 per
share for common stock holders of record as of March 2013.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Dividend
Restrictions Applicable to the Utilities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Since
NVE is a holding company, substantially all of its cash flow is provided by
dividends paid to NVE by NPC and SPPC on their common stock, all of which is
owned by NVE.&nbsp;&nbsp;Since NPC and SPPC are public utilities, they are
subject to regulation by the PUCN, which may impose limits on investment returns
or otherwise impact the amount of dividends that the Utilities may declare and
pay.&nbsp; While the PUCN has in the past imposed a dividend restriction with
respect to NPC and SPPC, as of December 31, 2012, there were no dividend
restrictions imposed on the Utilities by the PUCN.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;In addition, certain
agreements entered into by the Utilities set restrictions on the amount of
dividends they may declare and pay and restrict the circumstances under which
such dividends may be declared and paid.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of the
Utilities&#8217; credit rating on their senior secured debt being rated investment
grade by S&amp;P and Moody&#8217;s, these restrictions are suspended and no longer in
effect so long as such debt remains investment grade by both rating
agencies.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to the restrictions imposed by specific
agreements, the Federal Power Act prohibits the payment of dividends from
&#8220;capital accounts.&#8221;&nbsp;&nbsp;Although the meaning of this provision is
unclear, </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name=bcl_connect_prev></a><!-- Do not modify before this point! !--><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">the Utilities believe that the Federal Power
Act restriction, as applied to their particular circumstances, would not be
construed or applied by the FERC to prohibit the payment of dividends for
lawful and legitimate business purposes from current year earnings, or in the
absence of current year earnings, from other/additional paid-in capital
accounts.&nbsp;&nbsp;If, however, the FERC were to interpret this provision
differently, the ability of the Utilities to pay dividends to NVE could be
jeopardized.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Ability to Issue Debt</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp; NVE</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Certain debt of NVE contain conditions of
borrowing, events of default, and affirmative and negative covenants.&#160; The most
restrictive of which is the Term Loan, which includes (i) a financial covenant
to maintain a ratio of total consolidated indebtedness to total consolidated
capitalization, determined on the last day of each fiscal quarter, not to
exceed 0.70 to 1.00 and (ii) a fixed charge covenant that requires NVE not to
permit the fixed charge coverage ratio, determined on the last day of each
fiscal quarter, to be less than 1.50 to 1.00.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;Under these covenant restrictions,
as of December 31, 2012, NVE (consolidated) would be allowed to incur up to $3.3 billion of additional indebtedness, which
includes the use of the Utilities revolving credit facilities.&#160; The amount of
additional indebtedness allowed would likely be impacted if there is a change
in current market conditions or material change in our financial condition.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; NPC</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.55in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC&#8217;s ability to issue debt is impacted by
certain factors such as financing authority from the PUCN, financial covenants
in its financing agreements and revolving credit facility agreements, and the
terms of NVE&#8217;s Term Loan.&#160; As of December 31, 2012, the most restrictive of the
factors below is the PUCN authority.&nbsp; As such, NPC may issue up to $725</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> </font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">million in long-term debt,
in addition to the use of its existing credit facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;However,
depending on NVE&#8217;s or SPPC&#8217;s issuance of long-term debt or the use of the
Utilities&#8217; revolving credit facilities, the PUCN authority may not remain the
most restrictive factor.&nbsp;&nbsp;The factors affecting NPC&#8217;s ability to
issue debt are further detailed below:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.55in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:62.2pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-25.5pt;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">a.</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financing authority
from the PUCN - As of December 31, 2012, NPC has financing authority from the
PUCN for the period ending December 31, 2013, consisting of authority: (1) to
issue additional long-term debt securities of up to $725 million; (2) to
refinance up to approximately $322.5 million of long-term debt securities; and
(3) ongoing authority to maintain a revolving credit facility of up to $1.3
billion.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:62.6pt;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><a name="EHW048ea8bc_1fe5_4db3_a385_1f92042f3b53"></a><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW048ea8bc_1fe5_4db3_a385_1f92042f3b53_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:62.2pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-25.5pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">b.</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial covenants
within NPC&#8217;s financing agreements &#8211; Under its $500 million revolving credit
facility, NPC must maintain a ratio of consolidated indebtedness to
consolidated capital, determined as of the last day of each fiscal quarter, not
to exceed 0.68 to 1.&#160; Based on December 31, 2012 financial statements, NPC was
in compliance with this covenant and could incur up to $2.9 billion of
additional indebtedness. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:62.6pt;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><a name="EHWab2c6204_06e0_4dd7_aac8_fa01d998626c"></a><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHWab2c6204_06e0_4dd7_aac8_fa01d998626c_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:62.6pt;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><a name="EHW286fb5e8_1044_43b8_bd1c_ac6e53e56599"></a><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW286fb5e8_1044_43b8_bd1c_ac6e53e56599_"></a>&#160;All other financial covenants contained in NPC&#8217;s financing
agreements are currently suspended; as NPC&#8217;s senior secured debt is rated
investment grade.&#160; However, if NPC&#8217;s senior secured debt ratings fall below
investment grade by either Moody&#8217;s or S&amp;P, NPC would again be subject to
the limitations under these additional covenants; and </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:62.6pt;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><a name="EHWa6eb0034_d1bb_4fd8_8557_740b6eedca65"></a><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHWa6eb0034_d1bb_4fd8_8557_740b6eedca65_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:62.6pt;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">c.<a name="EHW5a4acdf1_e455_477e_8c12_a53a4d5eba92"></a>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW5a4acdf1_e455_477e_8c12_a53a4d5eba92_"></a>&#160;&#160; </font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial
covenants within NVE&#8217;s Term Loan &#8211; As discussed in NVE&#8217;s </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Ability to Issue
Debt</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, NPC is also subject to NVE&#8217;s cap on additional consolidated
indebtedness of $3.3 billion.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-indent:.55in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;Ability to Issue General and Refunding Mortgage Securities</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">To the extent that NPC has the ability to
issue debt under the most restrictive covenants in its financing agreements and
has financing authority to do so from the PUCN, NPC&#8217;s ability to issue secured
debt is still limited by the amount of bondable property or retired bonds that
can be used to issue debt under NPC&#8217;s Indenture.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC&#8217;s Indenture creates a lien on substantially all of
NPC&#8217;s properties in Nevada.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2012, $3.8 billion of
NPC&#8217;s General and Refunding Mortgage Securities were
outstanding.&nbsp;&nbsp;NPC had the capacity to issue $1.6 billion of
additional General and Refunding Mortgage Securities as of December 31,
2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;That amount is determined on the basis of:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:31.5pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">1.<a name="EHWb7cacfe8_df11_4d3d_b55d_3ed6ff35417f"></a>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHWb7cacfe8_df11_4d3d_b55d_3ed6ff35417f_"></a>70% of net utility property
additions; and/or</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:31.5pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">2.<a name="EHWc31633ad_bf00_4354_a456_4cb87fc4cf81"></a>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHWc31633ad_bf00_4354_a456_4cb87fc4cf81_"></a>The principal amount of
retired General and Refunding Mortgage Securities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="display:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financing authority

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:58.3pt;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><a name="EHWbcdcd2bf_ddce_444a_a10a_2483f908c46d"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHWbcdcd2bf_ddce_444a_a10a_2483f908c46d_"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">For
balance sheet presentation, the regulatory tax asset is included in regulatory
assets and the regulatory tax liability is included in regulatory
liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;The regulatory tax asset balance consists of future
revenue to be received from customers due to flow-through of the tax benefits
of temporary differences and goodwill recognized from the merger of NPC and
NVE.&nbsp;&nbsp;Offset against these amounts are future revenues to be refunded
to customers (regulatory tax liabilities).&nbsp;&nbsp;The regulatory tax
liability balance consists of temporary differences for liberalized
depreciation at rates in excess of current rates and unamortized investment tax
credits.&nbsp;&nbsp;The regulatory liability for temporary differences related
to liberalized depreciation will continue to be amortized using the average
rate assumption method required by the Tax Reform Act of 1986.&nbsp;&nbsp;The
regulatory liability for temporary differences caused by the investment tax
credit will be amortized ratably similar to the accumulated deferred investment
tax credit.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:10.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">At December 31, 2012, NVE has a gross
Federal NOL carryover of $1.1 billion, NPC of $723.7 million and SPPC of $161.1
million.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:10.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Considering all positive and negative
evidence regarding the utilization of NVE&#8217;s and the Utilities&#8217; deferred tax
assets, it has been determined that NVE, NPC and SPPC are more-likely-than-not
to realize all recorded deferred tax assets, except the Arizona coal credits on
NVE and NPC.&nbsp;&nbsp;As such, these Arizona coal credits represent the only
valuation allowance that has been recorded as of December 31, 2012 on NVE and
NPC.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:10.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Accounting for Uncertainty in Income Taxes</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under Accounting
for Uncertainty in Income Taxes, as reflected in the FASC, uncertain tax
liabilities are all long-term and are included in the &#8220;other deferred credits
and liabilities&#8221; line item on the balance sheet.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

31 are as follows (dollars in millions)</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">:&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">On
September 15, 2012, NVE and the Utilities filed a Form 3115, Application for
Change in Accounting Method, with the IRS requesting a change in method of
accounting for routine repair and maintenance costs deductible under &#167;162 to
use the Transmission and Distribution Property Safe Harbor Method of Accounting
as required by Rev. Proc. 2011-43.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NVE
and the Utilities classify interest and penalties related to income taxes as
interest and other expense, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp; NVE and the Utilities
have not accrued interest or penalties as of December 31, 2012, December 31,
2011 and December 31, 2010.&nbsp;&nbsp;NVE and the Utilities do not expect
unrecognized tax benefits to change within the next twelve months.&#160;&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NVE
and its subsidiaries file a consolidated federal income tax
return.&nbsp;&nbsp;Current income taxes are allocated based on NVE&#8217;s and each
subsidiaries&#8217; respective taxable income or loss and tax credits as if each
subsidiary filed a separate return.&#160; The U.S. federal jurisdiction is the only
&#8220;significant&#8221; tax jurisdiction for NVE.&#160; In July 2012, the IRS concluded their
examination of NVE with respect to its Federal income tax returns for December
31, 2005 through December 31, 2008.&#160; The audit is currently under review by the
Joint Committee on Taxation.&#160;&#160; As of December 31, 2012, NVE is no longer
subject to examinations by U.S. federal, state, or local tax authorities for
years before 2008, with a few exceptions</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>








<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTE
10.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name=Retirement></a></font></b><a href="#Retirement"><b><u><font color=blue face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">RETIREMENT PLAN AND
POSTRETIREMENT BENEFITS</font></u></b></a></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><a name="Retirement_bclEnd"></a><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&#160;</font></b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE has a single employer defined benefit pension plan
covering substantially all employees of NVE and the Utilities.&#160; NVE allocates
the unfunded liability and the net periodic benefit costs for its pension
benefit and other postretirement benefit plans to NPC and SPPC based upon the
current, or in the case of the retirees, previous, employment location.&#160; Certain
grandfathered and union employees are covered under a benefit formula based on
years of service and the employee's highest compensation for a period prior to
retirement, while most employees are covered under a cash balance formula with
vesting after three years of service. &#160;NVE also has other postretirement plans,
including a defined contribution plan which provides medical and life insurance
benefits for certain retired employees. </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Plan Changes</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2012, NVE offered a
voluntary lump sum pension payout to former employees not currently of
retirement age but eligible for future benefits and certain retiree
participants already receiving benefits under NVE&#8217;s pension plan in an effort
to reduce NVE&#8217;s future pension obligation.&#160; The 2012 payouts, as indicated in
the benefits obligations table below, increased benefits paid by approximately
$28.9 million.&#160; Of the offers still outstanding at December 31, 2012, NVE
expects to payout an additional lump sum of approximately $15.6 million from
the pension assets during 2013. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2011, the sale of
California Assets, as discussed in detail in Note 15, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Assets Held for Sale</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">,
resulted in employees being transferred to CalPeco.&#160; Certain employees who did
not want to transfer, and who could not obtain comparable positions with NVE,
had their service periods bridged to retirement age under the terms of the
collective bargaining agreement with IBEW 1245.&#160; Amounts recorded for this
event were not material.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE also has a non-qualified
Supplemental Executive Retirement Plan and a Restoration Plan for executives.
NVE contributed $26.5 million to establish a rabbi trust for these plans in
2009.&#160; See Note 4, </font><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Investments in Subsidiaries and Other Property</font></i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, for
details regarding the trust assets.&#160; NVE&#8217;s obligation under these supplemental
and restoration plans is included in &#8220;Accrued retirement benefits&#8221; in NVE&#8217;s
consolidated balance sheet, and amounted to $36.1 million at December 31, 2012.
NVE is not required to make contributions to the plans.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>
