<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Plan Assets</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;line-height:normal;">NVE&#8217;s investment strategy is to ensure the safety of the
principal of the assets and obtain asset performance to meet the continuing
obligations of the plan.&#160; NVE contributed a total of $22.1 million and $40.6
million in 2012 and 2011, respectively, towards the qualified pension and other
postretirement benefit plans.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;line-height:normal;">NVE strives to maintain a reasonable and prudent amount
of risk, and seeks to limit risk through diversification of assets.&#160; Also, NVE
considers the ability of the plan to pay all benefit and expense obligations
when due, and to control the costs of administering and managing the plan.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NVE&#8217;s
long term strategy for the pension plan assets is to maximize risk adjusted
returns while maintaining adequate liquidity to pay plan benefits.&#160; NVE is
committed to prudent investments with ample diversification in terms of asset
types, fund strategies, and investment managers.&#160; As such, NVE has elected to
include an appropriate mix of indexed and actively managed investments to
accomplish its strategy.&#160; The allocation for pension plan net assets at
December 31, 2012 is 61% fixed income, 26% U.S. equity, 7% international equity
and 6% cash.&#160; The allocation for pension plan net assets at December 31, 2011
is 61% fixed income, 19% U.S. equity, 14% international equity, 5% cash and 1%
other.&#160; The long-term target allocation for pension plan net assets is 65%
fixed income, 20% U.S. equity, and 15% international equity.&#160; The fixed income
investments are benchmarked against government and corporate credit bond
indices.&#160; U.S. equity investments include large cap, mid-cap, and small-cap
companies with an emphasis towards small and mid-cap investments relative to
the Russell 3000 Index.&#160; International equity is currently actively managed and
includes investments in both established and emerging markets.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
allocation for the other postretirement benefit plan net assets at December 31,
2012 is 49% equity securities, 48% fixed income and 3% cash.&#160; The allocation
for other postretirement benefit plan net assets at December 31, 2011 is 51%
equity securities, 46% fixed income and 3% cash.&#160; The long-term strategy for
the other postretirement benefit plan net assets is similar to the pension plan
net assets strategy as described above.&#160; The target allocation for other
postretirement benefit assets is 60% equity and 40% fixed income. The equity is
invested in indexed securities that track the S&amp;P 500 Index.&#160; The fixed
income is indexed and benchmarked against government and corporate credit bond
indices.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:61.9pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">(1)</font></sup><a name="EHWc911bb95_870f_44dc_84db_3ac57d7e5582"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHWc911bb95_870f_44dc_84db_3ac57d7e5582_"></a>Cash and cash equivalents consist of investment in commingled funds that
are primarily comprised of money market holdings and marketable securities,
U.S. Treasury bills and commercial paper valued and redeemable at cost. </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:61.9pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">(2)</font></sup><a name="EHW2e34524e_2923_4fb1_809c_1ee6114a4c48"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW2e34524e_2923_4fb1_809c_1ee6114a4c48_"></a>This category includes approximately 27% small and mid-cap and 73% broad
market domestic equity investments. </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:61.9pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">(3)</font></sup><a name="EHWeb306590_868a_4441_8d53_74e76c172e64"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHWeb306590_868a_4441_8d53_74e76c172e64_"></a>This category includes approximately 26% small and mid-cap and 74% broad
market domestic equity investments.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:61.9pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">(4)</font></sup><a name="EHWec2d1687_aac7_4994_9128_6caaf185a462"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHWec2d1687_aac7_4994_9128_6caaf185a462_"></a>Level 1 investments are comprised of fixed income securities that
primarily invest in U.S. Treasury bonds.&#160; Level 2 investments consist of
commingled funds that track the Barclays Capital Long Government and Corporate
Credit Index and the Barclays Capital Aggregate US Fixed Income Index. </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:61.9pt;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-25.9pt;"><sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;">(5)</font></sup><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:8.0pt;line-height:normal;"> <a name="EHW1d736672_f80b_4abe_869a_77d0cd2de4f4"></a>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name="EHW1d736672_f80b_4abe_869a_77d0cd2de4f4_"></a>The administrative trust
net assets/liabilities are primarily comprised of amounts payable to and from
brokers for sold and purchased securities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The discount rates for 2012 and
2011 related to the benefit obligations were determined by identifying a
theoretical settlement portfolio of high quality corporate bonds sufficient to
provide for the plans projected benefit payments.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
discount rates for 2012 related to the net periodic benefit costs were
determined by identifying a theoretical settlement portfolio of high quality
corporate bonds sufficient to provide for the plans projected benefit payments.
However, to determine the discount rates for 2011 and 2010 related to the net
periodic benefit costs, NVE&#8217;s projected benefit payments were matched to the
yield curve derived from a portfolio of over 300 high quality Aa bonds with
yields within the 10th to 90th percentiles of these bond yields.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Assumed
health care cost trend rates have a significant effect on the amounts reported
for the health care plans. A one-percentage-point change in assumed health care
cost trend rates would have the following effect</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">: &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The expected ROR on plan assets was determined by
considering a realistic projection of what assets can earn, given existing
capital market conditions, historical equity and bond premiums over inflation,
the effect of &#8220;normative&#8221; economic conditions that may differ from existing
conditions, and projected ROR on reinvested assets.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.25in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; There were no significant
transactions between the plan and the employer or related parties during 2012,
2011, or 2010.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NOTE 11.&nbsp;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <a name=Stock></a></font></b><a href="#Stock"><b><u><font color=blue face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">STOCK COMPENSATION PLANS</font></u></b></a><a name="Stock_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE&#8217;s executive long-term incentive plan for key management
employees, which was approved by shareholders in May 2004 and amended and
restated in 2011, provides for the issuance of up to 7,750,000 of NVE&#8217;s shares
to key employees through December 31, 2013.&#160; The plan permits the following
types of grants, separately or in combination: nonqualified and qualified stock
options, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock units, performance units,
performance shares, and bonus stock. During 2012, NVE granted restricted stock
units, performance units and performance shares under the long-term incentive
plan.&#160; The Company also has an employee stock purchase plan which is available
to all employees who meet minimum service requirements.&#160; The employees can
choose to have amounts deducted from their paychecks which will be used to buy
NVE&#8217;s common stock at a discount.&#160; The plans are discussed in more detail
below.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the long-term incentive plan and employee stock
purchase plan, NVE may settle awards by either new issuances of shares, open
market purchases, or issuance of treasury shares.&#160; See Note 13, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Common Stock
and Other Paid-In Capital, </font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">for further discussion on treasury stock.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Total stock-based
compensation expense for the following years was as follows (dollars in
thousands)</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">: &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Non-Qualified
Stock Options</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Elected officers and key employees specifically designated by
a committee of the BOD are eligible to be awarded non-qualified stock options
(NQSO&#8217;s) based on the guidelines in the plan. These grants are at 100% of the
then current fair market value, and vest over different periods as stated in
the grant. These options have to be exercised within ten years of award, and no
earlier than one year from the date of grant.&#160; At the time of grant, rights to
dividend equivalents may be awarded; however, historically, dividend
equivalents have not been granted.&#160; The options may be exercised using either
cash or previously acquired shares valued at the current market price, or a
combination of both.&#160; The Committee also allows cashless exercises, subject to
applicable securities law restrictions or other means consistent with the
purpose of the plan and the applicable law.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">There have been no grants of non-qualified stock options made
to employees since 2007.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">A summary of the status
of NVE&#8217;s nonqualified stock option plan as of December 31, 2012, 2011, and
2010, and changes during the year is presented below</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">:&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

million and $0.5 million in 2012, 2011 and 2010, respectively.&#160; The tax benefit
realized for the tax deductions from option exercises was immaterial for all
years.&#160; The fair value of options vested was zero for all years presented.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The fair value of each nonqualified option has been estimated
on the date of grant using the Black-Scholes option pricing model using the
following assumptions: Average Dividend Yield, Average Expected Volatility,
Average Risk-Free Rate of Return, and Average Expected Life.&#160; As of January 1,
2011 all of the nonqualified stock options have been fully vested and expensed.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:10.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:115%;">Performance
Awards </font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:10.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:115%;">&#160;&#160; Performance
Units</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Performance Units vest at the end of a three-year
period to the extent that specific stock price related performance targets are
met, as determined by the Compensation Committee.&#160; If the established
objectives are not met, the Performance Units are forfeited.&#160; Performance Units
are typically paid in shares after vesting.&#160; At the time of grant, rights to
dividend equivalents may be awarded; however, historically, dividend
equivalents have not been granted.&#160; These awards do not have any voting rights
associated with them.&#160;&#160; Performance Units granted are measured based on NVE&#8217;s
TSR relative to the average TSR of companies listed in the S&amp;P Super
Composite Electric Utility Index throughout the three-year performance
period.&#160;&#160; The Committee determined that the awards will vest according to the
table shown below (a proportionate amount of shares will vest in the case of
performance between the percentiles listed below)</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">:&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:10.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><i><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:115%;">&#160;&#160; </font></i><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:115%;">Performance
Shares</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Performance
Shares vest at the end of a three-year period, based on average aggregate
Corporate Goal performance under the Short Term Incentive Plan (STIP) and the
average STIP payout over those three years.&#160; If the established objectives are
not met, the Performance Shares are forfeited.&#160; Performance Shares are paid in
shares, minus applicable taxes, based on the then fair market value of the
shares.&#160; At the time of grant, rights to dividend equivalents may be awarded;
however, historically, dividend equivalents have not been granted.&#160;&#160;
Performance shares do not have any voting rights associated with them.</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160; &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:10.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:115%;">There were no performance units or
performance shares issued in 2010.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Compensation
expense for performance units and performance shares is recognized ratably over
the three year vesting period.&#160; In the event the conditional criteria are not
met, the awards are forfeited and the expense is reversed.&#160; Performance units
and performance shares are accounted for as liability awards and compensation
costs are measured at each balance sheet date using the Company&#8217;s closing stock
price for that date.&#160; The closing trading price of NVE stock on December 31,
2012 was $18.14. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Restricted
Stock Units</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Elected officers and key employees specifically designated by
a committee of the BOD are eligible to be awarded restricted stock units based
on the guidelines in the plan. These grants vest over different periods as
stated within the terms of each grant.&#160; The issuance of these shares is
conditional upon the employee retaining employment with NVE throughout the
entire vesting period.&#160; Of the 169,000 units granted in 2012, 125,000 are
eligible for dividend equivalents over the vesting period.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">There
were no restricted stock units issued in 2010.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Compensation
expense for restricted stock units is recognized ratably over the vesting
period of each grant.&#160; If employment is terminated prior to the end of the
vesting period, the award is forfeited and the expense is reversed.&#160; Restricted
stock units are accounted for as liability awards and compensation costs are
measured at each balance sheet date using the Company&#8217;s closing stock price for
that date.&#160; The closing trading price of NVE stock on December 31, 2012 was
$18.14. </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Employee Stock Purchase Plan</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The employee stock purchase plan is
available to all employees who meet minimum service requirements.&#160; In 2010,
shareholders approved an additional 1,000,000 shares for distribution under the
plan, bringing the total authorized up to an aggregate of 1,900,162 shares of
common stock.&#160; According to the terms of the plan, employees can choose twice
each year to have up to 15% of their base earnings withheld to purchase NVE&#8217;s
common stock. The option price discount is 15%, and the purchase price is the
lesser of 85% of the market value on the offering commencement date, or 85% of
the market value on the offering exercise date. Employees can withdraw from the
plan at any time prior to the exercise date. Under the plan NVE sold 134,069,
134,266 and 147,457 shares to employees in 2012, 2011 and 2010, respectively. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In accordance with the Stock Compensation Topic of the FASC,
NVE recognized compensation expense in 2012, 2011 and 2010 related to the
employee stock purchase plan.&#160; The expense for 2012 was calculated for the
employees&#8217; purchase rights based on the stock price at the exercise date.&#160; The
expense for 2011 and 2010 was estimated for the employees&#8217; purchase rights on
the date of grant, using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model.&#160; The following
assumptions were used for those years, with an option life of six months</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">:&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Purchased Power </font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; The
Utilities have several contracts for long-term purchase of electric energy; the
expiration of these contracts range from 2013 to 2039</font><font color=red face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">.&#160;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">While the Utilities are not required to make payment if power is not
delivered under these contracts, estimated future payments are included in the
tables above.&#160;&#160; Related party purchase power agreements have been eliminated
from the NVE totals for the year 2013. </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Purchased
Power - Not Commercially Operable</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; The
Utilities entered into several contracts for long-term purchase of electric
energy in which the facility remains under development.&#160; This represents the
estimated payments under renewable energy power purchase contracts, which have
been approved by the PUCN and are contingent upon the developers obtaining
commercial operation and their ability to deliver power.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Coal &amp; Natural Gas</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; The
Utilities have several long-term contracts for the purchase of coal and natural
gas; the expiration of these contracts range from 2013 to 2019.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Transportation</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The
Utilities have several long-term contracts for the transport of coal and
natural gas.&#160; Also included in the transportation obligations is the TUA with
GBT, of which NPC will be responsible for 95% and SPPC 5%.&#160; The TUA remains
contingent upon final construction costs, and reaching commercial operation.&#160;
The expiration of these transportation contracts range from 2013 to 2054.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Long-Term Service Agreements</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></i></b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">The Utilities have long term service agreements for
the performance of maintenance on generation units.&#160; Obligation amounts are
based on estimated usage.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Capital Projects</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Capital
projects at NPC includes NPC&#8217;s requirement to purchase the CDWR&#8217;s share of the
undepreciated cost of capital of Reid Gardner Generating Station Unit No. 4 in
2013 (see Note 5, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Jointly Owned Properties</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">), at which time NPC will be
required to assume all associated operating and maintenance costs for the
Unit.&#160; Additionally, the Utilities have obligations regarding the construction
of ON Line, of which NPC will be responsible for 95% and SPPC 5%.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Operating Leases</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; The
Utilities have entered into various non-cancelable operating leases primarily
for building, land and equipment.&#160; Contract expiration dates range from 2013 to
2103.&#160; NVE&#8217;s rent payments meeting the above described criteria for 2012 and 2011
were $2.4 million and $2.4 million respectively.&#160; Prior to 2011, NVE did not
have non-cancelable operating leases that were material.&#160; NPC&#8217;s rent payments
meeting the above described criteria for 2012, 2011 and 2010 were $9.6 million,
$11.5 million and $13.6 million respectively.&#160;&#160; SPPC&#8217;s rent payments meeting
the above described criteria for 2012, 2011 and 2010 were $5.8 million, $7.4
million and $14.0 million respectively</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">. &nbsp;</font></p>

<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Environmental</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; NEICO </font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NEICO, a
wholly-owned subsidiary of NPC, owns property in Wellington, Utah, which was
the site of a coal washing and load-out facility. The site has a reclamation
estimate supported by a bond of approximately $5 million with the Utah Division
of Oil and Gas Mining, which management believes is sufficient to cover
reclamation costs. Management is continuing to evaluate various options for
this property going forward, including reclamation or sale to a third party.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Reid Gardner Generating Station </font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October 4,
2011, NPC received a request for information from the EPA-Region 9 under
Section 114 of the Federal Clean Air Act requesting current and historical
operations and capital project information for NPC&#8217;s Reid Gardner Generating
Station located near Moapa, Nevada. NPC operates the facility and owns Units
1-3. Unit 4 of the facility is co-owned with the California Department of Water
Resources. The EPA&#8217;s Section 114 information request does not allege any
incidents of non-compliance at the plant. NPC completed its responses to EPA
during the first quarter of 2012 and will continue to monitor developments
relating to this Section 114 request. At this time, NPC cannot predict the
impact, if any, associated with this information request.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SPPC&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Valmy Generating
Station</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">On June 22, 2009,
SPPC received a request for information from the EPA-Region 9 under Section 114
of the federal Clean Air Act requesting current and historical operations and
capital project information for SPPC&#8217;s Valmy Generating Station located in Valmy,
Nevada. SPPC co-owns and operates this coal-fired plant. Idaho Power Company
owns the remaining 50%. The EPA&#8217;s Section 114 information request does not
allege any incidents of non-compliance at the plant, and there have been no
other new enforcement-related proceedings that have been initiated by the EPA
relating to the plant. SPPC completed its response to the EPA in December 2009
and will continue to monitor developments relating to this Section 114 request.
At this time, SPPC cannot predict the impact, if any, associated with this
information request.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; NPC and SPPC</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Regional Haze Rules&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2005, the EPA finalized amendments to its Regional Haze Rules
that require the installation and operation of emission controls, known as best
available retrofit technology (BART), for industrial facilities emitting air
pollutants that reduce visibility in certain national parks and wilderness
areas throughout the U.S. Certain NVE generating facilities are subject to BART
requirements. Pursuant to the EPA&#8217;s Regional Haze Rules, individual states were
required to identify the facilities located in their states that will have to
reduce sulfur dioxide (SO2), nitrogen oxide (NOx) and particulate matter
emissions under BART and then set emissions limits for those facilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=#151515 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=#151515 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June 2011, the EPA </font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">published in the Federal Register its
proposal </font><font color=#151515 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">to approve
Nevada's State Implementation Plan (SIP) implementing the Regional Haze Rules
for affected units in the State of Nevada, which includes units at our Reid
Gardner, Tracy and Ft. Churchill Generating Stations.&#160; </font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">However, in March 2012, the EPA approved
Nevada&#8217;s SIP as it pertains to all affected units and emissions, except for NOx
controls at Units 1-3 at the Reid Gardner Generating Station.&#160; The specified
compliance date for this action, which includes the affected Tracy and Ft.
Churchill Generating Station units, is January 1, 2015.&#160; In that same March
2012 Federal Register notice, the EPA stated that it intended to make a BART
determination on those Reid Gardner Generating Station Units at a later date.&#160;
In August 2012, the EPA published its final determination for NOx BART controls
for the Reid Gardner Generating Station Units 1-3, approving and rejecting
certain components of Nevada&#8217;s SIP.&#160; For the limited portions of Nevada&#8217;s SIP
that EPA rejected, it put in place a Federal Implementation Plan (FIP) that
will remain enforceable until such time as Nevada submits a revised SIP to
address the concerns the EPA noted in its August 2012 Federal Register notice.&#160;
Within the August 2012 notice, the EPA approved Nevada&#8217;s determination in its
SIP that the installation of selective non-catalytic reduction technology
(SNCR) represented BART for purposes of compliance with the Regional Haze Rule,
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">with a specified compliance date of
January 1, 2015.</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:1.75pt;"> </font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October 19,
2012, NPC submitted to EPA a Petition for Reconsideration of the August 2012
final rule requesting EPA to reconsider the compliance deadline so that it be
set no earlier than June 30, 2016, which would match the modified compliance
data put forward by the State of Nevada.&nbsp; The modified State&#8217;s compliance
date of 2016 also applies to SPPC.&#160; Since filing of the Petition for </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>

<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name=bcl_connect_prev></a><!-- Do not modify before this point! !--><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Reconsideration, NPC has participated in various
discussions with EPA regarding the compliance date.&nbsp; A final decision from
EPA on the Petition for Reconsideration remains pending. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE continues to work toward
finalizing the retrofit designs for the affected BART units.&#160; NVE filed and has
already received approval from the PUCN to retire Tracy Generating Station
Units 1 and 2, and install retrofit controls on Tracy Generating Station Unit 3
and Ft. Churchill Generating Station Units 1 and 2.&#160; NVE intends to also file
with the PUCN the request to install SNCRs on Reid Gardner Generating Station
Units 1, 2 &amp; 3.&#160; Compliance with the Regional Haze Rules are estimated to
cost approximately </font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">$77.1 million,
excluding AFUDC, over the next several years; however, these costs are
preliminary and subject to change based on final engineering analysis and
retirement of generating station units.&#160; NVE expects that costs incurred to
comply with the Regional Haze Rules would be capitalized and recovered through
the Utilities&#8217; regulatory proceedings similar to other environmental compliance
requirements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Environmental groups have challenged both
of the EPA&#8217;s final determinations with respect to Nevada&#8217;s regional haze SIP
submittal.&#160; In May 2012, WildEarth Guardians petitioned the Ninth Circuit to
review the EPA&#8217;s March 2012 approval of Nevada&#8217;s SIP for all affected units and
emissions except NOx controls at the Reid Gardner Generating Station, alleging
that the EPA&#8217;s approval did not conform to the requirements set forth in the
Regional Haze Rule.&#160; NVE has intervened in that lawsuit.&#160; In October 2012,
Earthjustice, on behalf of the Moapa Band of Paiute Indians, Sierra Club, and
the National Parks Conservation Association, petitioned the Ninth Circuit to
review the EPA&#8217;s August 2012 final determinations pertaining to NOx controls at
the Reid Gardner Generating Station.&#160; NVE has intervened in this lawsuit.&#160; At
this time management is unable to determine the likelihood of success by
petitioners in these litigation matters.&#160; An adverse decision in either lawsuit
could impact our compliance strategy for the Tracy, Ft. Churchill and Reid
Gardner Generating Stations, and could result in the requirement to install
more stringent emissions controls, or the retirement of certain units earlier
than currently planned.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Mercury
and Air Toxics Standards (MATS) </font></i></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">In December 2011, the EPA signed for publication in
the Federal Register</font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;"> </font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">a final rule regulating hazardous air pollutant (HAP)
emissions from coal- and oil-fired electric utility steam generating units.&#160;
The rule, referred to as the MATS rule requires coal- and oil-fired electric
utility steam generating units to meet HAP emission standards reflecting the
application of the maximum achievable control technology (MACT). The final MATS
rule (previously referred to as the Utility MACT Rule) was published in the
Federal Register on February 16, 2012. The final rule establishes emission
limits for hazardous air pollutants from new and existing coal-fired and
oil-fired steam electric generating units. The rule requires sources to comply
with the emission limits by April 16, 2015, with a potential one year
compliance extension available for sources that are unable to complete the
installation of emission controls before the compliance deadline. Numerous
petitions for review of the final MATS rule have been filed with the United
States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia. The court has established
a schedule for the litigation that has final briefs being filed as soon as in
April, 2013.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The final rule
does not specifically list control technologies that are required to achieve
the MATS emission standards.&#160; Coal- and oil-fired electric generating units are
required to meet the applicable HAP emission limits using whatever control
technology, or combination of technologies, they deem appropriate for their
specific situation. In general, control technology requirements will be a
function of the fuel being fired and the performance of existing air pollution
control systems. Based on a review of emissions data available from NVE&#8217;s
generating units, as well as emissions data available from EPA for similar
sources, the Utilities anticipate that SO<sub>2 </sub>and/or acid gas reduction
will be required at SPPC&#8217;s Valmy Generating Station, Unit 1 to achieve
compliance with the MATS standards.&#160; At the present time, SPPC believes a dry
sorbent injection system will be selected as the final control option for Unit
1, at an estimated capital cost for SPPC&#8217;s 50% ownership interest of approximately
$6.4 million, excluding AFUDC.&#160; Note that the actual cost will be dependent
upon final engineering design. </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:.05pt;">o</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">n</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.05pt;">s</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-top:.55pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;line-height:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2008, NPC
signed an Administrative Order of Consent (AOC) as owner and operator of Reid
Gardner Generating Station Unit Nos. 1, 2 and 3 and as co-owner and operating
agent of Unit No. 4. Based on the AOC, in 2008, NPC recorded estimated ARO and
capital remediation costs. However, actual costs of work under the AOC may vary
significantly once the scope of work is defined and additional site
characterization has been completed.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE and the
Utilities seek to continually comply with environmental regulations; however,
given the uncertainties involved in the federal, state and local regulatory
environment, future costs to comply may be material.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Litigation Contingencies</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="_DV_C2"></a><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Peabody Western Coal Company &#8211; Royalty Claim </font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NPC owns an 11% interest in the Navajo Generating
Station, which is located in northern Arizona and operated by Salt River
Project (SRP). Other participants in the Navajo Generating Station are Arizona
Public Service Company, Los Angeles Department of Water and Power and Tucson
Electric Power Company (together with SRP and NPC, the &#8220;Navajo Joint Owners&#8221;).
NPC also owns a 14% interest in the Mohave Generating Station which is located
in Laughlin, Nevada and was operated by Southern California Edison (SCE) prior
to the time it became non-operational on December 31, 2005. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June 1999, the Navajo Nation filed suit against SRP,
several Peabody Coal Company entities (collectively referred to as &#8220;Peabody&#8221;)
and SCE in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia (the &#8220;DC
Lawsuit&#8221;).&#160; NPC was not a party to the DC Lawsuit although, as noted above, it
is a participant in both the Navajo Generating Station and the Mohave
Generating Station.</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;"> </font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The DC Lawsuit asserted claims relating to the
renegotiation of coal royalty and lease agreements and alleged, among other
things, that the defendants obtained a favorable coal royalty rate for leases under
which Peabody mined coal for both the Navajo Generating Station and Mohave Generating
Station by improperly influencing the outcome of a federal administrative
process.&#160; The DC Lawsuit sought $600 million in damages and punitive damages of
not less than $1.0 billion.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2004, Peabody brought suit against the Navajo Joint
Owners in state court in St. Louis, Missouri, seeking a declaration that the
Navajo Joint Owners are obligated to reimburse Peabody for any royalty, tax or
other obligations arising out of the DC Lawsuit.&#160; In July 2008, the court
dismissed all counts against NPC, two without prejudice to their possible
re-filing.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August 2011, all claims in the DC Lawsuit were
dismissed pursuant to a settlement agreement among</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;"> </font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">the Navajo Nation, Peabody, SRP and SCE.&#160; At the
request of SRP, NPC contributed an immaterial amount toward the settlement of
the DC Lawsuit based on its 11% ownership stake in the Navajo Generating
Station.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SCE also has asked that the Mohave Joint Owners,
including NPC, contribute toward the settlement based upon their ownership
stakes in the Mohave Generating Station. NPC has not agreed to contribute to
SCE&#8217;s portion of the DC Lawsuit settlement.&#160; Management has discussed the
matters with SCE, but does not believe the impact of any claim by, or
settlement with, SCE will be material to NPC.</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;</font></p>


<DIV bclFooter>





<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font><font style="mso-no-proof:yes;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;">156</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font></p>

<DIV bclHeader>





<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>



<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>





</DIV>
<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;
SPPC </font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;
Farad Dam </font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June 2001, SPPC sold four hydro
generating units (10.3 MW total capacity) located in Nevada and California to
TMWA for $8.0 million.&#160; One of the units, the Farad Hydro (2.8 MW), has been
out of service since the summer of 1996 due to a collapsed flume. Under the
terms of the contract with TMWA, SPPC is not entitled to receive the proceeds
of sale relating to Farad unless and until it has reconstructed the Farad
facility in a manner reasonably acceptable to TMWA or, alternatively, SPPC
assigns its casualty loss claim to TMWA and TMWA is reasonably satisfied
regarding its rights with respect to such claim.</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;"> </font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The current estimate to rebuild the diversion dam, if
management decides to rebuild, is approximately $20 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">SPPC filed a claim with the Farad Dam&#8217;s
insurers, Hartford Steam Boiler Inspection and Insurance Company and
Zurich-American Insurance Company, and in 2003 </font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">initiated federal court litigation against the insurers.&#160; The insurers contested
the extent and amount of insurance coverage.&#160; Coverage was established through
this litigation, but until July 2012 the matter remained in litigation to
determine the amount of coverage. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In July 2012, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth
Circuit entered its order reversing the valuation holding of the U.S. District Court
and setting the value of Farad Dam at $19.8 million dollars (as was argued by
SPPC), with some deduction for depreciation to be determined on remand. The
court also affirmed SPPC&#8217;s right to recover $4.0 million dollars in permitting
and design costs, but held that if SPPC accepts the money, rather than rebuild,
the $4.0 million is part of the $19.8 million replacement cost.&#160; In addition,
the court held that SPPC is entitled to recover full replacement cost in the
event of a rebuild, and that the District Court is free, on remand, to extend
the three year time to rebuild to start at the conclusion of all litigation. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=windowtext face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">It is not known at this time when the
District Court will set hearings for the issues remanded by the Ninth Circuit.
Management cannot assess or predict the outcome or the impact of the District
Court decisions at this time, but they are not expected to be material to SPPC.
</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; Other Legal Matters</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NVE and its subsidiaries, through the course of their
normal business operations, are currently involved in a number of other legal
actions, none of which, in the opinion of management, is expected to have a significant
impact on their financial positions, results of operations or cash flows</font><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">. &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#002060 face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other
Commitments</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160; NPC and SPPC</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; ON Line TUA</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font color=windowtext face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the second quarter of 2011,
NVE began to construct Phase 1 of ON Line, which is a joint project between the
Utilities and GBT-South. Construction of Phase 1 consists of the initial 500 kV
interconnection between the Robinson Summit substation on the SPPC system and
the Harry Allen substation on the NPC system.&#160; ON Line has an expected
in-service date of no later than December 31, 2013.&#160; The Utilities will own a
25% interest in Phase 1 and have entered into a TUA with GBT-South for its 75%
interest in Phase 1. Under the terms of the TUA, NVE&#8217;s future lease payments
are adjusted for construction costs, including cost overruns; for which the
Utilities expect to get regulatory recovery of.&#160; For accounting purposes NVE is
treated as the owner of the construction project in accordance with Lease
Accounting, The Effect of Lessee Involvement in Asset Construction of the FASC.
As a result, as of December 31, 2012, capitalized construction costs associated
with GBT&#8217;s 75% interest were $264.9 and $14.2 million at NPC and SPPC,
respectively, in CWIP with a corresponding credit to other deferred
liabilities. NVE expects to recover future lease payments including cost
overruns through the Utilities&#8217; regulatory proceedings.</font><font color=windowtext face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;"> &nbsp;</font></p>








<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><a name=Commonstock></a><a name="Commonstock_bclEnd"></a><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NOTE
13.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></b><a href="#Commonstock"><b><u><font color=blue face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">COMMON STOCK AND OTHER
PAID-IN CAPITAL</font></u></b></a></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Policy on
Shareholder Rights Plans&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">NVE&#8217;s policy is to seek shareholder approval prior to
the adoption of a shareholder rights plan, unless the BOD, in the exercise of
its fiduciary duties and with the concurrence of a majority of its independent
members, determines that, under the circumstances existing at the time, it is in
the best interest of NVE&#8217;s shareholders to adopt a shareholder rights plan
without first </font><!-- Do not modify beyond this point! !--><a name=bcl_connect_next></a></p>
<DIV bclFooter>





<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font><font style="mso-no-proof:yes;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;">157</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;"></font></p>
